rows.label: Asset quality: slippages and SMA-2 rising
rows.why: Fresh slippages rose to ₹7,046 crore from ₹5,500 crore in Q4 and SMA-2 roughly doubled QoQ, with ₹1,400-1,500 crore pulled back to date, though management says GNPA/NNPA (at multi-decade lows) are not a concern.

tone.note: Management was confident on record profit, multi-decade-low GNPA/NNPA, and holding 3% domestic NIM and 14-15% credit growth; it was defensive on the sequential slowdown in deposits (0.5%) and advances (0.32%), rising slippages and SMA-2, and evasive on ECL quantum, bulk deposit share and margin beyo

500113|2026-03.headline: SAIL Q4 FY26: PAT up 43% YoY on higher NSR and volumes; FY27 sales volume target 22 mn tons and capex guided to INR15,000 crore.
500113|2026-03.overview: SAIL reported Q4 FY26 crude steel output of 4.9 mn tons (up 4% YoY), sales volume of 5.3 mn tons (up 4%) and turnover of INR30,541 crore (up 5%). PBT rose 48% and PAT 43% YoY in the quarter, and management said Q4 borrowings fell by INR3,200 crore. For FY26, record sales volume of 19.9 mn tons (up 11%) and a roughly 1 mn ton inventory reduction drove borrowings down about INR8,150 crore, and management said the FY26 balance sheet carries no audit qualifications for the first time in many years. Management said NSR rose about INR4,000/t from Q4 to April-May, while coking coal cost is also rising, with a stated impact of INR1,400-1,500/t in Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: YoY, no rail price arrears in FY26 vs ~INR1,800 crore in FY25
management hopes to lower it in FY27

segments.name: Long products
segments.commentary: Q4 NSR INR53,400/t; April NSR INR57,600/t and mid-May about INR57,800/t. March long-product price increase was about INR1,500/t.

segments.name: Flat products
segments.commentary: Q4 NSR INR51,000/t; April INR56,700/t and mid-May about INR56,000/t. Flat price increase in March was about INR1,400/t. A safeguard duty on flat imports is in place.

segments.name: Bokaro Steel Plant
segments.commentary: EBITDA recovered sharply in H2 FY26 after FY25 breakdowns and a Hot Strip Mill repair that ran 2 months beyond plan. Better flat-product NSR and SMS fixes also helped, and management expects further improvement in FY27.

segments.name: Salem (stainless)
segments.commentary: Still loss-making. CR mill yield is 83-84% against a 90% target, and LPG has been replaced with PNG. Management plans to feed imported stainless slabs to idle CR and SR mill capacity.

segments.name: NSL / RINL volumes
segments.commentary: NSL total volume was 1.12 mn tons in FY26, with Q4 near 0.1 mn tons. Sales of RINL products began in February, at about 48,000-50,000 tons in Q4, and are guided at 0.6-0.7 mn tons in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume target of 22 mn tons (about 22.5 mn tons including RINL products), up from 19.9 mn tons in FY26.
FY27 crude steel production target of 22.5 mn tons against stated capacity of 21 mn tons, to be reached through debottlenecking and operational efficiency.

Capex guidance: INR15,000 crore in FY27, INR18,000-19,000 crore in FY28, and INR20,000-25,000 crore per year after that, to be funded mainly from internal accruals with incremental long-term borrowings.
Coke rate target to fall by about INR20/kg in FY27 after the earlier reduction; management aims for a further drop in coke rate.

Employee strength is 49,752 as of 1 April 2026, with a further reduction of 3,400-3,500 expected in each of FY27 and FY28. A VRS targeting 500-1,000 exits is under way. Pay revision from 1 January 2027 is not yet in the guidance and will be provided for in Q4 FY27.

Q1 FY27 inventory: management aims for no build-up in Q1 and expects Q2 to be sluggish with inventory reduction in Q3 and Q4. Coking coal cost is up about INR2,000/t to about INR21,500/t, implying a cost impact of INR1,400-1,500/t on production cost.
capex_capacity: Crude steel capacity is 21 mn tons; FY26 output was 19.43 mn tons. FY27 target is 22.5 mn tons through debottlenecking and operating beyond rated capacity.

New capacity expansion projects at IISCO (about 4.5 mn tons, INR35,000-36,000 crore), Bhilai (about 3.5 mn tons, about INR30,000 crore, yet to be announced) and Bokaro (about 3 mn tons, about INR18,000 crore) are the three cleared expansions.

IISCO packages are tendered and groundwork is starting, with spending rising from FY28 and some spending in Q4 FY27. Bokaro and Bhilai spending is mainly expected from FY29; new capacity is expected from FY30-31.
Capex in FY27 covers debottlenecking, AMR (asset modernisation/replacement) and expansion projects.
Iron ore: FY26 production was 38 mn tons with a 56 mn ton target for FY27 and 80 mn tons as the longer-term ramp-up goal. The Chiria mine is a new lease, not a renewal.
demand_pricing: Indian steel consumption grew about 8% in FY26 while production grew 11%. India became a marginal net exporter, with exports of 6.5 mn tons and imports of 6.6 mn tons.
Q1 demand is expected to be muted, with destocking, then a pickup from Q3. Rupee depreciation and firmer international prices support landed cost and selling prices.

Cost pressure: the Middle East situation pushed up limestone/flux costs (CFR from about $23-24 to about $35/t), with an impact of only INR100-200/t on saleable steel. Fuel constraints were managed through PNG and LPG banks.
Rail freight prices: FY25 arrears were about INR1,800 crore; FY26 provisional rates are lower, and the FY25 rate finalisation could affect FY27. Management said the direction is unclear.
Flat safeguard duty and cheaper import blends are limiting import volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 and FY28 volume guidance and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 sales target of 22 mn tons (vs 19.9 mn in FY26); FY27 capex INR15,000 crore against about INR9,100 crore in FY26; FY28 about INR18,000-19,000 crore; then INR20,000-25,000 crore per year.

qa_highlights.question: Realisations in Q4 and April-May, and cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 blended NSR about INR52,000/t; April about INR57,000/t. Coking coal rose from INR18,200/t in Q4 to about INR21,000 in April and INR21,800 in May. Q1 consumption cost impact is smaller because of about 30 days of inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity and the path to 22.5 mn tons?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 21 mn tons. Growth to 22.5 mn tons comes from debottlenecking and efficiency gains, with new capacity only from FY30-31. Management said output could reach 23 mn tons later.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Q3 to Q4 EBITDA bridge explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Input prices were a INR272 crore headwind, offset by a INR429 crore gain from better raw-material usage (higher PCI, more oxygen, better iron ore use).

qa_highlights.question: Can 100%+ utilisation be sustained given the capacity figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DPR capacity is not a hard limit for blast furnaces and SMS; productivity can exceed design, citing examples of 2.3 going to 3 and the operations of peers.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded and what is the leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects internal accruals to cover most of FY27 capex, with incremental long-term borrowings beyond that. Net debt to equity is 0.37 and is expected to fall further in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital rise with the monsoon season?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for no inventory build in Q1 but said Q2 will be challenging, with inventory reduction planned for Q3 and Q4.

risks_watch: Wage revision from 1 January 2027: the impact is not yet in guidance and may be booked in Q4 FY27; past revisions were about 15%.
Coking coal and imported coal costs are rising, with the Q1 cost impact estimated at INR1,400-1,500/t against a NSR tailwind.
Q1 and Q2 demand softness and destocking; inventory build risk.
Rail freight price finalisation for FY25 could go either way in FY27.
Middle East supply disruption affecting fuel, flux and raw material routes (Strait of Hormuz).
Salem Steel Plant losses and BISL disinvestment status; the Chiria mining lease is still pending.
Achieving 22 mn tons on the 21 mn ton stated capacity and funding INR15,000 crore capex in FY27.
500113|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 profit growth, volume records and the clean audit position, with a clear FY27 target. Cautious on Q1-Q2 demand and on the outcome of the wage revision and rail price decisions, which management called unclear.
key_quotes: So far as expansions are concerned, actually, we've cleared for 3 plants.

Company has posted highest ever sales volume at 19.9 million tons, almost like 20 million tons, which margina lly -- I mean, it is close to 20 million tons with a growth of 11% as compared to the previous year.
after a pretty long time, many years and decades, you can say, that the balance sheet of '25 -'26 is totally clean from the qualifications.
But overall, in sellable steel, its impact will be hardly INR100 or INR200.
So you can say that the cost impact will be around INR1,400 to INR1,500 per ton.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: April NSR of about INR57,000/t vs Q4 blended INR52,000/t (+INR4,000/t), but Q1 FY27 coking coal cost hit of INR1,400-1,500/t and a 2026 wage revision not yet in guidance partly offset it.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY30-31 for new capacity; debottlenecking to 22.5 mn t in FY
rows.why: Crude capacity is 21 mn t against 19.43 mn t output (92% utilisation) and the FY27 target of 22.5 mn t, but the three cleared expansions (IISCO 4.5 mn t, Bhilai 3.5 mn t, Bokaro 3 mn t) only arrive FY30-31, so new capacity within the window rests on debottlenecking, not new plants.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 sales target of 22 mn t vs record 19.9 mn t in FY26 (+11%), with RINL products guided at 0.6-0.7 mn t; Q1-Q2 expected to be sluggish, so the growth is back-loaded.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 92% with 21 mn t rated capacity and FY27 capex of INR15,000 crore, stepping up to INR18,000-19,000 crore in FY28 and INR20,000-25,000 crore a year after; Bhilai (about INR30,000 crore) is yet to be announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 PAT up 51% and Q4 PAT up 43% with NSR up about INR4,000/t into April-May, but the 22 mn t target depends on Q1-Q2 destocking and the rail-freight outcome is unclear.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Coking coal rising to INR21,800/t in May (cost impact INR1,400-1,500/t in Q1), Q2 expected sluggish with inventory build risk, and FY25 rail arrears (about INR1,800 crore) could go either way.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: RINL products began selling in Feb 2026 at about 48,000-50,000 t in Q4 and are guided at 0.6-0.7 mn t in FY27; no other new product launch was discussed.

rows.label: Coke rate cut of INR20/kg in FY27
rows.why: Management commits to a further INR20/kg coke-rate reduction after the earlier cut, and the Q3-to-Q4 EBITDA bridge already showed a INR429 crore gain from better raw-material usage.

rows.label: Net debt to equity down from 0.37
rows.why: Borrowings fell about INR8,150 crore in FY26 (INR3,200 crore in Q4) and management expects net debt to equity to fall further in FY27, with capex of INR15,000 crore mostly funded from internal accruals.

rows.label: Salem stainless turnaround
rows.why: Salem is still loss-making with CR mill yield at 83-84% against a 90% target, and management plans to feed imported stainless slabs to idle CR and SR capacity.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 record volume, profit growth, debt reduction and the FY27 22 mn t target and capex path; it was cautious on Q1-Q2 demand, coking coal cost, the wage revision and rail price outcome, and analysts pressed on whether 100%+ utilisation on 21 mn t capacity is sustainable.

500113|2026-06.headline: SAIL Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose over 50% to INR4,356 crore (16.7% margin) despite 4.8 Mt crude steel output, aided by advanced capital repairs and better NSR.
500113|2026-06.overview: SAIL reported Q1 FY27 EBITDA of INR4,356 crore versus INR2,925 crore a year earlier, with margin of 16.7% and EBITDA per tonne of INR10,464. PBT and PAT rose to INR2,159 crore and INR1,636 crore from INR890 crore and INR685 crore. Crude steel output fell to 4.8 Mt (4.9 Mt CPLY) and sales volume dropped about 7-8% to 4.2 Mt, as major capital repairs at IISCO, Durgapur and Bokaro were advanced into Q1 by design. Average NSR was INR57,100/t, up about INR5,000/t from Q4 FY26, and borrowings were flat at INR21,729 crore versus INR21,663 crore at 1 March 2026.

financial_highlights.change: up more than 50% vs CPLY INR2,925 crore
vs INR685 crore CPLY, about 150% growth
up about INR5,000/t vs Q4 FY26 (INR52,000/t)
vs INR21,663 crore on 1 March 2026; about INR21,400 crore today
from about 0.38-0.39 at start of year
vs Q1 target of INR2,306 crore
vs INR2,944 crore CPLY; includes differential VRS cost

segments.name: Iron ore / mines (third-party sales)
segments.commentary: Q1 iron ore sales turnover INR574 crore vs INR157 crore CPLY, with volume 1.1 Mt vs 0.31 Mt; EBITDA about INR150 crore. Sales are mainly from Odisha group of mines, and Chhattisgarh auctions have fructified for Q2.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Flats about 52.7% and longs about 34.8% of sales; semis fell to about 11-12.5% from 14% in Q1 FY26. Finished steel share rose to 89% from 86%.

segments.name: NMDC Steel / RINL
segments.commentary: NMDC Steel marketing sales were nil vs 3.73 lakh t CPLY; RINL semis sales were about 93,000 t (new this year). NSL plus RINL combined was about 2.76 lakh t CPLY.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 volume guidance maintained, with growth over FY26 expected by year-end; Q2-Q4 production to exceed last year's levels.
Q2 NSR expected to be about INR1,000-2,000/t lower than Q1; July NSR averaged INR55,600/t (flats INR56,900, longs INR54,200).
Imported coking coal cost expected to fall about INR1,000-2,000/t from August; Q2 coal cost seen INR1,000-1,500/t below Q1 (Q1 imported INR21,300/t).
FY27 capex target INR15,000 crore, rising to over INR20,000 crore in FY28 and about INR25,000-26,000 crore thereafter.
Cost reduction of about INR2,000/t targeted in FY27 from Q2 onward; by FY29 variable cost down INR3,000-4,000/t from IISCO expansion, with fixed cost up INR1,500-2,000/t, net about INR2,000/t.
Inventory to be held flat in Q2 and reduced in Q3 and Q4 to lower FY27 inventory year-on-year.
Railway price revision for FY27 expected in FY28; management says no further downward hit to P&L expected.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex INR2,575 crore against Q1 target INR2,306 crore; full-year target INR15,000 crore.
Major capital repairs advanced into Q1 at IISCO, Durgapur and Bokaro, reducing crude steel output by about 0.1 Mt vs CPLY.
Durgapur: TMT bar mill planned to produce 0.8-0.9 Mt/yr, expected September to December 2027; this will sharply reduce semis availability from Durgapur.
Captive Tasra coking coal mine under development, production expected around December 2026; captive mine coal cost estimated INR5,000-6,000/t vs indigenous average INR13,100/t.
Subgrade iron ore fines inventory about 32 Mt; first auction of about 3 Mt put up, with rates awaited.
demand_pricing: Indian steel consumption grew more than 8% YoY in Q1 FY27 while production grew about 3%; net imports about 0.4-0.5 Mt vs about 0.3 Mt CPLY.
Gap between primary and secondary TMT narrowed to about INR5,000/t.
June to July long-product prices fell about INR2,000-3,000/t; recent upward momentum of INR500-1,000/t expected. Flat product prices fell about INR1,000/t between June and July.
Safeguard duty of 11.5% remains in place (second year of three-year term). Anti-dumping investigation has been initiated and may bring relief.
Government imposed definitive anti-dumping duty on met coke; management says no impact as SAIL has captive coke capacity matching its needs.
Coal mix: about 85% imported, 15% indigenous (of which about 5% from captive mines). Imported coking coal: hard about 62%, soft about 23%.
Rail price: provisional FY27 price about INR74,000/t, which management expects to be revised upward.

qa_highlights.question: What were Q1 NSR vs Q4, and how do July prices and Q2 NSR look?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 NSR was INR57,100/t vs Q4 INR52,000/t. Monsoon-driven seasonal decline expected in Q2, with Q2 NSR about INR1,000-2,000/t lower than Q1; longs more affected than flats.

qa_highlights.question: Is full-year volume guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management maintained full-year volume guidance and expects growth over last year by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for coal costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported coal was INR21,300/t in Q1 vs INR18,100/t in Q4. Index fell from about 235 to 220; coal cost expected to fall INR1,000-2,000/t from August.

qa_highlights.question: Is third-party iron ore sales growth sustainable, and what about subgrade inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Mines sales more than doubled YoY, adding about INR400 crore turnover and INR150 crore profit. Target of about 8 Mt for captive mines; subgrade inventory about 32 Mt with 3 Mt first auction in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 capex and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target INR15,000 crore; FY28 above INR20,000 crore; later years INR25,000-26,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-reduction plan through FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR2,000/t cost cut in FY27 from Q2; by FY29 IISCO expansion cuts variable cost INR3,000-4,000/t, with fixed cost up INR1,500-2,000/t, net about INR2,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the Gulf conflict affect input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel impact limited due to in-plant gas use; flux cost up on freight but offset by lower usage, saving about INR25 crore. Limestone and imported coal costs rose; coal up about INR3,500/t YoY.

risks_watch: Q2 seasonal weakness: monsoon-driven NSR decline and rain-hit demand; management aims to hold inventory flat in Q2.
Logistics constraints (rake availability) still limit mine sales; subgrade auction outcome pending.
Pay commission from 1 January 2027; wage provision decision deferred to Q4 FY27.
Railway price revision (FY27 price to be set in FY28) and anti-dumping outcome on flats.
Working capital borrowings reduction and inventory reduction in Q3-Q4 to meet deleveraging goal.
Production volume recovery in Q2-Q4 after Q1 maintenance; Tasra captive coal timing (around December 2026).
500113|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on profitability and cost trajectory, with the margin and per-tonne EBITDA framed as best-in-years. Cautious and hedged on Q2 pricing and volume, with many figures described as guesswork and some answers unclear or deflected.
key_quotes: EBITDA margin at 16.7% is one of the best since '21 -'22, when the steel market at that time was at its peak and coal price was at its bottom in '21 -'22.
EBITDA per tonne also crossed a benchmark figure of INR10,000 per tonne and stood at INR10,464 per tonne in quarter 1 '26 -'27.
Yes, we are maintaining the full year volume, and we'll be having a growth over last year by the year-end.
So far as capex is concerned, this year, we're planning a target of INR15,000 crores, and this is going to increase in the next 2, 3 years because our expanses are on.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets about INR2,000/t cost reduction in FY27 from Q2, and Q2 coal cost seen INR1,000-1,500/t below Q1 (Q1 imported INR21,300/t), but Q2 NSR is guided INR1,000-2,000/t below Q1 NSR of INR57,100/t, so net margin direction is partly offset.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q5 FY27 (Durgapur TMT bar mill, Sep-Dec 2027); Tasra captive
rows.why: Durgapur TMT mill of 0.8-0.9 Mt/yr is under construction for Sep-Dec 2027 and Tasra captive coking coal mine is due around December 2026, but these are timed beyond or at the edge of the window and the mill is outside the 2-4 quarter window for most of it.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Full-year volume guidance maintained with growth over FY26 expected by year-end and Q2-Q4 production guided above last year, but Q1 sales fell about 7-8% to 4.2 Mt and crude output dipped to 4.8 Mt from 4.9 Mt.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex target of INR15,000 crore is held and stepping up to over INR20,000 crore in FY28 and INR25,000-26,000 crore thereafter, with Q1 capex of INR2,575 crore above the INR2,306 crore target, so further capex programme details are likely to be formalised.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Railway price revision expected to be upward (provisional FY27 rail price about INR74,000/t) and anti-dumping relief may come, but management is hedged on Q2 pricing with July NSR at INR55,600/t, below Q1's INR57,100/t.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 NSR guided INR1,000-2,000/t lower than Q1 and July NSR averaged INR55,600/t, with monsoon-driven demand weakness and long product prices down INR2,000-3,000/t from June to July; management tone on Q2 is cautious.

rows.label: INR2,000/t cost reduction in FY27 from Q2
rows.why: Management targets about INR2,000/t cost cut in FY27 from Q2 onward, with imported coking coal expected to fall INR1,000-2,000/t from August.

rows.label: Third-party iron ore sales to 8 Mt target
rows.why: Mines third-party sales were 1.1 Mt in Q1 vs 0.31 Mt CPLY (INR574 crore turnover vs INR157 crore), target of 8 Mt is set but rake logistics constrain sales and subgrade auction outcome is pending on about 32 Mt inventory.

rows.label: Inventory and working capital reduction to cut borrowings
rows.why: Inventory to be held flat in Q2 and reduced in Q3 and Q4, with borrowings flat at INR21,729 crore and debt-equity down to 0.36 from about 0.38-0.39.

tone.note: Management was confident on margin, per-tonne EBITDA and the INR2,000/t cost trajectory, but cautious and hedged on Q2 NSR, volumes and coal, with several figures described as guesswork; analysts pushed on Q2 pricing, volume recovery and subgrade iron ore inventory.

500113|2026-09.headline: SAIL Q2 FY27 PAT rose to INR1,774 crore on 5.2 MT sales and EBITDA of INR4,561 crore, despite higher imported coking coal costs.
500113|2026-09.overview: SAIL's Q2 FY27 sales volume rose 24% QoQ to 5.2 MT and turnover reached INR31,766 crore (+20% YoY), with EBITDA of INR4,561 crore and PAT of INR1,774 crore. Imported coking coal rose about INR1,700/t QoQ to INR22,930/t, compressing margins, though volume, inventory reduction and high-end mix offset it. Borrowings fell to INR20,583 crore and inventory dropped to 1.59 MT, while management guided to about 21 MT FY27 sales (cut from 22 MT) and a capex step-up to INR15,000 crore this year and over INR1.2 lakh crore over FY27-FY31. Management said Q3 and Q4 prices and technical parameters should improve, with October NSR up about INR4,000/t over the Q2 average.

segments.name: Iron ore fines (external sales)
segments.commentary: H1 sales about 2.5 MT vs 0.9 MT last year (+167%), with profit of INR388 crore vs INR124 crore CPLY. FY27 target is 7-8 MT vs internal 10 MT target.

segments.name: Rails and bars
segments.commentary: Rails were about 8% of volume and bar and rod about 22% of production volume; rails hold a larger share of turnover. Rail sales expected at 1.2-1.3 MT this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 saleable steel sales guidance cut to about 21 MT from 22 MT, with H1 at 9.33 MT; includes about 0.5 MT of RINL volume and no NMDC sales.
FY27 iron ore production now expected at 48-50 MT vs 56 MT internal target; H1 was about 19.5-20 MT.
FY27 capex guidance INR15,000 crore (H1 INR5,500 crore; Q3+Q4 INR9,000-10,000 crore); FY28 above INR20,000 crore, FY29 about INR25,000 crore; about INR1.2 lakh crore over FY27-FY31.
Imported coking coal guided at about INR23,500/t in Q3 and about INR22,000-23,000/t in Q4; Q3 average around INR23,800-23,900/t (about INR1,000 above Q2).
Inventory target of 1.2-1.3 MT by year-end (15 days at 30 Sep vs 17.5 days at 31 Mar); plants and ports target 30-35 days.
Employee count expected at about 46,000 by FY27 year-end and 26,000 by 2031; separations of 3,000-4,000 a year plus VRS.
Interest cost may rise in H2 after a 25 bp repo hike; management expects debt to rise from FY28 as capex ramps.
capex_capacity: Expansion from 20 MT to 35 MT across IISCO, Bokaro, Bhilai and Rourkela; IISCO packages already ordered and work started, Bokaro in advanced tendering, Bhilai tendering to start shortly, Rourkela DPR ready for in-principle approval.
Rowghat iron ore mine: interim mining at about 3 MT under EC; ramp-up path 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 14 MT over 3-4 years after MDO main mining starts (1+ year away).
Tasra coking coal mine to start production from January 2027, expected to lower imported coking coal dependence.
Gua mines to expand from 4 MT to 10 MT via MDO appointment; 2 MT RSP pellet plant on course and in advanced stage.
Long-term aspiration of 100 MT iron ore by FY31-32 (80-85 MT is the fallback); excludes Chiria.
demand_pricing: Q2 average NSR was about INR54,400/t long and INR57,000/t flat (average INR55,500/t); October NSR is INR58,700/t long and INR61,700/t flat, about INR4,000/t above Q2.
Imported coal index (Platts) peaked at $290/t in August and stabilised at $266-267/t.
Q2 EBITDA hit by rainy-season furnace and raw material issues in Jharkhand and Odisha; technical parameters improved in October.
Rail price revision had about INR300 crore positive impact in Q1 and nil in Q2.
Q2 EBITDA per tonne about INR8,170 vs H1 about INR9,561; management targets INR11,000-12,000/t levels in Q3-Q4.
Management cited WSA forecast of 1.7% global steel demand growth in CY27 and India consumption growth of about 8% in CY26 and CY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity upfront when capex spans 4-5 years, given single-digit return ratios?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed timing matters and said the FPO will be timed to investor confidence; capex will be funded through about INR50,000 crore of internal accruals over 4 years, with debt and FPO later.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 volume still be 22 MT and does it include RINL and NMDC?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is now about 21 MT given H1 of 9.33 MT; it includes RINL (H1 184,000 t, Q2 88,000 t, full-year up to 0.5 MT) but excludes NMDC.

qa_highlights.question: Imported coal price outlook, given earlier guidance of a INR1,000-2,000 decline?

500117|2026-03.headline: DCW Q4 FY26 PAT rose 60% YoY to Rs.18 crore and FY26 EBITDA rose 11% to Rs.240 crore, with net debt cut to Rs.71 crore.
500117|2026-03.overview: Q4 revenue was Rs.609 crore (+13.2% YoY, +17% QoQ) and Q4 EBITDA including other income was Rs.70 crore (+14% YoY, +40% QoQ). FY26 revenue was Rs.2,144 crore (+7.2%) and EBITDA Rs.240 crore (+11.2%), with PAT up 60% to Rs.48 crore, helped by lower finance cost. Management said profit growth came from volumes, utilisation and cost gains rather than price, since realisations fell across most products, with C-PVC down more than 20%. Specialty EBITDA fell 6.5% to Rs.177 crore on C-PVC–PVC spread compression, while basic chemicals EBITDA rose to Rs.54 crore from Rs.19 crore. Management withheld FY27 EBITDA guidance and cited pricing volatility from the West Asia conflict; the earlier Rs.400 crore target looks derailed.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals (C-PVC, SIOP)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA Rs.177 crore (-6.5%) and margin about 30%, down about 6 points, as C-PVC realisations fell over 20% against unchanged PVC input prices. Q4 EBITDA Rs.39 crore, down 16% YoY and 22% QoQ. SIOP margin is still 35-40%, per management.

segments.name: Basic chemicals (caustic soda, soda ash, chlorine-neutral)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA Rs.54 crore vs Rs.19 crore, with margin 3.5% vs 1.3%, helped by fixed-cost absorption and solar power substitution. Q4 EBITDA Rs.30 crore vs Rs.14 crore a year earlier. Caustic realisation was about $350/t in Q4 and above $400/t in Q1 FY27 per management.

segments.name: Synthetic rutile
segments.commentary: Record FY26 sales volume and reduced inventory. Management guided that the spread should stay elevated vs last year on a better mix from ex-China long-term contracts. It is reported within basic chemicals, and no quarterly realisation was disclosed.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 EBITDA guidance. CFO said the Rs.400 crore target communicated earlier is 'derailed' by pricing pressure in commodities and specialty; a Rs.300 crore figure could not be confirmed.
Scheduled term loan repayment of about Rs.130 crore in FY27; with Rs.71 crore net debt, the company expects to be net cash positive by end-FY27.
Finance cost for FY27 is guided to fall by about Rs.12-13 crore to around Rs.50 crore, or slightly below, if working-capital credit lines are not used heavily.
The 10 kt final C-PVC phase was completed in late March 2026; benefits are expected from Q1 FY27 and are expected to be annualised over the year.
Management expects caustic and soda ash prices to stay elevated for a couple of quarters; VCM/PVC spreads may be under pressure due to the West Asia conflict.
capex_capacity: C-PVC capacity was raised from 20 kt to 50 kt: 30 kt was added this year, with the final 10 kt completed in late March 2026. C-PVC volumes rose to about 37-38 kt from about 22 kt.
SIOP debottlenecked from 18 kt to 28 kt; output reached 24 kt last year and is now near capacity. Future SIOP spend is aimed at value-added grades, not volume.
Commodity capex will focus on efficiency, not volume. Growth capex will go into specialty or niche chemistries. New capex announcements are on hold until the geopolitical situation clears.
Renewable (solar) project was commissioned in FY26 and substitutes about 25% of power from TNEB. Further solar investment is on hold pending clarity on Tamil Nadu banking rules.
Management said incremental C-PVC payback is about 2-2.5 years at current prices; ROC is 8.56% (slide 20), and management said it would be above 14-15% at 2023-24 commodity prices.
demand_pricing: C-PVC realisations fell more than 20% in FY26 with unchanged PVC input prices, compressing the PVC–C-PVC spread. Management said spreads have returned to pre-war levels, and a pass-through lag in March is expected to normalise in the coming quarter.

Caustic soda operating rates fell in Southeast Asia due to petrochemical feedstock shortages, tightening supply. Demand from paper and textile dipped, but alumina demand is strong, and there has been no production curtailment.
Soda ash import price is about $250/t, and prices are supported by the loss of Iran and Russia imports and higher freight.
Synthetic rutile realisation depends on the export mix; ex-China customers pay better prices. Management is building long-term ex-China contracts.

Management said Epigral, Lubrizol and other new C-PVC capacity still leaves room for imports, so it does not expect a domestic glut. It also noted that dumping cases on PVC and soda ash were not implemented, and that China and Korea C-PVC duties were applied earlier.

PVC feedstock VCM is sourced largely from the Middle East. Supply was disrupted by the Gulf war, so the company is buying at higher cost, which it cannot fully pass through. Management said two European PVC plants (about 2 lakh t, including Vinnolit) closed in 2025, before the conflict.

500124|2026-06.headline: Dr Reddy's halts semaglutide injectable API commercial supply after impurity out of spec in scale-up batch; 6-7 million pens now expected Nov-March.
500124|2026-06.overview: Dr Reddy's disclosed on July 9, 2026 that an impurity from a scaled-up synthetic semaglutide API process was out of specification in finished drug product testing, halting API dispatch to long-term partner OneSource. Management says the issue is a process/reaction problem requiring parameter tweaks and repeat validation (three validation batches), with no equipment change expected. Commercial supply is now targeted to resume in October, with 6-7 million pens expected from November to March FY27 versus the earlier plan that assumed sales from July to October. Management says no recall, no regulatory filing change, no patient safety impact on product already supplied, and no penalties expected, though some customer down-payment arrangements may need renegotiation. The company said oral semaglutide is unaffected because it uses a different API source.

qa_highlights.answer: Management is exiting low-margin staples (rice, pulses) to a few channels and focusing on jaggery, brown sugar variants and premium whites. Value-added products are expected to reach 30%+ gross margin. New sweet product launches are planned later in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Any acquisition progress in food/FMCG?
qa_highlights.answer: Management named ethnic snacking and culinary convenience as target segments. It is in talks on entry routes but gave no deal details; strengthening the current model comes first.

qa_highlights.question: Nutra division scale-up and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: No new Nutra India launches. Valensa is the growth lever, with two launches (prostate and dermal health), a reoriented strategy and a new management team. Expected to lift both top line and bottom line.

qa_highlights.question: Any positive ethanol policy change post the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: The government has signalled E30 through BIS; positive action is expected via allocations in the new ethanol year. Pricing action is unlikely, but blending increases are expected.

qa_highlights.question: How is capital allocated after the refinery restructuring?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on CPG (brand building, distribution and A&P, with no real capex) and on cost and efficiency in the core business. Only capex is the Rs 45 crore jaggery facility.

qa_highlights.question: When will CPG break even and what share of profit could it reach?
qa_highlights.answer: Break-even in 6-8 quarters and a good single-digit EBITDA margin by the end of the decade. No share-of-profit target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not give a timeline and said it is focused on strengthening the business operations.

500125|2026-06.headline: EID Parry Q1 FY27: sugar revenue rose to Rs. 410 crore on 0.89 LMT volumes, while PSRIPL refinery closure drove a Rs. 610 crore impairment offset by a Rs. 591 crore reversal.
500125|2026-06.overview: Tamil Nadu crushing fell to 1.47 LMT from 2.12 LMT as units ran 54 days versus 37, and gross recovery eased to 7.95% from 8.02%. Sugar sales volume rose to 0.89 LMT from 0.56 LMT, lifting revenue to about Rs. 410 crore from Rs. 347 crore, though average realisation slipped to Rs. 40.02 per kg from Rs. 40.97. CPG turnover roughly halved to Rs. 94 crore from Rs. 188 crore as management deliberately recalibrated the model toward higher-margin products, with quarterly breakeven targeted in 4-5 quarters. PSRIPL refinery operations have ceased and Rs. 665 crore was infused in the quarter to settle bank obligations.

segments.commentary: Production 351 LL vs 412 LL YoY; sales 380 LL (ENA 138 LL, ethanol 242 LL) vs 413 LL. Realisation fell to Rs. 63.49/litre from Rs. 67.59.

segments.commentary: Generation 180 LU vs 221 LU; exports 89 LU vs 122 LU. Tariff rose to Rs. 4.89/unit from Rs. 3.67, but segment revenue fell to Rs. 6.6 crore from Rs. 7.53 crore.

segments.commentary: Revenue about Rs. 6.22 crore vs Rs. 6 crore YoY, with consolidated Nutra turnover about Rs. 61 crore vs Rs. 27 crore. Growth is driven mainly by US subsidiary Valensa; India is about 20% of consolidated Nutra turnover.

segments.commentary: Turnover Rs. 94 crore vs Rs. 188 crore YoY, a deliberate recalibration toward margin-accretive products. Management says the absolute contribution margin pool has grown; quarterly breakeven is targeted in 4-5 quarters.

India: SY 2025-26 net sugar production about 28 MMT (vs 26 MMT); domestic consumption 28 MMT; exports 0.8 MMT; ethanol diversion about 2.9-3 MMT; closing stock about 4.2 MMT.

qa_highlights.question: When will CPG reach quarterly breakeven, are new ethnic snacks/culinary categories organic or acquired, and what is the jaggery plant timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: CPG revenue fall is an intentional recalibration toward margin-accretive products; quarterly breakeven targeted in 4-5 quarters. New categories still under exploration, both organic and inorganic. Jaggery plant in Karnataka to commission in about 6 months, more than doubling jaggery capacity; both plants together could deliver close to Rs. 100 crore turnover.

qa_highlights.question: Nutra: how much growth comes from US Valensa versus India, and what EBITDA margin is achievable at scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is largely from Valensa with new launches. Steady-state EBITDA margin is 12-15%. India is about 20% of consolidated Nutra turnover; Europe certification issues in India business were not entirely company fault and have been resolved.

qa_highlights.question: What KPIs will management track by March 2027 to judge the disciplined approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus on working capital efficiency, leveraging debt cost, monetising non-core assets, cost reduction and improving current ratio; aiming for a stronger balance sheet by March 2027 and March 2028 and over the next 4-6 quarters. Standalone debt: about Rs. 150 crore long-term and Rs. 800-900 crore short-term, with CPG margin KPIs set for breakeven in 4-5 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh crush fall, and is TN sugar still viable or in need of restructuring?
qa_highlights.answer: Cane availability in TN and AP is a macro concern as farmers shift to other crops; crush in these geographies expected flat to about 5% lower in SY 2026-27, with Karnataka the only make-up source. Management is running tight cost control in these states and says further restructuring discussions continue, with no specific plan announced.

qa_highlights.question: PSRIPL: what is the cash outgo versus the non-cash impairment and reversal, and is there more to fund?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs. 610 crore was infused (already in public domain); Rs. 55 crore loan given in Q1, totalling Rs. 665 crore. The Rs. 591 crore reversal relates to remeasured guarantee liabilities and is non-cash; about Rs. 18 crore fresh impairment in Q1. Of the Rs. 130 crore envisaged, Rs. 65 crore remains, to be given over time as required. Asset sales expected but no value quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone debt as of 30 June and seasonal rise in short-term debt once crushing starts?
qa_highlights.answer: Short-term debt about Rs. 980 crore at 30 June versus about Rs. 1,250 crore at 31 March 2026; long-term about Rs. 150 crore. Short-term debt is linked to working capital and will rise when crushing starts; management aims to reduce feedstock imports and improve the position.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise from about Rs. 51 crore to Rs. 59 crore YoY, and is it a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Increase due to VSS (voluntary separation scheme) in legacy plants, not CPG capability building. One-off in one plant so far, with more VSS intended to cut fixed costs.

qa_highlights.question: Sugar: will the company favour sugar over ethanol given high sugar prices, and what is ethanol capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said producing more sugar makes sense at current prices, with a base sugar volume maintained for customers. Distillery capacity is 582 KLPD (about 18 crore litres), of which about 120 KLPD is grain-based. Switching is margin-driven, but OMC supply commitments carry penalties per litre if undelivered.

500126|2026-03.headline: P&G Health FY26 sales rose 16% to close to ₹1,400 crore and PAT rose 30% to ₹327 crore, with volume growth at mid-single digits.

Growth was attributed to the Integrated Growth Strategy, three FY26 innovations (Livogen Iron Gummies, Neurobion Nerve Pain Relief Cream, Evion L5000), and expanded pharmacy coverage of about 30,000 added pharmacies and HCPs. Over five years, sales grew about 1.4X and profit about 1.8X, with average sales growth in the high single digits and average profit growth of 13%. Management declined to give forward guidance, FY27 launch details, or a margin target.

segments.commentary: Each grew at high single digits in FY26. Management separately acknowledged IQVIA-indicated de-growth in Evion and Polybion, without quantifying it.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Recovered in FY26. Nepal grew 3X and Sri Lanka grew high single digits, supported by Neurobion Forte and Evion Forte launches. Export volume and price split was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export growth driver and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports grew in FY26, with Nepal at 3X and Sri Lanka at high single digits, driven by consumption, availability, detailing and launches such as Neurobion Forte and Evion Forte. No export figure in rupees was given.

Consolidated Q4 EBITDA including other income was INR 99.3 crore (6.5% margin) with PAT of INR 15.9 crore; FY26 consolidated EBITDA was INR 573.6 crore (9.4%) and PAT INR 161.5 crore. Standalone Q4 EBITDA was INR 57 crore (4.7%) and PAT a loss of INR 10.7 crore, with an exceptional labour-code cost of about INR 38-40 crore. The Board cut the dividend payout from 140% to 90%, subject to shareholder approval. Management guided to about 7 lakh tons of pipe dispatches and 13-14% EBITDA margin in FY27, with recovery expected from Q3 FY27.

500136|2026-03.headline: Ester Industries Q4 FY26 consolidated adjusted EBITDA of INR53.6 crore (15.5% margin) excluding INR10.24 crore FX-loan MTM; reported net loss of INR27.5 crore for FY26.

Consolidated total income rose 7.2% YoY to INR345.1 crore in Q4, with reported EBITDA of INR43.3 crore (12.6%) and PAT of INR7.9 crore. Full-year consolidated net loss of INR27.5 crore was driven mainly by non-cash MTM losses on euro-denominated term loans and a INR2.7 crore labour-code gratuity charge. Management expects BOPET margins to hold for 18 to 24 months, though Specialty Polymers softened in the quarter on demand loss in one marquee product and mix shift.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew about 2.2x YoY to INR65.7 crore on higher third-party volumes. Q4 segment EBIT INR42 crore (+73% YoY), margin 13% (+440 bps).

guidance_outlook: Management expects meaningful BOPET margin improvement in FY27 and beyond; sustained BOPET margins projected for about 18 to 24 months.
Q1 FY27 12-micron VA spread expected at INR30 to INR35/kg, versus INR32 to INR33 in Q4 FY26.
FY27 capex about INR70 crore consolidated: INR15 crore for new projects (stated IRR above 20%) and the balance for sustenance and maintenance; FY27 repayments about INR85 crore.
Borrowings targeted below INR40 crore by 31 March 2027, implying significant net debt reduction; cost of funds 9-10% consolidated.

Ester Filmtech utilisation 85% in Q4 FY26; Ester Industries 72%; consolidated about 78%. Management says film lines could run at 100% but chooses balanced operation to avoid low-margin volume.
Hyderabad rPET extruder (20,000 MT per annum) commissioned to support PCR film demand and sale of film-grade and textile-grade rPET.

ELITe JV (50:50 with Ester Loop Infinite Technologies): FEED completed by Tata Consulting Engineers; Toyo Engineering appointed as engineering consultant; land acquisition in progress, expected in the next few months.
demand_pricing: Management says Indian BOPET industry operating rates are about 80%; demand growth expected at 8-10% p.a. versus 6-8% previously, supported by FMCG growth and PWMR-driven substitution from BOPP/BOPE.

Raw material (PTA/MEG chips) moved sharply in March-April; management said it rose about 40% in April, passed through by value-add, and is now about INR100/kg of chips.
US reciprocal tariffs were struck down by the US Supreme Court; a 10% global tariff is now in place and is under legal challenge.
DGTR anti-dumping duties on Chinese and other BOPET imports recommended; Ministry of Finance notification still pending.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~15.5% adjusted EBITDA margin sustainable, and what is steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins would likely stay near 15% depending on market conditions and will be far better than the last 12-15 months average; BOPET margin support expected for 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ELITe contribution and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: No P&L impact in FY27. Operations expected by end CY28 (later stated as Q4 CY28 to Q1 CY29), so major benefit from FY30; first phase about 70,000 tonnes, close to USD150 million revenue at full utilisation with 40-45% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Specialty Polymers margins and revenue soften in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonality, lower demand for one key specialty product (still under assessment, not quantified), and mix shift toward lower-margin VAP products. Management says FY26 volume and value grew about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Debt reduction plan and FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Total debt about INR730-732 crore (long-term about INR380 crore). FY27 repayments about INR85 crore; capex about INR70 crore; borrowings to be kept below INR40 crore, implying INR45 crore reduction.

qa_highlights.question: How is euro-loan FX exposure being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Euro moved from about INR84 at loan sanction to about INR112 now, with about INR24 appreciation in 12-15 months. Management will partly offset via exports and take hedges opportunistically; Euribor 2.2%, with 75 bps markup, keeps cost of debt at Ester Filmtech under 7% in rupee terms.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost base is crude-linked and does feedstock hit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw material is a pass-through and value-add adjusts with supply-demand, so feedstock does not erode margins; VA is driven mainly by operating rates.

ELITe project timing has already slipped (land acquisition pending); project depends on land and EU ESPR demand by end CY28.
Anti-dumping duties still need Ministry of Finance notification; Chinese pricing and US tariff litigation remain open.
Ester Filmtech state subsidy of INR9.57 crore approved but not yet received; upside if collected, not in P&L.

500136|2026-06.headline: Ester Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA up 103% to INR58.9 crore, margin 13.3% vs 8.3%, PAT INR18.6 crore vs loss INR7.2 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q1 run-rate be sustained for the remaining three quarters, and were there one-off gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged an other income component and said it was one-time; it expects sustainable good earnings for the next 6 to 8 quarters on supply-demand balance and stable prices.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments will drive the INR2,000-2,200 crore revenue goal and how will margins evolve over 2 to 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are price (global prices expected to hold above the last 2-3 years), higher utilisation in films, specialty polymers and rPET, a rising share of high-priced specialty products, and operational efficiency. Management said it should reach the target in 2 to 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will ELITe face competition, given other players are already building textile-to-textile capacity?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Specialty Polymers and its margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to flat to single-digit growth in FY27, with a pipeline maturing in H2, and a 20% plus CAGR over 3 to 5 years. Margins may normalise in percentage terms, but absolute EBITDA and EBIT should grow from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What are the other income split, cash balance, debt repayment and JV funding plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income of about INR9.8 crore comprised treasury income of about INR3 crore, FD and investment interest of about INR3.5 crore, and FX gain of about INR1 crore, with the rest balance. Gross debt is INR720-722 crore, targeted to fall by INR100 crore to about INR620 crore by year-end. Cash is about INR235 crore, of which about INR140 crore is earmarked for the JV. 500144|2026-03.headline: Finolex Cables Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 22% YoY to a record electrical segment INR 1,697 crores, but margins were squeezed by Middle East-driven input costs.
500144|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew about 22% YoY and QoQ, with EBITDA up 7% YoY and PAT up 6% YoY, while full-year revenue rose about 19% and PAT about 14%. Management said late-quarter Middle East disruption, rupee depreciation and higher raw material costs left margins slightly under pressure, and inventory was built up by about INR 300 crores. Communication cables grew about 30% YoY in Q4 after flat full-year revenue, helped by hardening fiber prices, while the EHV JV turned profitable. Management declined to give formal guidance, citing volatility in the Middle East situation.

about INR 237 crores total; unallocable about INR 224 crores

segments.commentary: Full-year revenue flat at about INR 500 crores with about 7% volume growth; Q4 revenue up about 30% YoY and QoQ. About three-fourths of the segment is optic fiber. Fiber draw capacity 4 million km, utilisation about 3.2 million km.

segments.commentary: Revenue about INR 450 crores and profit about INR 21 crores in FY26; started the year with an order book of about INR 380 crores. Key machinery utilisation above 80%.

segments.commentary: Export revenue about INR 52 crores in FY26 versus about INR 30 crores in FY25; export share about 0.5-1% now, targeted at 2-3% over two years.

500144|2026-06.headline: Finolex Cables Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% to INR 2,013 crore and PAT 59% to INR 221 crore, helped by a temporary communication-cable margin spike near 30%.
500144|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 44% YoY to INR 2,013 crore, with PBT of INR 277 crore (up about 62%) and PAT of INR 221 crore (up about 59%). PBT margin expanded to 13.4% from 11.8% and PAT margin to 10.7% from 9.6%. Electrical cables drove growth on volume and price, while communication cables margins were lifted by low-cost opening fiber inventory that management said will normalise. Copper rod revenue collapsed to INR 8 crore as the rod plant shut on LPG shortage.

segments.name: Electrical cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,767 crore, up about 47%. Automotive, battery, flexible, solar and agricultural cables grew high double digits in volume; building wire grew low single digits in volume as channel destocked. Management said domestic electrical margin of about 10.5% should be sustainable.

segments.name: Communication cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 176 crore, up about 62% from INR 109 crore, with margin close to 30%. Volumes up about 30%; INR 30-40 crore of the revenue was exports to the US and Europe. Management expects margins to normalise to low double digits by year-end as opening inventory is consumed.

segments.name: Copper rod
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 8 crore vs INR 403 crore a year ago; rod plant shut for the quarter due to continued restriction on LPG availability.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Described as a weak link: fans were short of commercial LPG and conduit pipes short of PVC. Target of INR 5 billion FMEG revenue by FY28 reiterated, though the season was largely lost.

guidance_outlook: Communication cable margin expected to normalise; management still sees double-digit margins, likely low double digits, at year-end if demand holds.
Fiber draw capacity to rise from 4 million km to 8 million km by September 2026 (end of Q2), directly rather than in two phases.
Cabling capacity to rise from 8 million to 10 million km, with a longer timeline than the draw expansion.
Preform (100 metric ton) plant expected to stabilise in the next couple of months; management expects it to be fully functional from the September quarter. Phase 2 preform doubling under review.
FY27 capex unchanged at about INR 300 crore.
FMEG target of INR 5 billion by FY28 still intact per management.
capex_capacity: Fiber draw capacity: moving from 4 to 8 million km in one phase, completion by September 2026; original plan was 4 to 6 then 6 to 8.
Preform plant of 100 metric tons, equivalent to about 4 million km of fiber; the balance of 8 million km requires bought-in preform. Phase 2 expansion will be decided later.
Cabling capacity: one plant full, the other about three-quarters utilised; expansion to 10 million km.
FY27 capex about INR 300 crore, unchanged.
Management confirmed R&D and capex steps for data-centre-grade cables, with no details given.
demand_pricing: Fiber prices (G.652.D): about USD 5-6/km in December 2025, peaked at USD 17-18, now settling at USD 11-13/km; premium fiber sold up to USD 50/km.
Communication cable demand is driven by data-centre and AI build-outs; long-term contracts are over half of communication revenue and were repriced in late June 2026.
Electrical cables: about 60% construction, with automotive cables above 14% of the mix in Q1; LV and HV cables about 7-8% of the mix.
Electrical cable price hike of about 3% taken in May 2026 amid copper at about INR 14,000 per kg level; channel inventory was lower at quarter end.
Domestic fiber consumption about 25 million km per year vs China at 400 million km plus; management sees 50-60 million km potential.
Germanium tetrachloride supply is restricted with long lead times; supply covers the calendar year, with no multi-year contracts available.
BharatNet: no update; winners waiting given high prices.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are EBITDA margins, and how much of the expansion is one-off versus mix or copper pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Export gains came from optic fiber opportunities that may not recur, so management is conservative on them. Domestic electrical margin of about 10.5% should be sustainable; communication margins will fall as old raw material is used up, to low double digits by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What fiber prices are prevailing and how do they compare with December 2025?
qa_highlights.answer: G.652.D went from USD 5-6/km in December 2025 to USD 17-18, and is now settling at USD 11-13/km. Management declined to forecast further movement.

qa_highlights.question: How much of communication cable revenue is exports and to which geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 35-40 crore of the communication revenue was exports, mainly to the US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 100 MT preform plant lift margins by about 100 bps once it is fully functional?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see margins improving from here and called 100 bps stretching it, given that elevated prices may not last.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue reach about INR 300 crore per quarter from fiber?
qa_highlights.answer: At USD 11/km on 8 million km a year, fiber-only sales would be about USD 88 million, or about INR 250-260 crore; cabling adds 20-30% value on top, so INR 300 crore is achievable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FMEG outlook and does the INR 5 billion FY28 target still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed LPG shortages for fans and PVC shortages for conduit pipes; the target of INR 5 billion by FY28 remains.

Fiber supply is tight: preform and germanium are restricted, with preform sourcing still partly external and contracts about a year long.
Input cost volatility from LPG, helium, PVC and fuel after Middle East disruption; supply chain risk to the copper rod plant.
Export revenue depends on episodic opportunities; management cannot give a repeatable export mix.
Preform contract repricing could raise raw material costs once older contracts reset.
FMEG remains weak; catching up on the lost fan and pipe season is uncertain.

500147|2026-03.headline: Standalone revenue rose 162% YoY to INR2,000 million in Q1 CY26 with EBITDA of INR114 million, while consolidated EBITDA margin was only 1.4%.
500147|2026-03.overview: John Cockerill India reported its first quarter of consolidated results, including China, Belgium and Germany entities from January 2026. Standalone revenue grew 162% YoY to INR2,000 million and standalone EBITDA turned positive at INR114 million (about 5.7% margin), but management attributed margin pressure to hiring costs, a mix shift toward large projects, and one-off integration expenses. Consolidated revenue was INR3.4 billion (+56% YoY) with EBITDA of INR49 million (1.4% margin). Consolidated order book was about INR33 billion and standalone order book about INR13 billion (+101% YoY). Management targets a consolidated EBITDA margin of around 3% now and more than 10% over three years, while fundraising and USA consolidation timing remain undecided.

500147|2026-06.headline: John Cockerill India Q2 CY26 standalone revenue up 82% YoY to ~INR149 crore; consolidated INR299 crore (+18% YoY), order book ~INR4,500 crore.
500147|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 82% YoY to about INR149 crore and consolidated revenue reached about INR299 crore, up 18% YoY, but both fell sequentially as Q1 benefited from closing older projects. Management attributed weaker Q2 margins to upfront costs on newly started projects, organisation-building spend and one-time consolidation costs after the China, Germany and Belgium entities were brought under the listed company. Order wins of about INR1,200 crore in the quarter lifted the consolidated order book to about INR4,500 crore (standalone about INR2,200 crore). Management expects revenue and margins to build in H2 as new projects ramp, though it gave no quantified guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Expected marginally lower in next two quarters

segments.name: Standalone (India)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR149 crore, up 82% YoY; top customers Tata Steel and JSW. Order book ~INR2,200 crore.

segments.name: Consolidated group
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR299 crore, up 18% YoY; ArcelorMittal to be added to top customers after consolidation. Order book ~INR4,500 crore. Top five customers ~80% of revenue.

segments.name: Value-added services
segments.commentary: Service revenue in Q2 about one-third of Q1; management says lower because project progress was slower, not lack of orders, and services margins remain strong.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated INR8,000 crore top-line as the CY30 north-star, to come from organic growth (JVD, Volteron) and external acquisitions; several acquisitions under evaluation, no timeline given.
Management said consolidated revenue in H2 should improve significantly; did not expect to reach the ~INR2,000 crore CY25 pro-forma figure but 'should not be very far' if US is included.
Execution of new orders to ramp in Q3 and Q4 as engineering and procurement progress; impact on H2.
Employee cost expected to rise as manpower is added on the execution side; other expenses to be marginally lower than Q2 level in the next two quarters.
One-time transaction, forex and notional interest costs expected to stop from H2 after the parent agreed to a share-based payment instead of cash.
Further order wins expected before year-end across Asia, Europe, US and India; a JVD contract in Asia is in advanced discussion, targeted this year.
capex_capacity: Taloja Rolls Coating facility put into operation in June 2026; testing and trial orders underway, production initiation now.
Advanced Coating facility at Taloja, India, inaugurated (value-added services).
Shanghai office opened in China; workshop for assembly of special machines planned to open in Q3 CY26.
Execution timeline on contracts is typically two to three years; management now uses three years as the working assumption for the current book.
Headcount expansion on execution side planned, with employee cost rising.
demand_pricing: Order inflow ~INR1,200 crore in Q2, driven by demand for advanced processing, electrical steel, downstream quality and plant modernisation.
Management cited EU tariff-quota regime (18.3 million tons, 15% duty beyond quota) as supportive for hot-rolling, cold-rolling and processing-line investments.
India per capita steel consumption ~93 kg vs global ~230 kg; India steel production expected at 161.7 million tons this year.

JVD (Jet Vapor Deposition) pitched as a zinc-coating alternative to hot-dip galvanizing; customer savings cited at least INR1,000 per unit, up to 20x that, mainly for automotive and AHSS grades; first contract delayed by customer investment-approval process.
Potential cold-rolling order in the range of EUR50-100 million expected this year.
Competitors named: SMS and Danieli (Tier-1 OEMs), also Primetals; all have downstream portfolios.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR8,000 crore CY30 top-line target still valid, and how will it be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, as a north-star; two streams: organic (JVD, Volteron) and external acquisitions, which are under investigation. Volteron IP sits with John Cockerill SA, not the listed entity, and is not yet commercial.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the CY25 pro-forma revenue (~INR2,000 crore) far above reported (~INR960 crore), and can the US entity bridge the gap?
qa_highlights.answer: INR2,000 crore was a guideline; US is not a large contributor. Revenue depends on order progress. Management expects significant H2 improvement and said the gap should not be very far if US is included.

qa_highlights.question: Why did John Cockerill SA reduce holding from ~75% to ~70.4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to group priorities; SA remains a large shareholder and will get convertible preferential shares that would take it back to 72%+.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost structure outlook (employee cost ~INR68 crore, other expenses ~INR70 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost to rise with execution hiring; other expenses marginally below current level in next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone and consolidated order book, service revenue, and top-customer concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated ~INR4,500 crore, standalone ~INR2,200 crore. Service revenue ~one-third of Q1. Top five ~80% of revenue; standalone top are Tata Steel and JSW.

qa_highlights.question: Quantum of one-time consolidation costs in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify; said it would come back to the analyst. Costs covered transaction, forex, notional interest, legal, audit and due diligence across Belgium, Germany and China.

risks_watch: Margin pressure in Q2 from upfront costs on new projects; recovery depends on H2 execution ramp.
Revenue lumpiness: sequential decline in Q2 from Q1 project close-outs.
Consolidation and ongoing parent-company cost sharing (R&D, technical development) may persist beyond one-time items.
JVD first commercial contract repeatedly delayed by customer investment validation; Volteron not yet commercial and needs pilot validation.
Gap between INR8,000 crore CY30 target and current run-rate; acquisition plans have no detail or timeline.

Customer concentration: top five ~80% of revenue.

rows.why: Several acquisitions are under evaluation with no timeline or detail, and the INR8,000 crore CY30 north-star relies on them alongside organic growth from JVD and Volteron.

500148|2026-03.headline: UFlex Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 31.8% YoY to Rs 6,265 mn at a 15.3% margin, the highest in 14 quarters, though management flagged spreads moderating in Q1 FY27.
500148|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12.8% QoQ and 5.7% YoY to Rs 40,973 mn, with EBITDA up 36.3% QoQ and 31.8% YoY to Rs 6,265 mn. Management attributed the jump to a March spike in film spreads, as raw material increases were more than passed through. For FY26, revenue grew 2.1% to Rs 155,130 mn and EBITDA rose 8.1% to Rs 19,836 mn, with margin up 70 bps to 12.8%. Management said spreads for BOPET and BOPP have since moderated significantly, and it declined to give an FY27 EBITDA margin range.

financial_highlights.change: Management said it expects a similar level going forward; analyst cited Rs 378 crore for FY25 base, management referenced Rs 700 crore last fiscal, figures were inconsistent on the call

segments.name: Packaging Films
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 128,037 MT, +11.4% QoQ and +0.9% YoY; FY26 volume fell 1% to 498,034 MT. Americas volume 31,883 MT (+23% QoQ, +18% YoY); Europe 35,367 MT (+12.9% QoQ, soft YoY); India 26,888 MT (+6.3% QoQ, -6.3% YoY); MEA 33,899 MT (+4.6% QoQ, +1.5% YoY).

segments.name: Packaging Solutions / Packaging (incl. aseptic, holography)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 38,842 MT, +7.1% QoQ and +1.6% YoY; FY26 volume up 5.1% to 151,755 MT. Aseptic packs rose 15.9% QoQ; FY26 aseptic volume 7.97 bn packs, +2.4%. Packaging Solutions is about 36% of revenue and about 40% of FY26 EBITDA.

guidance_outlook: Company expects FY27 performance to be better than FY26, driven by better utilisation of new capacity, product mix and capacity coming online in FY27.
Aseptic FY27 sales volume guided to about 10.0-10.5 bn packs, up from about 8 bn in FY26, including part-year contribution from the Egypt 12 bn facility.
Management declined to give an FY27 EBITDA margin range, citing Q1 still in progress.
Margin outlook: non-film packaging margins expected to hold; packaging film margins expected to moderate with industry trends, especially in India.
Roughly Rs 1,900-2,000 crore of the Rs 2,169 crore consolidated CWIP expected to be capitalised during FY27.
capex_capacity: Aseptic 12 bn-pack facility in Egypt expected to commission in H1 FY27; remaining capex about Rs 972 crore.
WPP bag facility in Mexico (mainly for US pet food) expected to commission in H1 FY27; remaining capex largely incurred. Installed WPP capacity about 80 mn bags.
PET recycling facility (rPET 36,000 MT and rMLP 3,600 MT) commissioned at Sector 155 at end of April 2026; ramp-up over next three quarters; Rs 47 crore remaining capex incurred.
54,000 MTPA BOPP line at Dharwad, India, expected to commission in FY27-28; significant capex in FY26-27. Manufacturing line capex about Rs 700 crore, mostly in FY26 and FY27.
Sanand (India) aseptic debottlenecking to 12 bn packs achieved in Q3 FY26. CWIP at March 2026 Rs 2,169 crore consolidated.
demand_pricing: In Q4, raw material (PET chips, BOPET and BOPP homopolymer) prices rose sharply in March, but market prices rose more, so spreads widened and some additional spread was realised.
Spreads have since moderated significantly, particularly for BOPET, and are well below Q4 levels as raw material prices softened and market prices fell.

Americas demand recovered after the US government shutdown; Europe demand soft YoY on weak CPG demand and cheaper imports; India film demand hit by customers deferring purchases amid price-correction expectations.
International revenue is 57% of total and India 43%; the mix has shifted toward overseas over the past year.
Egypt benefited from localised sourcing as supply chains were disrupted in the region.

qa_highlights.question: What is the spread outlook for BOPP and BOPET, and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads spiked in March and widened in Q4, but have moderated significantly in Q1 FY27, especially for BOPET; utilisation rose sequentially in Q4 and management will watch it closely given price softening.

qa_highlights.question: What is the depreciation, finance cost and capitalisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated depreciation and finance cost were each about Rs 787 crore and Rs 777 crore, with both expected to remain at similar levels. Roughly Rs 1,900-2,000 crore of CWIP is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will leverage come down and what is the peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to net debt/EBITDA improving from 4.51x in Q3 to 4.35x in Q4, which excludes EBITDA from projects yet to commission, and expects further improvement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aseptic volume outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Aseptic volume expected at about 10.0-10.5 bn packs versus about 8 bn in FY26, including part-year Egypt contribution; FY26 utilisation about 80% plus on the 12 bn capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory and cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-film packaging margins expected to hold, film margins may moderate. Blended cost of funds about 9% (was above 9%); refinancing is premature, with cheaper overseas funding expected to help.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company commit to an EBITDA margin range for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it was too early in Q1 to give an annual EBITDA range and would track margin developments closely.

risks_watch: Film spreads have moderated sharply from March peak; Q1 FY27 margins at risk, especially in India films.
Commissioning timelines for Egypt aseptic (12 bn) and Mexico WPP facilities (H1 FY27) and the ramp-up of rPET/rMLP capacity.
Leverage at 4.35x net debt/EBITDA and about Rs 8,500 crore debt; monitor leverage as new capacity contributes EBITDA.
Q&A on aseptic packaging: a PIL and litigation involving liquor packaging in some states; management declined to quantify exposure.
Shareholder-value question on the stock's valuation and promoter stake; management said it respects market price and would convey the suggestion to promoters.
Inconsistent finance cost figures stated on call (Rs 378 crore vs Rs 700 crore for FY25); verify against filings.
500148|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the Q4 recovery and the new capacity, but noticeably cautious on Q1 FY27 margins and spreads, and evasive on FY27 EBITDA range, WPP pricing and liquor-related aseptic exposure. Management also declined to quantify several analyst questions.
key_quotes: both the aggregate EBITDA recorded during the quarter and also the EBITDA margin achieved was the highest in the last 14 quarters, which was after Q1 of FY23.

the company expects to perform better in FY27 than FY26, driven by improved utilization of recently commissioned capacities, product mix optimization and additional capacities expected to come online during FY27.
I think it will be a little premature to give a sense of what kind of EBITDA range will be there for the year as a whole.

rows.why: Q4 margin of 15.3% was lifted by a March spread spike that has since reversed for BOPET; management expects packaging film margins to moderate while non-film packaging margins only hold; FY26 margin was 12.8%.

rows.why: Egypt 12 bn aseptic facility expected to commission in H1 FY27 with Rs 972 cr remaining capex; Mexico WPP commissioning H1 FY27; Rs 1,900-2,000 cr of Rs 2,169 cr CWIP to be capitalised in FY27; Sector 155 rPET plant already commissioned end-April 2026.

rows.why: Aseptic volume guided to 10.0-10.5 bn packs vs about 8 bn in FY26 (+25-31%), Q4 consolidated volume 166,879 MT (+10.3% QoQ), but India film volume was -6.3% YoY in Q4 as customers defer purchases.

rows.why: Utilisation rose sequentially across most plants and aseptic FY26 utilisation is about 80%+ on 12 bn capacity, but management said 'we are not saying no to the capex' without committing to a new board-approved project beyond the Dharwad BOPP line (Rs 700 cr) already under way.

rows.why: Aseptic volume guided to 10.0-10.5 bn packs from about 8 bn in FY26 with Egypt 12 bn plant, and rPET/rMLP recycled capacity (36,000 MT and 3,600 MT) ramping over three quarters from end-April 2026.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA improving from 4.51x to 4.35x
rows.why: Leverage fell 16 bps QoQ to 4.35x and management expects further improvement, but ~Rs 8,500 cr debt and 4.35x leverage remain high while new capacity is yet to earn EBITDA.

rows.label: Blended cost of funds down to about 9%
rows.why: Cost of funds fell from above 9% to about 9%, with cheaper overseas funding expected to help, but management said refinancing is premature.

rows.label: Liquor-packaging PIL and litigation on aseptic packs
rows.why: A PIL and litigation involving liquor packaging in some states exists, management declined to quantify exposure against aseptic volume of about 8 bn packs in FY26.

500148|2026-06.headline: UFlex Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38% YoY to Rs 53,972 million and EBITDA rose 92% to Rs 9,198 million, with margin at 17%.
500148|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 38% YoY to Rs 53,972 million and reported EBITDA rose 92% to Rs 9,198 million, with margin up 480 bps to 17%. Normalized EBITDA (after Rs 825 million forex derivative adjustment) was Rs 8,373 million, up 78%, at a 15.5% margin. Overseas operations (Egypt, Mexico, Nigeria) contributed about 91% of the Rs 4,410 million incremental EBITDA, while India volumes and Aseptic softened. Management guided to 35% growth in FY27 revenue and EBITDA over FY26, while saying Q2 would see some normalization from exceptional Q1 realizations.

financial_highlights.metric: Normalized EBITDA (post Rs 825 mn forex derivative adjustment)

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 580 million, 1.5% margin in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Packaging Films (India)
segments.commentary: Volume 29,323 MT, up 9.1% QoQ but declined YoY against a high Q1 FY26 base affected by industry supply shortage. Converters resumed buying after May-June price normalization.

segments.name: Americas
segments.commentary: Volume 31,724 MT, up 18% YoY, supported by US onshoring push and constrained West Asia/India imports.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Volume 35,653 MT, flat YoY; low-priced imports pressured CPP, CIS BOPET steady. Demand expected to moderate next quarter on seasonal holidays.

segments.name: Middle East and Africa
segments.commentary: Volume 39,486 MT, up 14.9% YoY and 16.5% QoQ; Egypt led growth and Nigeria benefited from export opportunities as customers derisked supply chains.

segments.name: Packaging (Aseptic and flexible)
segments.commentary: Volume down 8.4% YoY to 37,285 MT due to shift to high-margin products in India, Aseptic softness from duty-free Indonesian imports, larger pack-size mix overseas and West Asia consignment delays.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth of about 35% over FY26 (management also cited 30%-plus in places); management said it normally avoids guidance.
Q2 expected to see some normalization from exceptionally strong Q1 realizations; management asked investors to benchmark YoY, not QoQ.
Expects FY27 EBITDA margin of about 14%-plus; said margins could be better if geopolitical conditions hold.
Debt-EBITDA targeted at about 3x in FY28 and below 3x by FY29; interest cost expected to fall by about 1% over the next year.
Volume to roughly double over three years to FY29 as Egypt Aseptic, Noida recycling and Mexico WPP ramp; FY26-FY29 CAGR indicated at least 10%, to be confirmed by IR.

Egypt Aseptic (12 billion packs) expected commissioning in H1 FY27, targeting around 30% utilization in year one annualized (about 2 billion packs in FY27 if started 1 October) and 60-70% in year two.

Noida Sector 155 recycling plant (39,000 MT per annum) commissioned 30 April 2026; capex about USD 30-32 million, no further capex planned.
Mexico 80-million-unit WPP bags plant commissioned 31 July 2026; capex about USD 54 million.
Egypt Aseptic greenfield (12 billion packs): over USD 100 million spent, about USD 15 million remaining; commissioning H1 FY27.
Dharwad BOPP brownfield: USD 10 million spent, about USD 50+ million planned over FY27-FY28. Remaining new capex about USD 80-100 million; management says FY27 capex cycle about 75% complete.
Domestic utilization about 70-73%; specialty films (metallizer, ultra-high barrier) utilized about 30-40%. India Aseptic installed capacity about 24 billion packs.
demand_pricing: BOPP prices up about 25-32% and BOPET up about 30-35% from February 2026 (pre West Asia war) levels, per management.
Management said raw material prices rose but less than finished goods, and prices now appear to be normalizing; prices described as stable at current levels while the West Asia crisis persists.
Overseas selling prices said to be about 2.5x India prices; overseas margins higher because pass-through is easier.
Aseptic faces duty-free imports from Indonesia under India trade treaty at aggressive prices; management says value realization improved via shift to value-added films.
Management said it carries little inventory, so Q1 realizations were passed through to customers; customers prefer UFlex's integrated, local supply for security of supply.

qa_highlights.question: How are price realizations and raw material trends shaping up in India and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: BOPP prices up 25-32% and BOPET up 30-35% since February 2026; raw material costs rose less than finished goods prices, which are normalizing.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 margin and growth sustainable for full-year FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing 2-3 years of capex; FY27 guided to about 35% revenue and EBITDA growth over FY26, with FY27 EBITDA margin about 14%-plus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalization expected in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined QoQ benchmarking; said Q2 will normalize from exceptional Q1 realization but growth remains about 35% YoY, with shipment timing risk around West Asia.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15.5% normalized margin sustainable and how much currency impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Forex impact about Rs 70 crore in the quarter (Rs 825 mn per the prepared remarks); management said margins are sustainable over next 3 years, not just FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for surplus cash: debt reduction vs capex vs shareholder returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus cash to go to debt reduction; leverage to fall to about 3x in FY28. No buyback planned; management prefers wealth creation via growth. 60-70% of future capex to value-added products.

qa_highlights.question: Interest rate and rating outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Rated AA by CRISIL and India Ratings; interest cost fell 0.3-0.4% this quarter and management targets a further 1% reduction in the next year.

risks_watch: Egypt Aseptic (12 billion packs) commissioning slipping beyond H1 FY27; management flagged a possible 1-2 week slip and about 2 billion packs in FY27 assumes a 1 October start
Q2 normalization after exceptional Q1 realizations; management declined QoQ benchmarking and flagged shipment timing risk from West Asia and Bab-el-Mandeb disruptions
Sustainability of pricing: BOPP up 25-32% and BOPET up 30-35% since February 2026; management said prices could correct if the West Asia crisis eases
Aseptic pressure from duty-free Indonesian imports under the India trade treaty; Aseptic volumes down 8.4% YoY company-wide and management expects recovery only from Q3

Guidance inconsistency on the call: 35% vs 30%-plus growth, FY27 EBITDA margin of about 14%-plus, and the 15.5% normalized margin treated as sustainable over three years; Q1 forex impact of Rs 825 mn (about Rs 70 crore per the Q&A)

Debt-EBITDA reduction from about 4.5x to about 3.5x, with a target of about 3x in FY28; interest cost cut of about 1% targeted over the next year; FY26-FY29 CAGR of at least 10% still to be confirmed by IR
