rows.why: Egypt Aseptic (12 billion packs, over USD 100 mn spent, ~USD 15 mn remaining) is due for commissioning in H1 FY27 with ~30% year-one utilisation (~2 bn packs in FY27 if started 1 Oct), and Dharwad BOPP brownfield (USD 50+ mn planned over FY27-FY28) is under construction, while Mexico WPP (commissioned 31 Jul 2026) and Noida recycling (commissioned 30 Apr 2026) are already live.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 volume was 173,471 MT (+1.7% YoY) with Americas +18% and MEA +14.9%, and Egypt Aseptic at ~30% year-one utilisation plus Mexico WPP and Noida recycling should lift volumes, with management targeting doubling by FY29 (FY26-FY29 CAGR at least 10%, unconfirmed).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Domestic utilisation is only ~70-73% and remaining new capex (~USD 80-100 mn) is already committed with management saying the FY27 capex cycle is ~75% complete, so a fresh capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is ~35% revenue/EBITDA growth (also cited as 30%+) with FY27 EBITDA margin ~14%+ and management says margins could be better if geopolitical conditions hold; Q1 normalised EBITDA was up 78%, so upside is conditional on pricing holding.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged Q2 normalisation from exceptional Q1 realisations and shipment timing risk from West Asia/Bab-el-Mandeb, and Egypt Aseptic could slip 1-2 weeks beyond H1 FY27, though FY27 growth still guided ~35% YoY.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Egypt Aseptic (12 bn packs) commissioning in H1 FY27 and shift to value-added films (60-70% of future capex to value-added products; specialty films utilised only ~30-40%) indicate new product and market capacity coming online.

rows.label: Debt-EBITDA to ~3x in FY28, below 3x by FY29
rows.why: Debt-EBITDA fell from ~4.5x in FY26 to ~3.5x in Q1 FY27, with surplus cash going to debt reduction and management guiding to ~3x in FY28.

rows.label: Pricing normalisation risk on BOPP/BOPET
rows.why: BOPP prices are up 25-32% and BOPET up 30-35% since Feb 2026, and management said prices could correct if the West Asia crisis eases, while currently stable.

rows.label: Aseptic recovery from Q3 vs Indonesian duty-free imports
rows.why: Aseptic volume fell 8.4% YoY to 37,285 MT (India aseptic capacity ~24 bn packs) and management expects recovery only from Q3, conditional on the Indonesian import pressure easing.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q1 delivery, ~35% FY27 growth and sustainable margins for three years, but evasive on QoQ normalisation and deferred the FY29 CAGR to IR; analysts pressed on guidance inconsistency (35% vs 30%+), the 15.5% normalised margin and forex impact.

500153|2026-03.headline: Ganesh Benzoplast Q4 FY26 consol PAT swung to INR152 mn from a loss, but JNPT rental reset (~INR23 cr rise) compresses LST margins for 2-3 years.
500153|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR1,115 mn and PAT turned to INR152 mn from a INR132 mn loss in Q4 FY25. Full-year FY26 consol revenue grew 10% to INR4,114 mn and PAT rose 93% to INR733 mn, with EPS of INR10.19. Management attributed the margin dip to a 30-year JNPT lease rental reset, with the old plots' rental rising to about INR25 cr from about INR2 cr, partly offset by a one-time INR9 cr income. Expansion of about 50,000 kL at JNPT is under way, with management guiding to commissioning by calendar year-end 2026.

segments.name: LST (JNPT, Kochi, Goa terminals)
segments.commentary: JNPT running at about 100% utilisation, Kochi at 80-85%+, Goa close to zero after bunkering demand left post mining ban. Management said rental segment EBITDA margin was about 45-47%, unchanged, per an analyst's read of prior disclosures; the company did not restate the segment margin split this quarter.

segments.name: Chemical division
segments.commentary: Management said Q4 had two exceptional charges: recertification costs for UK/Europe and settlement of staff dues and salary hikes. Excluding these, Chemical PAT would have risen at least 15% YoY. Chemical capex is limited to small debottlenecking.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Large INR175 cr JSW port order; engineering complete, groundwork expected after monsoon. Margins described as higher single digit. Value executed not disclosed.

guidance_outlook: JNPT expansion of about 50,000 kL (about 40,000-49,000 kL phase) to be completed by December 2026 (calendar year-end), with revenue expected from Q4 FY26/calendar year-end.
A further about 60,000 kL capacity is planned for next year; combined capex for both phases is about INR100 cr. Installed capacity to rise about 15%.

Management expects rentals to rise 5-6% annually on existing tanks, and the EBITDA margin to recover over 2-3 years; another view was that the cost is recovered in 15-18 months with new tanks at about 80% EBITDA margin.
Goa petroleum modification (blended petrol approvals) to start after monsoon and finish by 31 March 2027; no contract signed yet. Capex about INR2 cr.
Chemical expected to remain on a steady path with no major capacity project.
capex_capacity: Total installed capacity about 3.50 lakh kL; about 2.80 lakh kL sits on JNPT plots, per management.
JNPT utilisation almost 100%, Goa close to zero, Kochi above 80-85%, overall about 95%.
JNPT expansion of about 50,000 kL under way at capex of INR40-50 cr for this phase; 3 large 45,000 kL tanks are being built.
Ammonia storage and LPG bullets capex of around INR450-500 cr is still under discussion and not initiated; about 5-6 acres of JNPT land is set aside.
Visakhapatnam LOI progress is on hold because of a dispute between a prior plot holder and the Visakhapatnam port.
demand_pricing: JNPT rentals are a mix of long-term storage contracts and spot. Management said no exceptional demand arose from the war-related supply disruption, so no pricing windfall was taken.

Management said JNPT lease rental reset happens every 30 years (last in 2025, next in 2055). The old plots' rental rose to about INR25 cr from about INR2 cr, a provision booked in Q4 for the cumulative amount.
A one-time exceptional income of INR9 cr came from termination of an LPG arrangement (around Feb-March 2025 per management).
Management said the company is pursuing a Singapore subsidiary for chemical basket trade, still at a preliminary stage.
Receivables over 6 months have risen because of extended credit terms in EPC; retention money is paid after one year. Management said there is no bad debt issue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and why is Goa near zero?
qa_highlights.answer: JNPT is near 100%, Cochin 80-85%+, Goa close to zero since the bunkering business left after the Goa mining ban; overall about 95%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall because of rental expense?
qa_highlights.answer: The JNPT land was acquired in 1995, and the 30-year rental reset took effect in 2025. Old-plot rent rose to about INR25 cr from about INR2 cr.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Chemical slow in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no slowdown. Two exceptional items (UK/Europe recertification and staff dues/salary settlement) hit the quarter; excluding them, Chemical PAT would have risen at least 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consol EBITDA margin fall from about 21-22% in Q3 to about 18-19% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the full INR25 cr annual lease rental was provisioned in Q4 cumulatively, and the YoY margin drop was about INR6 cr against the INR23 cr rise. The company expects to pass the cost to customers and recover it in 15-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 50% capex complete by Q1 or the full phase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the entire 49,000 kL phase will be completed by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add ports outside JNPT, Kochi and Goa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will only deploy capital where ROI matches or beats JNPT. No such opportunity has been found, though it is open to overseas deals with back-to-back contracts.

risks_watch: JNPT rental reset compresses LST margin; recovery timeline of 2-3 years depends on 5-6% annual rental escalation.
Goa terminal near zero utilisation, with INR10-12 lakh/month holding cost; petroleum handling there has no signed contract.
Expansion timing: 50,000 kL due by December 2026 and 60,000 kL next year; any slip would delay revenue.
Receivables over 6 months rising because of EPC credit terms and retention money.
Visakhapatnam LOI on hold; ammonia/LPG bullet capex of INR450-500 cr not yet initiated.
Management could not give the JSW EPC executed value or the Goa total historical investment on the call.
500153|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the JNPT expansion and long-term rental escalation, but defensive on margin compression and receivables. Several answers were vague or deferred (Goa investment, EPC progress, segment margin split), and some management statements conflicted on timing.
key_quotes: So, this is every 30 years, there is a reset in the rentals by the ports.
Chemical is also running more or less on steady state.
So, the combined capex for both of the capacities together is approximately INR100 crores.

rows.why: Goa petroleum modification (blended petrol approvals, capex about INR2 cr) is set to start after monsoon and finish by 31 March 2027, but no contract is signed yet; Singapore chemical-basket subsidiary is at a preliminary stage.

rows.why: Engineering is complete on the INR175 cr JSW order with margins described as higher single digit, though executed value was not disclosed and groundwork only starts after monsoon.

500153|2026-09.headline: Ganesh Benzoplast to divest JNPA, Goa and Cochin liquid tank farms plus Daund rail for INR1,154 crore, with INR500 crore due around January 2027.
500153|2026-09.overview: Management, on an investor call held October 7, 2026, outlined the sale of the LST (liquid storage tank) businesses at JNPA, Goa and Cochin, together with the JNPA-linked Daund rail business, for INR1,154 crore plus an exit-linked consideration. Payment is staged: about INR500 crore by January 2027, about INR300 crore by March 2027, and the balance INR354 crore over 12 to 18 months tied to port approvals and tank commissioning. Of the first INR500 crore, about INR190-200 crore goes to tax and bank-limit closure and about INR200 crore to a buyback and special dividend, with INR100 crore for chemical expansion and EPC book growth. Management guided chemical PAT to about INR18 crore in FY26 rising to INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years, and EPC PAT to about INR150 crore by around FY30. Much of the Q&A probed the rationale for exiting the higher-margin LST business and the lack of quarter-wise numbers.

financial_highlights.metric: Divestment consideration (JNPA, Goa, Cochin LST + Daund rail)
financial_highlights.change: plus further consideration linked to investor exit valuation (not quantified)

financial_highlights.metric: Planned shareholder return from first tranche (buyback + special dividend)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR5 crore PAT in FY24 (full year)
management says profit up ~1,000% over last 2 years
management now expects above INR200 crore

segments.name: LST (liquid tank farm) – divested
segments.commentary: JNPA, Goa and Cochin liquid tank farms and JNPA-linked Daund rail are being sold for INR1,154 crore. JNPA expected in books until about Dec 2026/Jan 2027, with Cochin and Goa removed gradually over the next calendar year. Company retains a small stake in a Kandla terminal, described as insignificant; a non-compete applies.

segments.name: Chemical (benzoic acid, sodium benzoate)
segments.commentary: Two plants, each about 1,000 tons/month; utilisation about 70-80%. One plant is being doubled, with completion expected July 2027. REACH certification obtained for UK and EU; orders over 600 tons received, expected to reach about 2,000 tons/year. Management targets chemical PAT of INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years.

segments.name: EPC (tankage, pipeline, petroleum)
segments.commentary: Order book expected to be about INR500-600 crore next year, with EPC revenue of about INR250 crore per annum from FY28 onward per management. Targeted 5% share of a INR70,000 crore 5-year petroleum-related EPC opportunity implies about INR150 crore PAT. EBITDA margin assumption 7-8% on a conservative basis, PAT margin basis not clearly specified.

guidance_outlook: Chemical PAT expected to be INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years (from INR18 crore in FY26); management says chemical profitability to rise 3-4x in 4-5 years.
EPC PAT of about INR150 crore targeted by around 2030, assuming 5% share of INR70,000 crore 5-year petroleum EPC pipeline.
Total PAT target of about INR210 crore in 3-5 years versus about INR70 crore currently; FY28 PAT growth target of 15-20% YoY.
Chemical revenue to rise about 20-25% in the year after capacity commissioning and about 70-80% in the following year, per management.
Debt expected to stay at minimum; company does not expect to need significant bank debt, although bank limits are needed for guarantees.
Further tranche proceeds to be used for expansion or shareholder returns, decided by the board based on capex visibility.
capex_capacity: Chemical capacity doubling at one plant (of two, about 1,000 tons/month each), targeted completion July 2027.
Stage 1 capex across chemical and EPC of not more than about INR150 crore.
New agro and specialty derivative plants planned with technology and licence partners; to be funded later, with back-to-back buyback arrangements with customers under discussion.
Management says no balance capex remains on the JNPA port asset, and that about 43 tanks are under construction at JNPA (per management answer on LST growth capex).
Capex to continue over the next 1-2 years; first stage expected to be complete by FY28.
demand_pricing: REACH certification enabled UK and EU exports; over 600 tons of orders received.
Management says the chemical business profit grew from INR5 crore (FY24) to INR15-16 crore (FY25), INR18 crore (FY26) with turnover broadly flat.
Crude-linked raw material costs: management says it passes through fluctuations to customers but cannot rule out margin impact at high crude prices.
Chemical EBITDA margin cited by analyst at 11-12%; management expects to sustain or improve it without a firm number.
EPC contract wins include KKR (about INR300 crore), GACL/NALCO JV pipeline, ANA Oleo, Allana, Adani MPL and Jindal projects.

qa_highlights.question: Deepesh Sancheti (Maanya Finance): what is the timeline for the next INR300 crore tranche, and how will EPC working capital be funded after debt is repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance INR354 crore spread over 12-18 months, milestone-linked to port approvals and tank commissioning. Bank guarantee lines used for EPC will be temporarily replaced with deal funds and reinstated; management says sufficient cash will come from tranches and PAT for EPC working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Romil Savaliya (CJ Shah Family Office): why has chemical top line been flat for years, and what is changing in EPC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it focuses on profitability, not turnover: chemical PAT went from INR5 crore in FY24 to about INR15-16 crore in FY25 and INR18 crore in FY26 on similar turnover. EPC is being moved from a support role for LST to an independent division targeting about INR150 crore PAT in 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Nishita (Sapphire Capital): what is the rationale for divesting the higher-margin LST business, and what is chemical capacity and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Rationale cited as projected cost increases and market movement over 2-3 years, plus the value offered by the buyer, which management said it judged fair. Chemical has two plants of about 1,000 tons/month each; one is being doubled by July 2027; utilisation is about 70-80%. Q1 chemical PAT of INR6 crore is chemical only, and EPC quarterly turnover was not given.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavesh Patel (Patel Investments): will the 40-45% shareholder return apply to later tranches, and what is FY28 PAT expectation and debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The buyback and special dividend apply to the first tranche only; later tranches depend on capex visibility and board decisions. Management targets 15-20% PAT growth YoY into FY28 from about INR70 crore. No significant bank debt is expected, though bank limits are needed for guarantees.

qa_highlights.question: Saurabh (Mangalam): is there a non-compete, will the company re-enter LST, and how exposed is chemical margin to crude?
qa_highlights.answer: A standard non-compete applies; the Kandla stake is a carve-out and insignificant; no plan to return to LST near term. Crude pass-through is attempted but margin impact cannot be ruled out at high crude.

qa_highlights.question: Prateek Kothari (CRK Stock Broking): what is the first tranche's use of funds and what is the chemical top-line ballpark?
qa_highlights.answer: Of the first INR500 crore, about INR200 crore goes to shareholders, about INR190-200 crore to tax and bank-limit closure, and the balance to chemical and EPC growth. Chemical FY26 revenue was about INR180 crore, now expected above INR200 crore; revenue expected to rise 20-25% in the year after commissioning and 70-80% in the following year.

qa_highlights.question: Krupa Sanjay Desai (Electrum Capital): what EPC revenue and margin are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: EPC revenue this year about INR50-60 crore given seasonality; about INR250 crore per year from next year with KKR and other contracts. Management cited a general expectation of about 10% margin but planned at 7-8%, specified as PAT; the INR150 crore EPC PAT is expected by about 2030.

risks_watch: Timing of the INR500 crore (about January 2027) and INR300 crore (March 2027) tranches depends on port approvals and shareholder approval; the INR354 crore balance is milestone-linked with no fixed date.
Q1 FY27 chemical PAT of INR6 crore (about 10% margin on INR60 crore revenue) is well above the FY26 run-rate; management says it aims to sustain it, but gave no firm guidance.
Loss of JNPA LST earnings from around the March 2027 quarter, with Cochin and Goa rolling off over the next calendar year; the group's profit base will shift to chemical and EPC.
Chemical capacity doubling at one plant targeted for July 2027; execution and ramp-up timing is key to the 20-25% and 70-80% revenue step-ups.
Crude-linked raw material costs could compress chemical margins; management cannot rule this out.

EPC targets (order book INR500-600 crore next year, INR2,500-3,000 crore in 4-5 years, 5% of INR70,000 crore pipeline) are unquantified attempts; working capital needs post-debt repayment are unclear.
Quarterly EPC turnover and profit were not provided; management will share on request, so segment disclosure remains limited.
key_quotes: So, combined with the chemical PAT of about INR60 crores and the EPC PAT about INR150 crores, you're looking at your company going in the next 3 to 4, 5 years to about INR210 crores of PAT, which is currently at 70.
And one important thing of about the buyback that you should know is that the promoters will not be participating in it.
But I cannot commit or I cannot speculate that no margins will ever be hit on how crude behaves suddenly, but we have -- I believe, enough systems in place to sustain any reasonable fluctuations.
So, capex will keep happening through the next 1 or 2 years continuously.
500153|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the growth outlook for chemical and EPC, with an emphasis on shareholder returns. Cautious and evasive on specific numbers and timelines: management repeatedly declined to speculate on future figures, gave port-approval timing only as "expected", and did not answer the ownership question about CJ Shah family stake.

rows.why: Chemical PAT guided above INR20 crore in FY27 versus INR18 crore in FY26, and Q1 FY27 chemical PAT of INR6 crore on about INR60 crore revenue implies about 10% margin, but management gave no firm margin guidance and flagged crude pass-through risk.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.why: Utilisation is 70-80%, Stage 1 capex is capped at about INR150 crore, and new agro and specialty derivative plants are planned with partners but unfunded, so further capex decisions depend on board capex visibility.

500165|2026-03.headline: Kansai Nerolac Q4 FY26 standalone revenue up 7.6% and PBDIT up 21%; management guides to 13-14% margin and high-single-digit decorative price increases.
500165|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 7.6% with PBDIT up 21% and PBT before exceptional items up 12.8%, while full-year standalone revenue rose 3.2% and PBDIT 1.2%. Consolidated Q4 PBDIT rose 30.6%. Management attributed the quarter's margin resilience to better mix in both decorative and industrial, and to lower other expenses. Price hikes totalling roughly 2% in March and 5-6% in each subsequent round were taken amid a crude and rupee shock tied to the West Asia crisis. The company said demand has held so far with no volume impact seen, but visibility for FY27 is "wait and watch."

PBT before exceptional items, FY26 standalone

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Management said the decorative volume-value gap was not significant, as low-profit items were deliberately curtailed. Growth in the decorative business was described as mid-single-digit or lower, and new products and super premium emulsions drove better mix. Decorative projects are now about 10%+ of sales, and new businesses (waterproofing, construction chemicals, wood finish) are also 10%+ and slightly higher than projects.

segments.name: Industrial - Automotive
segments.commentary: Auto coatings grew close to double digits in Q4, with passenger vehicle demand healthy and a long waiting list cited by customers. Two-wheeler demand grew at high double digits, and commercial vehicles and tractors grew at double digits.

segments.name: Industrial - General and Powder
segments.commentary: Overall industrial grew slightly higher single digits in Q4 per management. Powder coatings returned to mid-single-digit growth with a good channel sales performance.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated the historical EBITDA margin band of 13-14% for FY27 on both consolidated and standalone bases, with an endeavour to reach the higher end. FY26 was said to have been within that range.

Decorative price increases: about 2% in late March, then 5-6% each on 10 April, 21 April and 11 May, for a net higher-single-digit increase as of now. Aniruddha Joshi's question put the cumulative effective hike in the low teens; management did not dispute it.
Industrial channel prices were revised effective mid-April. OE price increases have been granted in part, with negotiation timing slightly delayed but effective-from dates protecting margins.

Management said a crude price of about USD 100 would be manageable with current price hikes. It expects to live with the inflation for about 6 months, with a possible second-half reversal if conditions improve.
Price increases could be scaled back through schemes if deflation arrives. Management said dealer incentives were adjusted in line with the price hikes.
capex_capacity: Capex is described as normal and in line with prior years.
Powder and industrial liquid coatings are running at about 70-75% utilisation, with sufficient capacity.
Management aims to grow performance coatings at double digits, tied to infrastructure spend and the expansion plan outlined at the February strategy session.
Paint Plus retail format has replaced NXTGEN Shoppe and Shop-in-Shop, with about 250+ stores opened.
Paint-as-a-service is present in more than 250 cities; the Illuminati architect and designer programme in 45+ cities; the painter programme covers more than 1.2 lakh painters.
demand_pricing: Decorative demand has improved since November, with an uptick across the last five months. Management said there was no volume impact from the price hikes so far.

Management said the market has seen a constant uptick since November, and that new entrants and unorganised players also took price hikes in January and February. Management expects unorganised-player impact to show up over 3-6 months, mainly in low-end products such as primers.
Management said that for the Q4 mix improvement, new products were a large contributor and super premium emulsions performed well. Market share was gained in focused T2 and T3 towns across India.
Dealer incentives are typically higher in April as a stocking month. Management said they are being adjusted with the price increases, in line with normal industry practice.
Auto demand is strong, with OEMs reporting long waiting lists. Demand in infrastructure, appliances and other industrial segments is described as standard and normal.
Management said the company is not chasing market share at any cost, and is focusing on profitable growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 growth came from decorative versus industrial, and what was the volume and mix contribution in decorative?
qa_highlights.answer: Auto was up close to double digits and industrial overall was up slightly higher single digits. Decorative was mid-single digits or lower. Mix improved in both segments, which lifted contribution and profitability.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes will sit in Q1, and how are B2B and industrial price negotiations going?
qa_highlights.answer: Decorative hikes were about 2% in March, then 5-6% each on 10 April, 21 April and 11 May, for a net higher-single-digit increase. Industrial channel prices were revised effective mid-April. OE price increases have been granted in part, with a slight delay in timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is 13-14% margin guidance for FY27 achievable, and does it assume current raw material costs persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the 13-14% band as the endeavour, with an aim for the higher end. It expects raw material prices to stabilise after a temporary panic-driven spike, and believes conditions should improve in the second half.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall about 150 bps as a percentage of sales year on year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a drop in fuel costs and fixed-cost leverage, plus ongoing cost and spend efficiency. It said there was no full-year true-up in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for decorative and industrial demand, and what would happen if crude corrects or stays high?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said auto demand is strong and deco trends are stable through April. If inflation persists, further price increases are possible. If deflation arrives, schemes would be adjusted first, with price cuts only if the softening is sustained. It said a crude price of about USD 100 would be manageable with current hikes.

qa_highlights.question: What share of sales do decorative projects and new businesses represent?
qa_highlights.answer: Decorative projects are about 10%+ of sales. New businesses (waterproofing, construction chemicals, wood finish) are also 10%+, slightly higher than projects.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation from crude and rupee depreciation. Management said price hikes will lag, so near-term margin pressure is possible; the sensitivity to 5-10% input cost increases was not quantified.
Management expects demand to be a wait-and-watch as the West Asia crisis and supply-chain disruption continue. A prolonged crisis could hit consumption through fuel and other costs.
Possible volume impact from price increases in the coming quarters, and inventory-led sales in April distorting secondary numbers.
Competitive intensity from new entrants and a delayed price increase among B2B and industrial customers.
Diwali timing is late this year, which could shift advertising and promotional spend across Q1 and Q2.
Other expenses fell about 150 bps as a percentage of sales YoY, which may not be sustainable if fuel costs normalise.
500165|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on execution and pricing discipline, with management stressing profitable growth and deliberately avoiding market-share chasing. It was cautious and evasive on FY27 demand, auto price quantum, and the timing of raw-material relief, repeatedly calling forecasts "very difficult" and "a crystal guessing" exercise.

500165|2026-06.headline: Kansai Nerolac Q1 FY27 standalone revenue grew 10.2% with PBDIT up 7.7%; management targets 13-14% margins for FY27 despite input cost pressure.
500165|2026-06.overview: Standalone net revenue grew 10.2% YoY, PBDIT 7.7% and PBT 5.1%; consolidated revenue rose 9.8%, PBDIT 8.3% and PBT 5.8%. Decorative value growth was high single digit with volume growth low single digit, as the company deliberately shed low-margin volume. Industrial coatings grew double digit in value, but price increases lagged, with about 5% realised so far at customer level. Management announced a INR601 crore capacity expansion across automotive, powder coating and resin, spread over about 2 to 2.5 years, and kept its margin ambition intact.

financial_highlights.metric: Industrial price hike achieved so far
financial_highlights.change: Still under negotiation; effective ask from 1 April

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Value growth high single digit; volume growth low single digit as premium mix was prioritised over low-margin, high-volume products. Economy grew mid-single digit and super premium grew double digit. Margins were stable YoY despite higher ad spend.

segments.name: Industrial (Automotive, Performance Coatings, Powder)
segments.commentary: Value growth double digit. Automotive and powder coating saw strong growth; liquid performance coatings led by construction equipment, drums and coil coating. Gross contribution fell about 1.3% as price increases lagged cost inflation.

segments.name: Auto Refinish
segments.commentary: Growth was flat. Management cited notable premium PU body shop wins and a transition from solvent-borne to waterborne systems that is on plan.

segments.name: Construction chemicals and premium wood finish
segments.commentary: Construction chemicals grew double digit; premium wood finish grew high single digit.

guidance_outlook: FY27 margin ambition of 13-14% is retained, subject to the geopolitical situation not worsening.
Q2 decorative price increase of about 3% expected to flow through; industrial price increase of another 3-5% expected in Q2.

Q2 will carry high-cost inventory and a seasonally weaker quarter, but management expects to maintain margins versus last year's same quarter, helped by sourcing, value engineering and formula optimisation.
Medium term, aim to reach the higher end of the 14%+ margin range within 2-3 years through premiumisation, industrial growth and fixed-cost leverage.
Expected ROCE on incremental capex is towards 18%, with per-KL capex on new capacity lower than the current programme.
Management expects a slightly better festive season, with Diwali in November giving October more painting days in Q3.
capex_capacity: INR601 crore capex for automotive, powder coating and resin capacity at Sayakha, Bawal and Hosur.
Capacity addition of 66,000 KL per year plus resin capacity of close to 10,000 metric tons per year.
The INR601 crore outlay is spread over about 2 to 2.5 years; normal annual capex is INR150-200 crore.
Part of the spend is front-loaded infrastructure, so future incremental capacity will be cheaper per KL.
Industrial capacity is expected to be full in about 2 years, requiring the addition.
demand_pricing: Competitive intensity in decorative remains high, with new entrants still testing the market; no change in pricing discipline, dealer incentives or scheme intensity versus last year or Q4 exit.
Network expansion: 1,700 dealers added in Q1; network additions targeted at 5-10% a year.
Industrial price hike to date about 5%, with more discussions expected to add in Q2.
Solvent inflation was sharp, but solvent inventory is only about 15 days, which made it hard to hedge.
Some free-product schemes continue in certain markets, not specific to the company's focus towns.
Input cost inflation peaked in June and has since eased slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Is decorative volume growth in line with the market, and is competition easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is not below competitors, but the company is deliberately avoiding low-margin, high-volume products. Competitive intensity remains high and is expected to persist through this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins flat YoY when the market leader expanded margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial price increases lag by 1-2 quarters, so the price-cost gap hit industrial gross contribution by about 1.3%. Ad spend rose in Q1 but was offset by mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value growth split in decorative and industrial?
qa_highlights.answer: Decorative value growth is high single digit and industrial is double digit. Q1 mix is heavier on decorative, and the mix changes each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the capex and what returns are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: INR601 crore over about 2-2.5 years on top of normal capex of INR150-200 crore per year. Management expects ROCE towards 18%, with lower per-KL capex on new capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pricing growth in Q1 and Q2 on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated pricing was about 4-5% in Q1. Q2 adds about 3% in decorative and another 3-5% in industrial.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any backward integration plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the new resin capacity is backward integration for automotive paint, but raw material integration is not on the card. The Kansai Group's global network can supply intermediates as needed.

risks_watch: Geopolitical escalation (West Asia crisis) could raise crude-linked raw material costs and disrupt supply chains.
Rupee depreciation may lift import costs; industrial price negotiations may still be incomplete in Q2.
Decorative volume growth is low single digit, and the company is ceding share in low-margin segments.
Ad and dealer investment is rising, and margin benefit depends on whether premium mix gains come through.
Whether the INR601 crore capacity delivers the targeted ~18% ROCE.
Auto Refinish growth was flat, and the solvent-to-waterborne transition is still in progress.

500171|2026-03.headline: GHCL Q4 FY26 revenue flat YoY at INR 808 crore; EBITDA margin rose to 23.9% as volumes (~11%) offset pricing (~-10%).
500171|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 808 crore, flat YoY and up from INR 773 crore in Q3, with sequential gains attributed to better domestic volumes and realisations. EBITDA was INR 194 crore (23.9% margin) versus INR 175 crore in Q3 and INR 244 crore a year ago; PAT was INR 120 crore. FY26 revenue was INR 3,144 crore and PAT INR 479 crore (15.2% net margin), with INR 415 crore returned via dividend and buyback. Management said global soda ash oversupply persists but import curbs from higher freight and a weaker rupee have firmed domestic prices from March. Bromine and vacuum salt projects are nearing full commissioning in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes rose ~11% while pricing fell ~10% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: How are funding and capital return balanced for the greenfield soda ash project?
qa_highlights.answer: Funding will be a mix of internal accruals and debt, with debt-equity kept below 1. Cash of about INR 1,000 crore is on the balance sheet; management said shareholder payouts are a conscious choice and the distribution pattern may change as the project progresses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and margin from bromine and vacuum salt in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: How much CWIP will be capitalised and what is the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 300 crore of the INR 450 crore CWIP will be capitalised once the bromine and vacuum salt projects are commissioned in Q1; a pipeline project at the existing facility is also in CWIP and is expected to be commissioned this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are roughly neutral to slightly positive given cost increases offset by realisation gains, and declined to forecast beyond the near term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of anti-dumping and safeguard duties?
qa_highlights.answer: Anti-dumping recommendation has gone to the finance ministry with no decision; a fresh safeguard quantitative-restriction application is under investigation and will take some months.

500171|2026-06.headline: GHCL Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose to INR233 crore (29.1% margin), which management says is transient and should not be read as run-rate.
500171|2026-06.overview: Revenue was INR798 crore, down from INR808 crore QoQ and INR823 crore YoY, while EBITDA rose to INR233 crore from INR194 crore QoQ and INR225 crore YoY. Management attributed the margin uplift to better realisation, lower-cost raw material and energy inventory, and cost efficiencies, and repeatedly guided investors to judge margins annually rather than quarterly. PAT including a INR40 crore post-tax exceptional item (ESOS Trust settlement) was INR191 crore; PAT before exceptionals was INR151 crore. Vacuum Salt and Bromine projects are commissioning, while the Greenfield soda ash project remains stalled on land acquisition with no timeline given.

segments.name: Soda ash (core, domestic and export)
segments.commentary: Margin lift attributed to realisation, low-cost inventory and efficiencies; management declined to quantify the realisation increase per tonne. Volumes played a smaller role per management.

segments.name: Vacuum Salt and Bromine (new downstream projects)
segments.commentary: Both plants are mechanically commissioned; commercial production of Vacuum Salt expected in Q2 FY27, Bromine output seasonally low in Q2 with production ramping in Q3-Q4. Management guided to INR150-170 crore revenue at 40-45% EBITDA margin at full utilisation, expected in FY28.

guidance_outlook: Margins expected to moderate from the Q1 level and revert to a normalised trend, driven by softer domestic demand, higher captive industry production and softening realisation; management asked investors to assess margins annually.
Vacuum Salt and Bromine: full utilisation expected in FY28; management said both plants should run at intended capacity during FY27 with gradual, phased scale-up.
FY27 capex guided at roughly INR140-150 crore, mainly for the two downstream projects plus factory infrastructure and regular capex.
Solar glass soda ash demand expected to rise from about 1.5 lakh tonnes to about 3.5 lakh tonnes as new capacity commissions around Jan-Mar 2027.
Dividend payout: last three years about 80-87% of profit distributed via dividend and buyback; management said Board would consider higher payout, with policy around 25%.

Bromine project: pre-commissioning complete; output seasonally lower in monsoon (Q2), production expected Q3-Q4 FY27.
Greenfield soda ash project: delayed primarily by land acquisition; no revised timeline, cost or return profile given. Management will update once land clarity is achieved.
No other pipeline projects beyond the two downstream projects and the Greenfield project, per management.
FY27 capex about INR140-150 crore.
demand_pricing: Global soda ash: supply exceeds demand, prices weak for about two to three years; China demand recovery slower than expected and Chinese inventories high. Management believes Chinese synthetic (Solvay) producers are making cash losses.
Some early Chinese capacity rationalisation and a short-term US plant closure noted; meaningful supply reduction still some way off.
India demand soft in Q1 due to conflict and domestic dynamics; management expects this to persist near term into monsoon, with some rise in imports.

Imports: about 80,000-82,000 tonnes/month in Q1 FY26 (about 20% of demand), fell to about 45,000-46,000 tonnes/month in Q4 FY26, and rose to about 73,000-74,000 tonnes/month recently. July data not yet available. Major sources: US, Turkey, and some China.

Landed cost of imported natural soda ash to India cited at about USD 180-190/tonne; base import duty about 7.5%, no anti-dumping duty. Safeguard quantitative restrictions under government consideration, no outcome yet.

qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed FY28 full utilisation; indicated INR150-160 crore revenue (later cited INR160-170 crore) at about 40-45% EBITDA margin for the two projects combined.

qa_highlights.question: Return on capital for the Greenfield soda ash project at current prices, and reasons for delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current prices should not be treated as sustainable and that long-term numbers given in the past still apply. Delay is due to land acquisition; no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify realisation gains versus cost gains in Q1 margin.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify; said margin gain was a mix of partial price increase, efficiencies and low-cost inventory, and asked analysts to focus on annual margin.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend payout plans given strong cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Payout was about 80-87% over three years via dividend and buyback; Board will consider. Management noted policy around 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Imports and trade protection status?
qa_highlights.answer: Imports rose to about 73,000-74,000 tonnes/month from 45,000-46,000 in Q4 FY26; no ADD in place; safeguard QRs still under government consideration.

Other than the Greenfield projects, we don't have at this point of time, any other projects in pipeline.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Margin hit 29.1% in Q1 FY27 from 23.9% in Q4 FY26, but management says it will moderate and revert to a normalised trend on softer domestic demand, captive production and softening realisation, and asked investors to judge margins annually.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Vacuum Salt is mechanically commissioned with commercial production guided for Q2 FY27, and Bromine pre-commissioning is complete with output ramping in Q3-Q4 FY27; the Greenfield soda ash project has no timeline (land acquisition stalled), so it is excluded from the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Solar glass soda ash demand is expected to rise from about 1.5 lakh to 3.5 lakh tonnes as new capacity commissions around Jan-Mar 2027, but Indian demand is soft into the monsoon and Q1 revenue fell 3% YoY to INR798 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is guided at only INR140-150 crore, mainly for the two downstream projects, and management says there are no other pipeline projects beyond these and the stalled Greenfield project.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided margins down from the 29.1% Q1 level and said Indian demand is soft, with China oversupply keeping prices weak for two to three years.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management explicitly expects margin moderation from 29.1% and softer realisation, and Greenfield soda ash has no timeline (cut from prior guidance).

rows.label: Vacuum Salt and Bromine downstream revenue at full utilisation
rows.why: Management guides INR150-170 crore revenue at 40-45% EBITDA margin at full utilisation, with both plants at intended capacity during FY27 and gradual phased scale-up.

rows.label: Safeguard quantitative restrictions on soda ash imports
rows.why: Imports rose to 73,000-74,000 tonnes/month from 45,000-46,000 in Q4 FY26 (about 20% of demand in Q1 FY26), and safeguard QRs are under government consideration with no outcome yet.

rows.label: Higher dividend payout
rows.why: Net cash surplus is above INR1,000 crore and payout has been 80-87% over three years; the Board will consider a higher payout, with a stated policy around 25%.

tone.note: Management was confident on cost leadership, long-term demand and Vacuum Salt/Bromine timing, but cautious and evasive on near-term realisation, price-versus-cost split, July imports and Greenfield timing; analysts pushed on how much of the 29.1% margin is sustainable.

500180|2026-06.headline: HDFC Bank Q1 FY27 reported profit growth of 5% YoY (9.8% adjusted); CASA ratio at 34%, cost of funds flat QoQ and down ~40-50 bps YoY.
500180|2026-06.overview: Management described a tough four months but said deposit growth was better than historical Q1 trends and market share gains continued. Reported PAT rose 5% YoY, which management said was 9.8% after adjusting for prior-year one-offs (HDB gains, floating and contingent provisions). Management guided that margins will not change quickly, with the non-retail cost of funds and borrowing mix (~11%) as the main levers. The call also covered the FCNR (B) window, ECLGS 5.0 disbursements of about INR 14,000 crore, the upcoming ECL transition on 1 April 2027, and the appointment of a new part-time Chairman, Rajiv Kumar. The MD reappointment and additional whole-time director appointments remain work in progress with no timeline given.

financial_highlights.change: Management says adjusted growth is 9.8% after excluding HDB gains and provisions in the prior year

financial_highlights.value: Flat QoQ (within a couple of bps); down about 40-50 bps YoY

financial_highlights.change: Down from earlier levels; industry around 5-6%
Analyst cited 34%; management target is around 38% (post-merger level)

financial_highlights.value: Close to INR 14,000 crore as of 30 June

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail is 52% of advances. Management said wheels, unsecured and mortgage disbursements grew strongly YoY, while the unsecured book growth remains in single digits. Gold loans and dukandar micro loans are described as growing.

segments.name: MSME / business banking
segments.commentary: Business banking, the largest MSME component, grew 22.3% YoY, and ECLGS 5.0 disbursements reached about INR 14,000 crore by 30 June.

segments.name: Corporate and wholesale
segments.commentary: Corporate and wholesale advances grew about 18%. Management said corporate spreads remain thin and it is being selective.

guidance_outlook: Margins: cost of funds is the main lever with a possible 40-50 bps change, but management said it will not change in a hurry. It does not expect margins to bottom quarter to quarter and sees a better full-year position.
Borrowings: management does not expect the borrowing mix to settle at 8-9%, and expects maturity and growth to bring it down over time.
Profit growth: management expects profit growth at or above balance sheet growth over the longer term, but not on a quarterly basis.
FCNR (B): documentation is complete with counterparty banks; management expects milestones in July-September and aims for a significant share of the system, similar to 2014-15.
ECL: transition effective 1 April 2027. Management expects some increase in credit cost from higher floors (unsecured stage 1 at 1%, stage 2 at 5%) but nothing material.
Customer acquisition: management expects a step-up in acquisition quality and value over the next nine months and in savings account growth over one to three years.
capex_capacity: Branch network is about 9,700 branches, with about 40% under five years old.
Investment in distribution will be slightly muted going forward, while technology spending continues, including AI and security.
Management expects efficiency gains from faster turnaround times over the next two to three years.
Some GenAI lighthouse programmes are expected to go into production during the year.
demand_pricing: Corporate spreads remain very thin amid intense competition; the bank is selective and pursues holistic primary relationships.
Granular deposit rates are reasonably stable, while non-granular (bulk) deposit rates remain elevated.
System liquidity averaged about INR 2.08 trillion in the recent quarter, with a peak of INR 5.5 trillion and a trough of negative INR 0.43 trillion.
Household deposit growth is among the lowest of the deposit categories.
Management says the bank gained market share on a stock and incremental basis in deposits. Its FY26 CASA growth was 9.5-10%, but it still gained share.
Time deposits are a major opportunity, with only 14% of customers holding them.

qa_highlights.question: Have margins bottomed out, and what are the headwinds and tailwinds, including FCNR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost of funds is the main opportunity, with a possible 40-50 bps change that will not happen quickly. It would not call a quarterly bottom but expects a better full year.

qa_highlights.question: Have the branch additions from FY22-23 scaled as expected, and what would restore SA market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-branch deposits are about INR 330 crore vs INR 266 crore in FY23. Management attributed the SA share slowdown to household deposit weakness and to tighter acquisition guardrails against mule accounts over FY24-26, and expects healthier SA growth over one to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the CASA ratio return to 40% and what is the CEO reappointment status?
qa_highlights.answer: The vision is to return to around 38%, the post-merger level, over the medium to long term. Management said the CASA-rate correlation is weaker, with growth to come from unit economics. On reappointment, the NRC and Board are working on it, with an announcement to follow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bond maturity profile and the rate benefit from replacing borrowings with deposits?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 40,000-50,000 crore of borrowings mature over the next couple of years. Replacing them with time deposits gives about 100-125 bps benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-time ECL transition impact and the ongoing credit cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current provisions are adequate for transition. Ongoing credit cost will rise because of higher floors, but the impact is not expected to be material, and contingent provisions cover it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for growth and PCR after the ECL transition?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate and wholesale grew about 18%, business banking 22.3% and mortgage disbursements about 14%. Coverage was 66% headline, and management said PCR is formula-driven and tied to book mix.

risks_watch: CASA ratio at 34% vs a target of about 38%; wholesale deposit share has risen to about 20%.
Non-granular deposit rates remain elevated and liquidity volatility is high.
Retail unsecured book growth remains in single digits, with cards book growth at 2.3%.
ECL transition from 1 April 2027 will raise standard-asset provisions via higher floors.
Leadership: MD reappointment is pending, and additional whole-time directors are expected but not yet appointed.
El Nino and West Asia geopolitical risks; management said El Nino impact will show in Q3 FY27.
500180|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on franchise, growth and the FCNR opportunity, but evasive on specific margin, CASA and leadership timelines, which management repeatedly deferred to the full year or to later announcements.
key_quotes: Advances, as we had envisioned a while ago, I think we are on the verge of pressing the pedal.

So, the thought process that we have as Srini did mention is that we are probably now after putting in our guardrails in terms of what kind of customers need to come in into the institution from an acquisition perspective, I think we are now ready to press the pedal.
The industry is more like a 5% or a 6%, right?
But 9.8% profit growth is still lower than the overall balance sheet growth correct.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Cost of funds is the main lever with a possible 40-50 bps change, flat QoQ and down ~40-50 bps YoY, and borrowings (~11% of total) can be replaced with time deposits for 100-125 bps benefit on INR 40,000-50,000 crore maturing over the next couple of years; management declined to call a quarterly bottom but expects a better full year.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network is about 9,700 with about 40% under five years old and per-branch deposits at about INR 330 crore vs INR 266 crore in FY23; investment in distribution will be slightly muted going forward, so no new capacity is signalled.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Corporate and wholesale advances grew about 18%, business banking 22.3%, mortgage disbursements about 14%, and FCNR (B) milestones are expected in July-September, though unsecured book growth is in single digits and cards book grew only 2.3%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management guided distribution investment to be slightly muted, with spending focused on technology (AI, security) rather than new capacity; utilisation is not discussed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No quantified near-term guidance; management guides only to longer-term profit growth at or above balance sheet growth and says quarterly profit growth will not be at that level, with reported PAT up 5% YoY (9.8% adjusted).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: ECL transition from 1 April 2027 will raise standard-asset provisions via higher floors (unsecured stage 1 at 1%, stage 2 at 5%), and management flagged El Nino impact in Q3 FY27, though it called the ECL credit-cost impact not material.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Some GenAI lighthouse programmes are expected to go into production during the year, but no consumer product or brand launches with numbers were discussed.

rows.label: Borrowing replacement with time deposits
rows.why: About INR 40,000-50,000 crore of borrowings mature over the next couple of years and replacing them with time deposits gives about 100-125 bps benefit, while borrowing mix is ~11% vs industry 5-6%.

rows.label: FCNR (B) window milestones
rows.why: Documentation is complete with counterparty banks and management aims for a significant share of the system, similar to 2014-15.

rows.label: CASA recovery toward ~38%
rows.why: CASA is about 34% vs a ~38% post-merger target, with household deposit growth among the lowest and savings account growth expected to recover over one to three years; management gave no near-term timeline.

tone.note: Management was confident on franchise, MSME/corporate growth and the FCNR opportunity, but deferred on margin bottom, CASA recovery and MD reappointment timelines; analysts pressed on margins, CASA and PCR after the ECL transition.

500180|2026-09.headline: HDFC Bank Q2 FY27: deposits up 18.8% YoY (incl. ~4pp FCNR(B) lift), NIM down to 3.32%, GNPA 1.11%, ROA 1.8%, quarterly PAT Rs 19.5bn.
500180|2026-09.overview: Management reported deposit growth of 18.8% YoY and AUM growth of 15.3% YoY, with retail disbursements above Rs 90,000 crore and ECLGS 5.0 contributing Rs 41,000 crore. Asset quality stayed strong with GNPA at 1.11% and credit cost at 44bps. NIM fell to 3.32% and cost of funds was flat QoQ at about 4.4%, driven by time-deposit mix from FCNR(B) inflows. CFO Srinivasan Vaidyanathan guided that Q2 is the margin bottom, with trajectory upward from Q3. The call also covered the CEO transition: Sashidhar Jagdishan is leaving, Anup Bagchi is incoming as MD and CEO, and Kaizad Bharucha has requested early retirement by end-December.

financial_highlights.change: includes ~4 percentage points lift from special FCNR(B) window
down QoQ; management did not give a YoY figure
highest across banks as of Aug 26, 2026

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail disbursements crossed Rs 90,000 crore in Q2 vs Rs 76,000 crore in Q1. Retail assets ex-agri grew about 11.2% YoY in September 2026, up from 9.1% in June and 7.4% in March.

segments.name: Business banking / MSME
segments.commentary: Business banking grew about 28% YoY, helped by ECLGS 5.0. MSME and mid-market EOP loan growth was 23.5% YoY vs 17-18% in prior quarters.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate book grew about 16.4% YoY and 2.8% QoQ. Management said peers grew a couple of percentage points faster and it will not chase corporate growth at the cost of returns.

segments.name: Agri
segments.commentary: Agri GNPA was stable from June to September 2026. Kharif sowing was down only 1.5-2% despite a monsoon shortfall, and management expects crop output variance of 3-5%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects NIM to be neutral to positive going forward, and said Q2 is the bottom with the trajectory upward from Q3.
About 70% of the loan book is floating; the 25bps repo hike in October should be largely factored in by December, which is a tailwind offset by full-quarter FCNR cost impact.
Mix shift towards retail and MSME is expected to lift yields over the next two quarters as back-book runoff (about 20-30% of retail book per year) reprices.
Management will operate LCR within 110-120% and expects LCR glide path to improve with new CEO's strategy, to be unveiled in about a month.
Draft insurance commission norms: comments due in November 2026; management flagged a high impact on bancassurance commissions, to be offset partly by cost and persistency levers.
capex_capacity: Distribution doubled over the last five years and is expected to mature over the next five years; branch deposit productivity described as best-in-class.
Turnaround time on product delivery down 10-15% and service TAT down 30% in the quarter; customer visits per resource per day up about 50% QoQ.
Savings accounts per branch per day up 19% QoQ; core incremental deposits per branch per day up 2.3x vs Q1.
Daily disbursal run rate for key retail and MSME products up 10-20% QoQ.
Headcount has grown about 10% CAGR over five to six years vs volume growth of 18-19%; management expects headcount to stay flat for now and rise in three to four years.
demand_pricing: Deposits grew about Rs 1.57 trillion in the quarter, of which about Rs 1.3 trillion was time deposits; loan growth was about Rs 1.58 trillion, so sources and uses were matched.
Branch-driven deposits are about 80% of total deposits.

Management says the retail CASA ratio is in the late 40s and stable over a long period; structural pressure on CASA is attributed to household savings behaviour and the HDFC Limited borrowing substitution of about Rs 2.6 lakh crore.
Management said MCLR-linked book is a single-digit percentage of the total book, and cost-to-assets is about 1.73-1.74%.
Management said wholesale and retail ROA are broadly comparable when viewed across the 20-F segment disclosures.

qa_highlights.question: When will the retail deposit share start rising, and what is the impact of agri/drought on the book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the retail mix decline to one-off outflows of large deposits (MSME, government, inherited and FCNR(B) leverage deposits), expects momentum to show later. On agri, Kaizad Bharucha said kharif sowing was down only 1.5-2% and agri GNPA was flat June to September; system book growth is single-digit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM decline in line with peers despite a slower corporate build-up?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said cost of funds was flat at about 4.4% due to the FCNR time-deposit mix and borrowing offsets to AT1 call relief. Kaizad Bharucha said back-book repricing in retail (20-30% annual runoff) should show up over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How will FCNR funds be deployed, and what is the margin outlook for next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FCNR funds are treated as deployed since deposit and loan growth were matched; PSL benefit requires deployment. Margins expected neutral to positive, with October repo hike tailwind offset by full-quarter FCNR cost; management said the trajectory is upward from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 the margin bottom, and will NIM improve from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO confirmed Q2 is at the bottom, with about 70% floating book repricing by December. Kaizad Bharucha said margin improvement will come from calibrated growth in higher-yield retail and MSME products, not from quarterly shifts in corporate exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Has slippage improvement been driven by mix or by better cohort outcomes?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said slippages are improving across most portfolios, not just from mix, and pointed to absolute slippage figures on the investor deck (Page 19).

qa_highlights.question: Can the industry earn ROE above cost of equity with current CASA dynamics?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the bank still has headroom to gain share in its under-penetrated districts (more than 54% of its 765 districts), where its share is 2-3pp below average. CEO said retail CASA is healthy and the structural CASA pressure is an industry issue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for headcount and operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO expects headcount to stay flat for a while, with a mix shift toward frontline roles, and to rise in three to four years. CFO said productivity is still under-realised, with recent productivity growth in double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Why are LCR and CD ratios weak, and what levers will lift liability growth?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said one-off outflows forced reliance on non-retail deposits with lower LCR cover. CFO said the 110-120% LCR band requires space for growth, and CDs are used opportunistically. Liquidity is described as comfortable beyond the LCR figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of draft insurance norms and the PSL shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the commission cut is high and the bank will look at persistency and cost structure to offset it; comments are due in November. PSL is about 50% at aggregate, with a shortfall in small and marginal farmer sub-targets that the bank is buying in the market.

risks_watch: NIM trajectory: Q2 is said to be the bottom, but the timing and size of repricing benefit versus full-quarter FCNR cost remain unquantified.
LCR at 113% vs 110-120% operating band; new CEO's liability strategy and LCR glide path due in about a month.
CASA ratio pressure from structural household savings shifts and large one-off deposit outflows; retail deposit share has declined in recent quarters.
Leadership transition: new MD and CEO Anup Bagchi takes charge; CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan is leaving; Kaizad Bharucha seeks early retirement by end-December 2026.
Draft insurance commission norms could materially reduce bancassurance income; comments are due in November 2026.
PSL shortfall in small and marginal farmer sub-targets; scarce and costly to source.
Agri credit exposed to uneven monsoon; watch agri GNPA and crop output (management expects a 3-5% variance).
500180|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, retail momentum and franchise strength, but cautious and deferential on liabilities, LCR and margins, with several questions deferred to incoming CEO Anup Bagchi. Tone turned emotional during the leadership handover.
key_quotes: The fact of the matter is that we are trying to enable a lot of product and service delivery journeys, which can help in having a one-click experience, including on bundling of products depending on the needs of the customer.

Yes, by all account, Parag, that is what we were alluding to, to say that the rate cycle having already kicked in earlier in October, that is a good tailwind on repricing 70% of the loans which are floating.
So, don't go by a quarter phenomenon, Nitin.

Mind you, whilst you're looking at an LCR, there's another metric called liquidity which may not be visible to you all but the institution's liquidity is extremely comfortable and probably slightly more than comfortable.
Yes, we are seeing better across most of these portfolios on the slippages, so it's not mix.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management said Q2 NIM of 3.32% is the bottom with trajectory upward from Q3, guiding neutral to positive; about 70% of the loan book is floating and the 25bps October repo hike should be largely factored in by December, though full-quarter FCNR cost offsets, and retail back-book repricing of 20-30% per year is expected to lift yields over two quarters.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new branches, plants or capacity additions were disclosed; management instead expects headcount flat for now and productivity gains from existing ~80% branch-driven deposit franchise, with headcount rising only in three to four years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Retail disbursements rose to above Rs 90,000 cr in Q2 from Rs 76,000 cr in Q1 (+18%), deposits grew 18.8% YoY and AUM 15.3% YoY, and retail ex-agri loans grew 11.2% YoY in September vs 7.4% in March, though corporate is growing only 16.4% and management will not chase it.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation not disclosed and no capex plans or land approvals were mentioned; the bank's stated focus is distribution productivity, with the LCR glide path and new CEO strategy (due in about a month) being the main pending strategic decision.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric revenue or profit guidance was given; upside depends on margin trajectory moving from 3.32% in Q2 and on asset quality holding, with GNPA at 1.11% (down 13bps YoY) and credit cost at 44bps.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Draft insurance commission norms (comments due November 2026) could materially cut bancassurance income with management flagging a high impact, and cost of funds is about 4.4% with LCR at 113% vs 110-120% band, so the margin recovery depends on repricing timing that is unquantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New CEO Anup Bagchi's liability and LCR strategy is to be unveiled in about a month, and 1.4 million new credit card issuances (+~19% QoQ) indicate active product push, but no specific new product launch was named.

rows.label: LCR glide path toward 110-120% band under new CEO
rows.why: LCR at 113% sits in the 110-120% operating band with midpoint ~115%, and management expects the glide path to improve under the new CEO's strategy due in about a month.

rows.label: Liability franchise build (relationships and CASA)
rows.why: 1.7 million liability relationships added in Q2 (+25% QoQ), savings accounts per branch per day up 19% QoQ and retail CASA growth 11.2% YoY vs 9% a year ago, but overall CASA growth slowed to 10.8% and retail CASA ratio is in the late 40s with structural pressure.

rows.label: CEO transition to Anup Bagchi
rows.why: Sashidhar Jagdishan is leaving and Anup Bagchi is incoming as MD and CEO, while Kaizad Bharucha has requested early retirement by end-December 2026, so leadership change is firmly under way.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality (GNPA 1.11%, credit cost 44bps), retail momentum and franchise productivity, but cautious and deferential on liabilities, LCR and margins, deferring several questions to incoming CEO Anup Bagchi; analysts pressed on NIM trajectory, CASA decline, LCR weakness

500182|2026-03.headline: Hero MotoCorp Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record ₹12,797 crores (+29% YoY) and EBITDA ₹1,856 crores (+31%), but management flagged a transitory margin hit from commodity inflation.
500182|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with ICE EBITDA margin up 100 bps YoY to 17%. Full-year FY26 revenue was ₹46,830 crores (+15%), EBITDA ₹6,871 crores (+17%) and PAT ₹5,268 crores (+14%). Commodity cost inflation starting March 2026 (₹2,000–2,100 per unit in Q4, offset by an equal revenue-per-unit increase) compressed gross margin by about 100 bps QoQ, and management expects a transitory margin impact in FY27. Management reiterated the 14–16% medium-term margin guidance but declined to commit to it for FY27 given the volatility.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 overall EBITDA margin (after ₹220 crore EV investment)

segments.name: India ICE business
segments.commentary: ICE EBITDA margin 17% in Q4 and FY26, driven by pricing, LEAP savings and operating leverage. Scooters grew 48% YoY; Destini capacity raised 50% and Xoom capacity being doubled.

segments.name: Electric (VIDA)
segments.commentary: EV scooter volumes 2.5x YoY; Q4 EV investment behind the business ₹220 crores. EBITDA loss per unit is declining each quarter per management. PLI now covers 3 products (~60% of portfolio), targeted to reach ~90%, worth ~13% of revenue as benefit.

segments.name: Global business
segments.commentary: Wholesale/dispatches grew 41% YoY, after 40% growth the prior year; present in 52 countries. Latin America is the main traction market; Africa launches planned for FY27.

segments.name: Harley-Davidson premium range
segments.commentary: Harley-Davidson range sales grew 26% YoY; X440T variant delivered 120% YoY growth in its launch quarter.

segments.name: Spare parts (PAM)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales ~₹6,200 crores (~+6%); management estimates ~50% of parts demand is currently served, with a second global parts centre in South India (₹700+ crores) to double parts handling capacity.

guidance_outlook: FY27 industry volume growth expected at high single digits, with scooters growing a couple of points faster than motorcycles; Hero expects to outgrow the industry in both.
Calibrated price increase of ~2% taken in April 2026 (₹700–₹3,500 per product); management says this does not fully cover the high-single-digit BOM cost increase.
Medium-term EBITDA margin guidance of 14–16% reiterated, but no FY27 commitment given; a transitory margin hit expected in the short term.
H1 FY27 growth expected to be stronger than H2 due to base effects; full-year growth momentum expected to continue.
Capex of over ₹1,500 crores committed for FY27, entirely in FY27, mainly for scooter and EV capacity.
Second EV capacity doubling expected before end of FY27; Xoom capacity doubling expected in the current quarter.
capex_capacity: EV capacity: expansion completed within about a month to reach ~50% above Q3 levels (~15,000 to ~25,000 units per month); a further doubling targeted before end of FY27. Management's ambition implies ~100,000 scooters/month.
ICE scooters: Destini capacity up 50%; Xoom capacity being doubled, expected to be complete this quarter.
Over ₹1,500 crores capex committed for FY27 for scooter and EV capacity expansion.
Second global parts centre in South India: over ₹700 crores, roughly doubling parts handling capacity.
Tirupati factory produces both ICE and EV scooters on separate lines within the same plant, sharing infrastructure.
demand_pricing: Dealer inventory around 5 weeks at the end of FY26, down from earlier in the year; EV scooter inventory in single-digit days nationally.
Retail growth outpaced dispatch growth in FY26, so channel stock fell and the company enters FY27 with healthier stock levels.
Post West Asia conflict, demand has not softened in April or the first week of May; the full cost inflation has not yet been passed to consumers.
Q4 average selling price up 3% QoQ across segments.
Management sees scooterization continuing (scooter share of industry up a couple of points each year) and says motorcycle demand is not being lost to scooters.
Retail market share has still declined arithmetically due to mix; management expects a reversal after a few more quarters of outgrowing the market in EV, scooters, exports and premium.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume outlook for motorcycles and scooters, and which models will drive growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry expects high-single-digit growth, with scooters growing a couple of points faster than motorcycles. Hero plans to outgrow the industry in both, with launches across commuter, high-displacement bikes and VIDA, though specifics were withheld.

qa_highlights.question: What is the quantum of the commodity and wage headwind, the price hikes taken, and the margin bridge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify given daily volatility. Price hike is ~2% of sale price, while BOM cost increases are in the high single digits. Offsets include BOM value engineering, LEAP savings, discretionary spend cuts and volume leverage, but these will not fully offset the impact in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: Have EV losses peaked, and how will PLI affect them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is still in the EV build-out phase and that EBITDA loss per unit is falling each quarter. PLI covers 3 products (~60% of portfolio), targeted at ~90%, worth ~13% of revenue; BOM cost reduction is also a lever. EV revenue and loss figures were deferred offline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the recalibrated strategy three months into the CEO role?
qa_highlights.answer: Continue dominance in entry and commuter motorcycles (over 90% share in some ranges; 93% of talukas covered). Prioritise scooters, EVs (including Ather and Euler partnerships and VIDA), other low-emission powertrains such as higher-ethanol-blend vehicles, technology, and exports.

qa_highlights.question: How should exports and global business be viewed for the next 12–24 months, and what are the near-term risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is led by Latin America, with Africa launches planned for FY27 and Bangladesh coverage being extended. Fuel price increases in Bangladesh and Sri Lanka are weighing on demand short term, and freight costs are being passed to retail pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the half-yearly growth pattern for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FY27 growth is expected to be stronger on base effects, with H2 relatively lower. Full-year growth momentum is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin decline of over 100 bps QoQ in Q4 despite price hikes matching commodity costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Material cost inflation of ~₹2,100 per unit vs. ~₹2,000 revenue increase; the margin percentage impact came from unrecovered margin on that cost (about 60% of the decline), plus higher EV BOM costs. Aluminium, steel and rubber led the basket, and plastics rose on crude prices.

risks_watch: Commodity (aluminium, steel, rubber, plastics) and labour cost inflation since March 2026; ~2% price hike is far below the high-single-digit BOM increase, so the Q1 FY27 margin is at risk.
EV losses remain large during the build-out phase; PLI benefit of ~13% of revenue depends on coverage rising from ~60% to ~90%.
Retail market share has declined arithmetically despite category share gains; management says a reversal requires several more quarters of outperformance.
EPR (extended producer responsibility) regulation still evolving; pricing and possible retrospective impact unclear, and industry is working on operationalisation.
Mandatory ABS regulation: no development in recent months.
Fuel price increases and West Asia developments could dampen demand and raise freight costs in export markets such as Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.

500182|2026-06.headline: Hero MotoCorp Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to INR12,999 crore on 23% volume growth, while EBITDA margin fell 120 bps QoQ to 13.3%.

Gross margin contracted 300 bps QoQ on about 4.5% net commodity inflation, but cost deferrals and LEAP savings held EBITDA margin to 13.3%. EV volumes rose 151% YoY, with VIDA at 57,000 units in the quarter and capacity being roughly doubled to about 45,000 a month by year-end. Management expects a marginal uptick in input cost inflation in Q2 and says the 14-16% medium-term EBITDA margin target will not be met in the short term.

segments.name: Parts, accessories and apparel (PAM)
segments.commentary: Parts business grew over 30% YoY in Q1 on volume and price. Management expects PAM growth of about 25% or more in FY27, with July trend similar.

Capex: GPC 2.0 parts capacity investment of INR750 crore announced, more than doubling parts handling capacity.

Retail finance penetration rose to about 65% last month; credit easing is helping demand.
Competition: Hero holds about 86% share of the 100cc segment; management says the category is not at risk from electrification near term.

qa_highlights.question: Demand on the ground for new EV and scooter models, and inventory levels given capacity expansion?

qa_highlights.question: How have price hikes been accepted and is 100cc demand stabilising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 100cc share is about 86% and the segment grew from 32% to about 33%. Retail finance penetration reached about 65% last month.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin return to 14-16% this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of returning to the 14-16% range in the medium term, not the short term. The focus is absolute EBITDA growth through volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV revenue share and EV profitability path?

qa_highlights.question: Why was the HF Deluxe price cut taken and what is the premium pipeline?

500183|2026-03.headline: HFCL Q4 FY26 revenue rose to Rs 1,824 crore and EBITDA margin to 18.47%, with a Rs 10,159 crore hyperscaler OFC contract and Rs 21,200 crore order book.
500183|2026-03.overview: HFCL reported its highest-ever quarterly and annual performance, with FY26 consolidated revenue of Rs 4,949 crore (up from Rs 4,065 crore) and PAT of Rs 329 crore (up from Rs 173 crore). Q4 revenue of Rs 1,824 crore grew sharply from Rs 1,211 crore in Q3 and Rs 801 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA margin at 18.47% versus 20.11% in Q3. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 20-25% and a 3-4% blended EBITDA margin expansion, driven by price realisations, EPC loss reduction and product mix, while announcing a Rs 580 crore preform plant, defence and aerospace acquisition, and a strategic restructuring committee. Management declined to give firm numeric guidance on several items.

Electronic fuze is undergoing upgrades for DRDO re-evaluation; BMP upgraded sample due June 26, 2026.
