Board approved a greenfield preform plant of 300 MT per annum at Rs 580 crore; location decision expected within the month. Management says in-house preform is at least 30% cheaper than buying.
Board approved an additional Rs 215 crore for data-centre connectivity (miniature multi-fibre and super high-density MPO assemblies); Rs 100 crore to be spent in FY27 and Rs 115 crore in FY28.

Ammunition complex in Andhra Pradesh groundbroken on 15 May 2026. IBR cable capacity above 14 million fibre km across 12 machines, expanding monthly; 14,000-fibre cable under development, 2-3 months away.
demand_pricing: Management expects demand to outstrip capacity for at least 5 years, citing AI, hyperscale data centres and telecom expansion; contracts being signed for up to 10 years.

Indicative export pricing per fibre km: $22-28 for data-centre fibre, telcos lower; overall range $18-28, with prices up significantly in the last six months. Spot prices are 5-15% above 5-year contract rates.

Long-term contracts have annual price reset clauses; management says large raw-material moves would be passed through. Preform cost increases from the start of the next calendar year are expected to be offset by customer price increases and value-added connectivity products.
Management cites 35% US duty on Chinese fibre and US customer reluctance to buy from China as competitive positives.

Order book of about Rs 26,665 crore: about Rs 16,000 crore optical fibre cable; about Rs 22,000 crore expected to execute within 5 years; contract durations range from 3 months to 4 years (cable), with BharatNet at 3 years and O&M at 7 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance conservative given the strong run-rate and tailwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers to under-promise: guidance moved from 20% to 40%+ growth, and it is 'always good to be conservative'. It did not give a formal annualised figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 23% EBITDA margin sustainable, and is there seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin comes from average contracts executed through the year, with no seasonality and no single high-margin order. It said the margin can be protected barring geopolitical shocks.

qa_highlights.question: Will preform cost increases hit margins from calendar 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Some preform contracts run into FY28. Management expects only a few percentage points of pressure, offset by customer price pass-through and higher-margin data-centre connectivity products; overall margin profile is expected to remain the same.

qa_highlights.question: What is the defence order book and what is the acquisition's effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence order book is about Rs 300 crore excluding the acquisition, about Rs 2,300 crore including it. Acquisition to complete within calendar 2026; export defence orders about Rs 2,200 crore. BMP-2 modernisation shortlisted, Army trials started 20 May with about 1.5 months to complete.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data-centre connectivity revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 100 crore in Q1 FY27 and about Rs 800 crore for FY27, with orders of about Rs 850 crore in hand. Capacity to rise 5x, with deliveries of cable starting this month and connectivity about a month later.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Army (EPC) contract restore profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the Army contract signing in mid-Q2 FY27, after which EPC revenue would rise and losses fall significantly. It did not commit to breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: How will debt and working capital evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-equity is about 0.3 and is expected to stay in that range, funded partly by internal accruals. Segment assets rose about Rs 400 crore net of segment liabilities (about Rs 600 crore liability increase).

risks_watch: Geopolitical disruption (e.g., Suez Canal closure) and government contract timing (Army contract signing and trials) could delay revenue and margin recovery.
Preform price increases from the next calendar year, with some older contracts priced below current market, could compress margins if pass-through is incomplete.
Restructuring committee with E&Y evaluating group simplification; outcome and impact on the defence subsidiary (HASPL) structure remain undisclosed.
Management said it is reviewing further fibre capacity expansion, indicating possible additional capex beyond the current plan.
Export concentration (about 60% of revenue) and US hyperscaler dependence; a shift in Chinese competitive pricing could affect realisations.
Q1 included about Rs 300 crore of Q4 unbilled revenue billed in the quarter; watch whether Q2 revenue holds near Rs 1,900 crore.

FY26 saw commissioning of 70,000 MT speciality carbon black capacity at Mahistikry (total 130,000 MT speciality, 250,000 MT overall) and de-bottlenecking of coal-tar pitch distillation to 600,000 MTPA. The company commissioned its first anode material plant (200 MTPA) on 23 April 2026 and reiterated LFP cathode Phase 1 (40,000 MTPA, INR 1,125 crores) timelines. Management guided to top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27 without giving numerical guidance, and reaffirmed a FY28 PAT target of INR 1,100+ crores.

Management targets INR3,000 Crores top line in 4-5 years and EBITDA breakeven in FY27, with a PCR plant by FY28. Distribution spans 49 distributors and over 1,000 dealers.

segments.name: Coal tar and carbon black (core)
segments.commentary: Holds over 65% domestic coal tar pitch share with 600,000 MTPA distillation capacity, and carbon black capacity is 250,000 MT including 130,000 MT speciality grades. Anthraquinone and carbazole capacity of 5,300 MTPA is due in two phases: 2,600 MTPA in Q2 FY27 and 2,700 MTPA in Q2 FY28.

segments.name: New energy materials
segments.commentary: A 200 MTPA anode plant at Mahistikry was commissioned in April 2026, with anode capex of about INR120 Crores to date. LFP cathode initial 2,000 MTPA is due in Q3 FY27 as Phase 1 of a 40,000 MTPA expansion (about INR1,125 Crores) that is due in FY28.

segments.name: Other (mining)
segments.commentary: No mining operations in Q1 as environmental and licensing approvals are awaited, with timing of 3 to 6 months cited. Segment EBIT fell to about INR1 Crore from about INR25 Crores.

guidance_outlook: Management maintained the INR1,100 Crores PAT target for FY28 and said nothing had changed, but gave no FY27 guidance.

Total capex announced is about INR2,000 Crores (LFP INR1,125 Crores, new announcements INR368 Crores, Birla Tyres INR500 Crores this year), with about INR1,000 Crores expected in each of FY27 and FY28.
Management said free cash flow will fund the capex with no incremental debt.
Management expects top-line growth from both volume and value next quarter.
Birla Tyres is expected to reach EBITDA breakeven and be cash positive in FY27.
Management said 40,000 MTPA LFP would yield about INR3,000 Crores top line at current prices, and 200,000 MTPA LFP would need about INR4,800 Crores capex.
capex_capacity: CNT: 200 MTPA plant, about INR70 Crores capex, commissioning targeted for Q4 FY27.
Super speciality carbon black: conversion of 6,000 MTPA existing capacity for INR170 Crores, with capacity start in FY28.
Anode: 200 MTPA plant commissioned April 2026, with no further anode capex announced; natural graphite and silicon carbon capacity planned.
LFP cathode: 2,000 MTPA initial capacity in Q3 FY27, Phase 1 of 40,000 MTPA in FY28, long-term target 200,000 MTPA in 5-6 years.
Anthraquinone and carbazole: 2,600 MTPA in Q2 FY27 and 2,700 MTPA in Q2 FY28; India's first commercial plant of its kind.
IBC plans a 7 GW battery facility in India, with operations expected by Q4 FY27, which will use Himadri raw material.
demand_pricing: Management cited global Li-ion battery demand rising from about 1.6 TWh in 2025 to about 6.8 TWh by 2035, with about 70% of growth in LFP.
CNT global market is about 30,000 MT; super speciality carbon black market is about 300,000 MT; speciality is over 1 million MT.
LFP pricing is said to be at parity with China, and management claims a cost advantage from India-based production and non-China raw materials.
Anode qualification: sample B supplied to customers; sample process takes 1.5-2 years, and management says approvals will be in place by commissioning.
Management says the West Asia situation did not materially affect supply; raw-material cost pass-through lifted finished-product prices.
Other expenses fell to about INR148 Crores excluding forex loss, from about INR172 Crores in Q4, driven by lower outbound freight and cost optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other-segment EBIT drop from INR25 Crores to about INR1 Crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mining did not operate this quarter while licences are awaited, so the mining profit did not recur; higher Birla Tyres revenue offset top-line effects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential of the new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: 40,000 MTPA LFP at today's prices gives about INR3,000 Crores top line; anthraquinone/carbazole about INR250-300 Crores; super speciality carbon black about 3x capex (about INR500 Crores); CNT less than INR100 Crores; 200 MTPA anode about INR120-130 Crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FX loss a recurring issue and what drove other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no hedging policy change and the FX loss was a one-off for the currency volatility; other income came from FD and mutual fund deployment, borrowings in CPs and mark-to-market gains on IBC, Sicona and Birla Tyres NCDs, and may swing 30-40% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Will the LFP and new capex be debt-funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said free cash flow will cover the capex with no incremental debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company increase its stake in IBC?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management called IBC a strategic investment and said it is not looking to raise its stake further.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margins on the new CNT and SSCB products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose margins, saying they are significantly higher than existing speciality carbon black.

qa_highlights.question: Is the LFP cathode economics viable against Chinese pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Excel-based cost comparisons are not reliable, cited cost advantages, and declined to disclose lithium carbonate sourcing.

risks_watch: Mining remains idle pending environmental clearance, which could take 3-6 months, with segment EBIT near zero.
Execution on LFP (2,000 MTPA in Q3 FY27, 40,000 MTPA in FY28) and anode commercialisation depends on customer approvals, which management said take 1.5-2 years.
Birla Tyres is not yet EBITDA positive, and its breakeven is targeted within FY27 after the TBB to OTR conversion.
Analysts questioned whether LFP pricing at China parity leaves a positive gross spread; management declined to disclose input costs.
Other income is volatile (30-40% QoQ swing) and the FX loss needs to be watched next quarter.

500184|2026-09.headline: Himadri Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose to INR 1,543 crore (+44% YoY) and PAT to INR 240 crore (+28%), while per-tonne EBITDA eased sequentially to about INR 21,000.
500184|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA was INR 308 crore (+27% YoY) and PAT INR 240 crore (+28% YoY); consolidated revenue was INR 1,691 crore and PAT INR 231 crore (+31%). Management attributed the sequential per-tonne EBITDA dip (from about INR 22,700-22,800 to about INR 21,000) to a raw-material pass-through lag, higher freight costs, and a higher export share (33% vs 26%). New carbon nanotube, LFP and anthraquinone/carbazole capacities are on schedule, with commissioning timelines reiterated, and the proposed merger of the Birla Tyres business into Himadri was announced. Mining is expected to restart this quarter after environmental clearance was received.

segments.name: Carbon black (speciality / core)
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation was 88% in Q2 FY27, with guidance of 88-95%; volume grew about 14,000 tonnes QoQ per management, after the 70,000 TPA commissioning. All new materials (CNT, super speciality carbon black) will be reported within the carbon segment.

segments.name: Birla Tyres (under Dalmia Bharat Refractories, trading for Himadri)
segments.commentary: Q2 trading revenue was about INR 140 crore at about INR 1 crore EBITDA (trading margin). Management says it is on track for breakeven and reiterated its top-line guidance; numbers will be added to Himadri on consolidation after the proposed merger.

segments.name: Mining (sand, West Bengal)
segments.commentary: No revenue in the quarter; it carried negative EBITDA because environmental clearance was pending. Clearance was received in October 2026, with operations to start in Q3 FY27 and a longer-term revenue potential of about INR 500 crore.

guidance_outlook: Maintains target of INR 1,100 crore+ PAT by FY28, to be supported by core business and new capacity commissioning.
Per-tonne EBITDA is guided to a range of about INR 20,000-24,000 going forward; management says it is confident of staying above INR 20,000 on a sustainable basis.

Capex spend of about INR 250 crore in Q2 FY27; total FY27 spend guided at INR 800-900 crore. Management said the roughly INR 1,500 crore programme over two years will be funded from internal accruals, not debt.
Most new capacity is expected to show full impact from FY29, per the analyst's read of management's reply.
Management expects working capital to normalise over the next two quarters and operating cash flow to turn positive on an annual basis.
Anthraquinone/carbazole (5,300 TPA) is now targeted for full commissioning together in Q4 FY27 instead of two phases, with about 9 months of full operation next year.
capex_capacity: Carbon nanotube (CNT): 200 TPA facility targeted for commissioning in Q4 FY27; production start stated as Q4 FY27.
LFP cathode active material: initial 2,000 TPA trial production in Q3 FY27, with samples to OEMs in Q4 FY27; next phase of 40,000 TPA deferred to end-FY28 so that qualifications are in place first.
Super speciality carbon black: planned 6,000 TPA targeted for Q4 FY28.
Anthraquinone and carbazole: 5,300 TPA total, with both phases commissioned together by Q4 FY27 to avoid a three-month shutdown.

Silicon carbon anode: engineering under way; formal capex and timeline to be announced later. Synthetic graphite anode plant has commenced operation, and samples have been shared with domestic and global customers.
demand_pricing: Volume grew 11% YoY in Q2 FY27 (1,46,000 tonnes cited on the call); revenue rose 58% YoY, driven by volume and higher raw-material-linked selling prices.
Export share rose to 33% of sales from 26% a year earlier; higher container freight rates, linked to the geopolitical situation, weighed on margins.
Gross margin fell about 500 bps YoY on a standalone basis, which management attributed to a raw-material pass-through lag, with 9-10 days of raw-material inventory held.
Management says realisations move with raw-material prices and should not be extrapolated; sequential per-tonne EBITDA is expected to vary between quarters.
Battery materials: management expects pricing to be in line with Chinese suppliers; anode products are at sample stage, with no realisation guidance given.
Carbon black demand described as robust; ENERGEX grades received approval for high-voltage cable and battery applications and have started commercial orders.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the sharp gross margin moderation, and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are stable and that per-tonne EBITDA was about INR 21,000 vs INR 17,900 YoY and INR 22,700-22,800 QoQ. The dip was attributed to pricing pass-through timing, higher freight and a higher export share, all described as temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Are the new LFP, anthraquinone and carbazole products margin-accretive from start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed yes, saying they would add to incremental margin from the start. For LFP, margin guidance was deferred until commercial discussions begin after the 2,000 TPA plant.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex has been spent, and what is planned for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 250 crore spent in Q2 FY27, with INR 800-900 crore expected in FY27. Commercial dates for projects fall before FY28, so most capacity impact is expected from FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and revenue potential of mining?
qa_highlights.answer: Environmental clearance was received in October 2026 and operations are to start in the current quarter. The longer-term top-line potential is about INR 500 crore, depending on volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did carbon black EBITDA per tonne fall vs the peer, and is there a sweet spot from coal tar?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw-material prices are correlated, so there is no pricing edge. The advantage is clean, self-produced feedstock for speciality carbon black, and the decline was attributed to freight and export mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding plan for the remaining capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the programme of about INR 1,500 crore over two years will be funded entirely through internal accruals. Working-capital debt was used earlier, and it is expected to come down over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commissioning and approval timeline for the LFP and anode products?
qa_highlights.answer: The LFP 2,000 TPA plant is to start trial production in Q3 FY27, with samples in Q4 and customer qualification taking 12-18 months. The 40,000 TPA expansion was deferred to end-FY28 so that approvals are in place first.

500186|2026-03.headline: HOEC's Q4 FY26 call: FY26 profit and revenue turned negative after HPCL crude sale reversal; management targets 10,000-11,000 boepd by mid-2027.
500186|2026-03.overview: Management, led by new MD & CEO Baroruchi Mishra with CFO Allen Joseph Andrade, reported FY26 revenue, EBITDA and PAT all negative, mainly due to reversal of a crude sale to HPCL (revenue would otherwise have been INR559 crores). Standalone PAT was INR288 crores versus INR344 crores a year earlier, and lifting cost was $28.4/bbl versus $28.6/bbl. Production is about 15 thousand boe/d with a further 4-7 thousand boe/d locked in by lack of infrastructure, and management targets 10,000-11,000 boe/d by mid-2027, 22,000 by 2028 and 32,000 by 2029. Most of the Q&A focused on HPCL crude settlement, the Dirok gas pipeline connection, B-80 workovers, and funding, where management gave few hard numbers and deferred FY27 debt and EBITDA guidance to next quarter.

segments.name: B-80 (Offshore, Mumbai High area)
segments.commentary: 2P reserves of 26 MMboe with about 1 MMboe produced to date; 2 subsea wells need workover, deferred from last quarter for lack of funds, and 3 new wells planned post-monsoon. Target 4,000-5,000 bbl/d plus 7.5-10 MMscfd gas from the program.

segments.name: PY-1 (Offshore/onshore gas, Krishna-Godavari-type gas processing link)
segments.commentary: Historically 45-50 MMscfd at start-up, now largely shut in. Plan is 2 development wells plus coiled tubing intervention, adding about 12-15 MMscfd by mid-2027, with one exploration well in a 4-well campaign.

segments.name: Dirok (Assam, gas)
segments.commentary: Currently producing 0.3-0.4 MMscm/d (about 15 MMscfd gross) versus 1.1-1.2 MMscm/d potential, constrained by DNPL pipeline (1 MMscmd flowing vs 2.5 MMscmd capacity). Potential 45 MMscfd, 70 MMscfd with 3 more wells once the DFL-Duliajan 24-inch, 175 km line is built in 2-3 years. Condensate 200-250 bbl/d now, 700-900 bbl/d at 45 MMscfd (gross).

segments.name: Kharsang (oil and gas)
segments.commentary: 9 wells drilled and production doubled; 9 more wells planned in the coming campaign. Gross production about 700+ bbl/d; significant gas found.

segments.name: B-15 (new award)
segments.commentary: 15 MMboe in-place reserves; FDP concept selection under way, FEED to follow, then FID. 3-5 wells possible; target 4,000-5,000 bbl/d and about 10 MMscfd, timing not committed.

segments.name: Cambay (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Focus on workovers, production enhancement and secondary recovery for low-cost incremental output.

segments.name: Greater Dirok / Umatara
segments.commentary: Exploration and appraisal upside; North Dirok exploration well (4,000-5,000 m) could add 10-15 MMscfd if successful.

guidance_outlook: Production target of 10,000-11,000 boe/d by June 2027, with management saying it is confident of above 8,000 boe/d at minimum.
Production ramp to 22,000 boe/d in 2028 and 32,000 boe/d in 2029.
Reserves: 1P about 40 MMboe, 2P about 60 MMboe, 3P about 109 MMboe; management values 1P-2P at USD3-5 billion depending on oil price.
FY27 and FY28 debt and EBITDA outlook deferred to next quarter's call.
HPCL crude proceeds expected over 2-3 months; Dirok pipeline connection hoped for in 1-2 months but no firm date given.
capex_capacity: Drilling plan: 20 wells in various stages of preparation; Kharsang 9 more wells, PY-1 2 development wells plus 1 exploration well, B-80 3 wells plus 2 workovers, Dirok 3 wells (all contingent on pipeline, funds and rig availability).
Two rigs planned, one each for PY-1/Kharsang and B-80; target to complete B-80 three wells and two workovers by May 2027, when rig tow insurance expires.
Dirok evacuation depends on NRL connection of 55 km DNPL replacement section (laid, not yet tied in; NRL shutdown possibly needed) and on the DFL-Duliajan 24-inch, 175 km line in 2-3 years.
Funding: internal accruals plus bank facilities under discussion; equity raise not ruled out but not committed.
demand_pricing: HPCL crude sale cancelled and resold to third-party buyers on a Brent-minus-X basis; first few weeks at a firm price agreed under the COSA, then Brent-linked.
Physical lifting of about 300-700 tonnes per week from HPCL refinery; full proceeds expected over 2-3 months.
Buyers accepted crude on an as-is, where-is basis after third-party sample analysis; management says B-80 samples show zero contamination from wells.
Last crude cargo sold at USD109/bbl (per management).

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 net production target, split by field?
qa_highlights.answer: 10,000-11,000 boe/d by June 2027; PY-1 about 12-15 MMscfd, B-80 4,000-5,000 bbl/d, Assam 70 MMscfd target, Kharsang doubling again with 9 wells. Management stressed that timing depends on drilling, financing and rigs.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 debt and EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Not given; management deferred this to the next quarter to avoid giving a number that could change.

qa_highlights.question: When will the HPCL revenue be realised?
qa_highlights.answer: Crude is being lifted weekly by trucks and sold to third parties over 2-3 months; the COSA conciliation with HPCL is still pending and expected to conclude within a few months.

qa_highlights.question: When will Dirok gas flow via the national grid / DNPL, and at what rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects flow in 1-2 months but cannot give a firm date. Current 0.3-0.4 MMscmd could rise to 0.8-0.9 MMscmd, against 1.1-1.2 potential, depending on pipeline allocation.

qa_highlights.question: How will B-15 and B-80 ramp, and what is the pace?
qa_highlights.answer: B-80: 3 wells and 2 workovers targeted by May 2027. B-15: 3-5 wells possible, FDP still at concept stage, with a 4,000-5,000 bbl/d target; tie-back to the B-80 facility or a separate export line is under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise equity, and what are the costs of production?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity not ruled out but no decision; focus is internal accruals and bank debt. Company-wide opex is about $28/boe; Assam is among the lowest, B-80 is high.

risks_watch: HPCL conciliation outcome and whether HPCL reimbursement or compensation is required; inventory is carried at 31 March valuation against lower current prices, and the Q4 PAT benefited from the HPCL derecognition.
Funding gap: INR260 crores tied up in crude receivables delayed B-80 workovers; capex depends on bank facilities not yet sanctioned.
Dirok production depends on DNPL pipeline tie-in and NRL and other shippers' allocation; the gas pipeline is owned by Assam Gas Company.
Rig availability, monsoon timing and subsea Christmas-tree condition for B-80 workovers; possible slippage of 3-6 months.
Earlier timeline commitments (connectivity, pipeline) have slipped repeatedly, per analyst feedback; management's targets are conditional.

500186|2026-06.headline: HOEC Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose to INR117.5 crore from negative INR194 crore, but PBT before exceptionals fell to INR12.5 crore on B-80 output loss and HPCL crude resale.
500186|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR117.5 crore versus a negative INR194 crore in Q4, which reflected reversal of the HPCL crude sale (INR259 crore). Kharsang output rose from about 12,300 to 17,400 BOE and crude realisation rose to about $95.5/bbl from $70.8/bbl. Standalone PBT before exceptionals fell to INR12.5 crore from INR30.4 crore, due to inventory-related cost offsets. B-80 output was hit by higher water cut, and the HPCL-stored crude is being resold to third parties at a slower pace than expected, with a further mark-to-market loss expected. Management is relying on debt to fund the B-80 workover and three-well programme.

segments.name: Kharsang (Arunachal, crude and gas)
segments.commentary: Output rose from about 12,300 to 17,400 BOE; nine-well programme doubled production year on year and workovers on 23 idle wells are underway (5-6 done). Gas is virgin and unsold for lack of pipeline.

segments.name: B-80 (offshore Mumbai)
segments.commentary: Production reduced by higher water cut from one producing well; compressor configuration changed and in test mode. Crude stored at HPCL Chembur is being sold via tankers; about 15% sold so far. Gas realisation around $15-16/MMBTU on exchange, average $16.5/MMBTU.

segments.name: Dirok (Assam, onshore)
segments.commentary: Operated with ~27% stake; currently producing only 50-70% of well capability due to evacuation limits. DNPL line capacity degraded to ~1-1.5 MMSCMD versus 2.5 MMSCMD design; average gas realisation about $12.5/MMBTU.

segments.name: PY-1 (East Coast, gas)
segments.commentary: Three wells suffered serious production loss; rig-less intervention contracted and funded from own books. Two new wells deferred and contingent on take-or-pay gas agreement with GAIL or IOCL. Realisation about $10-12/MMBTU.

segments.name: Cambay, Gujarat (Asjol, Balol, Palej)
segments.commentary: Palej debottlenecking delivered 5-6% production increase last quarter; management guides 20-30% increase over time. Sucker rod pumps ordered and a new exploration block pending final approval.

segments.name: B-15 (new block)
segments.commentary: Recoverable reserves 16 MMBOE; FDP under preparation with three to four concepts, including tie-back to ONGC platform. Drilling planned in FY28.

guidance_outlook: Dirok: DNPL capacity restoration via hot-tap expected by December 2026, targeted at 2.5 MMSCMD from 1-1.5 MMSCMD; locked-in volumes 0.5-0.7 MMSCMD gross.
B-80: two workovers in Oct-Nov 2026; three new wells (1,000-1,500 bbl/well per simulation, range 700-1,400 or 8,900-13,000 bbl total cited) by June 2027; workovers 500-800 bbl/well.
B-80 crude inventory at HPCL Chembur expected to clear by end-October/early November 2026; sales from FSO in October in 120,000-150,000 bbl tranches.
Management expects further mark-to-market loss of about 7-10% on the remaining HPCL crude; explicitly not guidance.
Kharsang: pipeline route survey tender closing; 24 km pipeline to Bordumsa; 14-18 months to complete; second phase of nine wells pending rig award and tubulars in 1-2 months.
Cash flows expected to fund B-15 by around Nov-Dec 2027; B-80 programme to be funded by debt being raised from market.
capex_capacity: B-80: rig award expected this month; workovers mobilised by October; three wells planned with production from June 2027; jacket and production deck installation required.
PY-1: two new wells deferred until a firm take-or-pay gas agreement; 15-20 MMSCFD potential cited from two wells.
Capex budget increased versus Q4 presentation, which management attributed to a contingency for rig scarcity; facility to be drawn down on need.
Kharsang pipeline: 24 km, 6-8 months for right of way plus 6-8 months for laying; target completion around December 2027 in best case.
Dirok: hot-tap works by Assam Gas Company Ltd and NRL bypass of about 150-200 m of pipeline inside NRL premises.
demand_pricing: Standalone crude/condensate realisation about $95.5/bbl vs $70.8/bbl previous quarter; benefited from favourable Brent.
Gas realisation blended $12/MMBTU vs $9.8 previous quarter; B-80 about $16.5/MMBTU, Dirok about $12.5/MMBTU.
Crude from B-80 resold to third parties; HPCL offtake continues by tanker with gantries added; realisation losses of INR4-6 crore incurred so far.
NRL can act as reseller and sell gas on exchange; management says gas can be sold within about three days once a credible grid path exists.
Oil sales to Digboi Refinery and mainly IOCL from Kharsang.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Northeast grid connectivity for Dirok be complete, and when would Dirok production ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets December 2026 for completion, driven by hot-tap works by Assam Gas Company Ltd and a ~100-200 m NRL bypass; hot-tap lead time quoted at 16-20 weeks, with NRL shutdown no longer needed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of B-80 crude stored at HPCL and when will it clear?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales to third parties via tankers are slower than expected; management hopes the entire HPCL Chembur inventory clears by end-October/early November 2026. About 15% sold so far with INR4-6 crore realisation losses.

qa_highlights.question: How much mark-to-market loss remains on the HPCL crude, and what is standalone EBITDA ex-adjustments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pegged the further loss at 7-10%, explicitly not guidance. The CFO declined to quantify EBITDA excluding inventory and profit petroleum adjustments and promised to revert.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B-80 rig campaign timeline and is the workover plan credible given past failures?
qa_highlights.answer: Two workovers (10-20 days each) after rig mobilisation by October; three wells (30-40 days each) with jacket and production deck, production by June 2027. Management cited rig intervention as higher-confidence than past chemical treatments; 2P reserves of 26 MMboe with 1.5-2 MMboe produced.

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex budget rise versus Q4, and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Increase is a contingency for rig scarcity, not cost inflation; facility drawn on need. Management is raising debt from market and banks, with some funding from internal accruals post-workovers.

qa_highlights.question: Will gas realisation be disclosed by asset, and what are the asset-level prices?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO agreed to resume asset-wise realisation disclosure in the next presentation. B-80 gas about $16.5/MMBTU (exchange $15-16), Dirok about $12.5, PY-1 about $10-12; blended $12.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt is outstanding and when will cash flows fund capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Gearing 0.04; bank loan INR20 crore. Management says internal cash flows fund B-15 by around November-December 2027; B-80 programme relies on debt.

qa_highlights.question: Why not pass HPCL crude price loss to HPCL under the agreement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the agreement reversed the sale and HPCL is cooperative; a conciliation process under a High Court-appointed Chief Justice is pending, and HOEC will not renege on the agreed offtake.

Kharsang gas monetisation: 24 km pipeline needs forest clearances; 14-18 months timeline; virgin gas unsold meanwhile. Protest reported in Tamil Nadu over drilling in allocated area, to be managed with state government.
Track quarterly: B-80 water cut and workover results, actual B-80 production versus 8,900-13,000 bbl target, and asset-wise realisation disclosure promised for next presentation.
key_quotes: So our take is that by December, this should be completed.
But that said, we are producing only 50%-70% of the capability from the existing well stock because of the lack of evacuation route.
So for delivering B-80 program, we will have to rely on debt.
But please don't take it as a guidance.

500188|2026-03.headline: Hindustan Zinc posted record Q4 FY26 revenue of INR13,544 crores and EBITDA of INR7,747 crores (57% margin), with zinc cost of production at $903/t.
500188|2026-03.overview: Hindustan Zinc delivered record quarterly and full-year results in Q4 FY26, with mined metal of 315 KT and refined metal of 282 KT, and full-year mined metal crossing 1.1 million tons. Zinc cost of production hit a post-underground-transition low of $903/t in Q4 and $959/t for FY26, both below guidance. Net cash closed at INR5,594 crores versus net debt of INR1,169 crores a year earlier. Management guided FY27 cost of production to $975–1,000/t and capex of $500–600 million, and reiterated plans for a 250 KTPA smelter at Debari and a larger 1 million ton smelter cluster in Rajasthan.

segments.name: Zinc (mined and refined)
segments.commentary: Q4 mined metal 315 KT and refined metal 282 KT, both records; FY26 mined metal 1.1 Mt and refined metal 1,048 KT. Growth came from higher ore output, better mined grades and debottlenecking at Chanderiya and Dariba.

segments.name: Silver and precious metals
segments.commentary: Precious metals contributed 45.0% of profitability. The company sold 12,000 t of lead concentrate in Q4 (about 37 t silver-equivalent including Q3 actions); Q4 concentrate sales were about INR500 crores revenue and INR330 crores EBITDA.

segments.name: Other operating income / ancillary business
segments.commentary: Other operating income rose from INR783 crores to INR1,362 crores in Q4 (per analyst). Sulfuric acid is about INR1,400 crores and scrap/residue about INR1,000 crores of FY26 cost credits; the gross-up from the third-party residue arrangement is about INR600 crores on each side (income and expense).

guidance_outlook: FY27 mined metal guidance 1,150 KTPA ±10 KT; refined metal 1,100 KTPA ±10 KT; refined silver 680 t ±10 t.
FY27 zinc cost of production excl. royalty guided at $975–1,000/t; management said it should come in below that range if conditions improve.
FY27 capex planned at $500–600 million for announced growth projects.
Hot Acid Leaching commissioning now expected in 2Q FY27; fertilizer project on track for commissioning in early 2Q FY27.
Renewable energy share expected at 30–35% in FY27, targeting 70% round-the-clock by FY28.
Silver output could reach 800+ t once the 250 KTPA smelter, LGLC circuit and tailings recycling are in place; management did not give a timeline beyond FY27.
Board announcement on the 1 million ton smelter expected around July after feasibility; conceptual plan and layout by end of Q1 FY27.
Brand, licence and strategic services fee contract with Vedanta is valid until 2030; FY26 fee about INR1,300 crores, FY27 similar at about INR1,100 crores (as stated by management).
capex_capacity: Debari 250 KTPA integrated zinc smelter: site mobilization complete, detailed engineering largely finalised; capex about $2,600/t, double-digit IRR per management.
Plan for a single-location 1 million ton smelter in Rajasthan (about 600–700 KTPA design, co-located with the 250 KTPA unit); smelter order expected in about one month and mill order by June.
Rampura Agucha tailings reprocessing plant: site work started, engineering complete.
Fertilizer plant (0.5 Mt): phosphoric acid plant expected in about three months, DAP plant around January 2027.
Renewable energy consumption 18% in FY26, with a targeted 30–35% in FY27.
Three critical mineral blocks secured (potash, tungsten, rare earths); work underway. Ore reserves 468.6 Mt with 25+ years of mine life.
demand_pricing: Q4 average zinc price $3,241/t (peak $3,487/t); lead averaged $1,931/t (peak $2,040/t). Silver has normalised from peak levels but management sees a structural deficit.

Hedging: Q1 FY27 zinc 20 KT at about $3,100/t and silver 25 t at about $57/oz; full FY27 zinc 71 KT at about $3,225/t and silver 59 t at about $60/oz. No hedges placed after Q3 FY26; policy is 10–20% of volume, within 12 months.
Q4 hedging delta versus market was INR1,100 crores; FY26 total delta INR1,500 crores.
Sulfuric acid prices are linked to the sulfur index and reset quarterly; management sees acid prices as an offset to input-cost moves.
VAP is about 24% of FY26 sales and commands only $50–60/t premium over SHG zinc, per management.
Coal: FY26 mix about 53% domestic, 18% renewable, 30% imported; Q4 domestic coal 64%. Management cited a roughly 40% price gap in favour of domestic coal.

qa_highlights.question: Hedge quantities for Q1 and full FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 hedges: zinc 20 KT at $3,100/t and silver 25 t at $57/oz. Full FY27: zinc 71 KT at $3,225/t and silver 59 t at $60/oz.

qa_highlights.question: Will silver output rise, and how does it reconcile with the FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guidance is 680 t, which with the 37 t MIC sale implies about 664 t already. Output could exceed 700 t if zinc falls to $2,800–3,000/t and silver stays near $60/oz, and management expects 800+ t once the new smelter and LGLC circuit are commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 35% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: The third-party residue arrangement is grossed up in both other operating income and other expenses at about INR600 crores a year each; management expects this to rise to INR1,200–1,500 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 zinc cost outlook versus FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 benefited from a 7.9% mining grade versus a 7.5% FY average; Q1 grades are historically 7.3–7.4%. Management said the guidance includes a provision for input-cost inflation (diesel, propane, chemicals, explosives), with an additional gas-shortage impact of about $11/t in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend plan and brand fee?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board declared a first interim FY27 dividend of INR11/share (about INR4,300 crores); FY26 total was INR10/share. Management confirmed a minimum 30% payout policy regardless of capex.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth be debt-funded and how much cash does the company hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will primarily be funded from earnings, with debt used only if cheaper than internal funds. Gross cash is about INR14,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What was the silver hedging approach and why did it stop after Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company hedged 10% of FY26 volume (20% in FY25) and stopped after Q3 because the EBITDA margin is already high and silver is a by-product. It will not hedge beyond 12 months.

risks_watch: Silver production guidance of 680 t is flat versus the FY26 run rate; the path to 700 t+ depends on zinc prices falling, which management framed as a trade-off.
Hedge book is about 10% of volume for FY27; prices above $3,225/t zinc and $60/oz silver leave the company exposed to unhedged upside, but the FY26 hedging delta was INR1,500 crores.
Input-cost inflation from diesel, propane, chemicals and explosives under the Middle East conflict; FY27 cost guidance includes a partial provision.
The 1 million ton smelter cluster has no Board approval yet; the Board decision is expected around July after feasibility. Capex and premium costs are not yet disclosed.
Renewal of mining leases expiring in 2030; management relies on first right of refusal but says a premium may be payable.
Ramp-up of the fertilizer plant (phosphoric acid in about 3 months, DAP around January 2027) and Hot Acid Leaching (commissioning 2Q FY27) have commissioning risk.
Fatal incident at Zawar mines on 25 January 2026 involving a business partner employee; corrective measures are underway.

500188|2026-06.headline: Hindustan Zinc Q1 FY27 record EBITDA of INR8,074 crores (59% margin) and net profit of INR5,469 crores, with zinc COP at USD851/t.
500188|2026-06.overview: Hindustan Zinc posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue (INR13,747 crores, up 77% YoY), EBITDA (INR8,074 crores, up 109% YoY) and net profit (INR5,469 crores, up 145% YoY) in Q1 FY27. Mine metal output of 268,000 t was the highest first quarter in five years, and refined metal rose 4% YoY to 260,000 t. Zinc cost of production excluding royalty fell to USD851/t, the lowest since the underground transition, helped by by-product realisation and better grades. The company sold 10 kt of lead concentrate (about 9 t silver and 6 kt lead metal) and ended with net cash of INR5,572 crores. Leadership is changing: Arun Misra hands over to Amarendu Prakash as CEO from 1 August 2026, and Amit Gupta is the new CFO.

segments.name: Zinc (mined and refined)
segments.commentary: Mined metal output of 268,000 t and refined output of 260,000 t, with zinc COP at USD851/t excluding royalty. Management guides to 1.1 million t for FY27 and expects Q4 at 280–290 kt.

segments.name: Silver
segments.commentary: Silver output of 149 t, with 10–15 t estimated locked in WIP; excluding concentrate sales, about 158 t was extracted. Silver contributed about 46% of profitability; the company needs about 175 t per quarter to reach its 680 t target.

segments.name: Lead and lead concentrate
segments.commentary: Sold 10 kt of inferior-grade concentrate stock from the RD mine ramp-up, realising INR315 crores. Company policy remains not to sell concentrate, and remaining old inventory will be used in smelters first.

segments.name: Sulphuric acid and fertiliser
segments.commentary: Sulphuric acid prices are reported up about 200% YoY. The phosphoric acid portion of the fertiliser plant at Chanderiya is due in Q2, and the full fertiliser plant is due in Q1 FY28 pending environmental clearance; about INR500 crores spent to date.

guidance_outlook: FY27 mined metal guidance of 1.1 million t reiterated; management sees no need to revise it and expects no further smelter shutdowns.
Zinc COP guided at USD975–1,000/t, with Q1 beating it through by-product realisation.
FY27 growth capex guided at USD500–600 million; INR800 crores spent in Q1.
Net cash position expected to be maintained at FY27 exit, based on volume and price assumptions.
Dividend policy unchanged: minimum 30% of profit plus 5% of reserves.
250 KTPA Debari integrated smelter and about 650 kt total metal capacity including mines: estimated INR24,000–25,000 crores, 36-month build, Board approval expected by Q3 FY27.
Tailings reprocessing plant construction started; about 30–35 kt zinc expected after about 24 months, with a 6–8 month ramp-up.
capex_capacity: Debari 250 KTPA integrated zinc smelter: mine development started to match mining capacity; capex estimate at a straight-line rate of about INR12,000 crores per 250 kt, pending tender outcome in about one month.
Tailings reprocessing plant: construction started and site mobilisation for infrastructure completed; 30–35 kt zinc output expected.
Hot acid leaching plant at Dariba and phosphoric acid/fertiliser plant at Chanderiya: on track for Q2 completion (phosphoric acid portion); full fertiliser plant by Q1 FY28.
Rampura Agucha and Chanderiya/Dariba debottlenecking, plus the 160,000 t pa roaster, supported output in Q1.
REE/Yttrium block in Gundlupet, Karnataka: exploration 2–3 years; production expected around FY2031–32.
demand_pricing: Zinc averaged USD3,466/t in Q1 with a high of USD3,625/t; lead averaged USD1,954/t.
Silver moderated to USD73/troy oz from the prior quarter's higher levels.
Hedge book: 48 kt zinc open at USD3,162/t and 34 t silver at USD63/oz; no hedging done in FY27 so far.
Coal mix: linkage coal share fell to 36% from 54% a year earlier and 64% in Q4; imported coal costs were higher, lifting power and fuel costs QoQ.
Revenue was supported by stronger dollar, higher by-product realisation and concentrate sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why did power and fuel costs rise QoQ despite lower metal output and higher RE share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower linkage coal materialisation due to mine conditions, plus costlier imported coal, partly offset by higher RE power use.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise FY27 production guidance and is 1.1 Mt achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident in 1.1 Mt: 260 kt in Q1 implies about 1,040 kt on a straight-line basis, and Q4 typically reaches 280–290 kt. No revision is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What net cash position is expected at FY27 exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to remain a net cash company at FY27 exit, based on its volume and price assumptions.

qa_highlights.question: Clarify the SEBI observations on related party transactions and the corrective steps taken.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said omnibus approvals have value limits; an alarm now triggers at 80% of the approved value, prompting Board and Audit Committee re-approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and capex for the 600+ kt smelter project?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex for the 650 kt including mines is estimated at INR24,000–25,000 crores; tendering is ongoing, a 36-month build is expected after Board approval, and Board approval is targeted by Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Silver guidance and what is needed per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says silver grades should improve in Q2–Q4 with better PPM ore, with the strongest output in Q4; the 680 t target is seen as achievable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fertiliser/phosphoric acid timeline and economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the phosphoric acid portion is due in Q2; the fertiliser plant is pending environmental clearance and is expected by Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Any update on government stake sale and dividend policy after the Vedanta demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Government stake sale is for the government to comment on. Dividend policy is unchanged: minimum 30% of profit plus 5% of reserves, with INR11/share already paid.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the USD50/t QoQ COP reduction and by-product effect?
qa_highlights.answer: COP is in line with the USD975–1,000/t guidance; the additional benefit comes from by-product realisation, which is credited through the COP, and no separate quantification was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the royalty ratio to revenue at a multi-quarter low because of sulphuric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphuric acid carries no royalty. Mineral royalty is set as a percentage of the LME price, so it is not a fixed percentage of revenue.

risks_watch: Silver output must average about 175 t per quarter for the rest of FY27 to reach 680 t; Q1 was 149 t with 10–15 t in WIP.
Input cost pressure from energy prices and coal mix (linkage coal 36% vs 54% a year earlier) could erode the COP gain.
Hedge losses of INR200 crores in Q1 and an open 48 kt zinc position at USD3,162/t may weigh on realisations if prices rise.
Leadership transition: new CEO takes over on 1 August 2026, and a new CFO has been appointed.
Related-party transaction governance: SEBI observations and new omnibus-limit alarm controls.
Fertiliser plant delayed by pending environmental clearance; full plant now expected in Q1 FY28.
Government stake sale speculation; no update from management.
500188|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on operations and cash generation, with the record quarter presented as a base for FY27 guidance. Management was measured on growth project timelines and noncommittal on the government stake sale and fertiliser unit economics.
key_quotes: we reported highest ever EBITDA of INR8,074 crores, resulting into a record net profit of INR5,469 crores, making a new milestone for the company.
we achieved the lowest quarterly zinc cost of production, excluding royalty, since underground transition to USD851 per ton, reflecting a decline of 16% year-on-year.
We still don't sell concentrate. We still have the same policy that we don't sell concentrate.

500188|2026-09.headline: Hindustan Zinc Q2 FY27 EBITDA hit a record INR9,285 crore (+108% YoY) at 62% margin, with net profit of INR6,412 crore; zinc COP guidance cut to $825-850/t.
500188|2026-09.overview: Hindustan Zinc reported record Q2 FY27 results, with revenue from operations of INR15,093 crore (+77% YoY), EBITDA of INR9,285 crore and net profit of INR6,412 crore (+142% YoY). Mined metal output rose 5% YoY to a record Q2 and refined metal rose 7%, while zinc COP fell to $703/t (down 29%). Management revised full-year zinc COP guidance down sharply to $825-850/t from $975-1,000/t, partly offset by about $50/t of geopolitical cost escalation. Net cash closed at INR11,268 crore after free cash flow before growth capex of INR6,389 crore in the quarter.

segments.name: Zinc (mined and refined)
segments.commentary: Mined metal production up 5% YoY to a record Q2 output; refined metal up 7% YoY. Zinc COP $703/t in Q2 and $776/t for H1, both excluding royalty.

segments.name: Silver
segments.commentary: Saleable silver production rose 20% YoY to 173 tonnes in Q2 and is about 45% of H1 profitability. H1 silver output of 321 tonnes plus 20 tonnes sold in concentrate gives about 340 tonnes; FY27 guidance is 680 tonnes.

segments.name: Lead concentrate / by-products
segments.commentary: Sold 10 KT of lead concentrate in Q2 (about 6,000 t lead, 10 t silver) for revenue of about INR300 crore and profit of INR155 crore. Sulfuric acid by-product benefited COP but is auctioned and not guided.

guidance_outlook: Zinc COP guidance for FY27 revised to $825-850/t from $975-1,000/t; management expects Q3 broadly in line with Q2 levels.
FY27 silver production guidance maintained at 680 tonnes; H2 delivery expected to meet it.
FY28 silver output of 730-750 tonnes is a hope, subject to debottlenecking projects; to be finalised towards year-end.
FY27 capex outlook about INR5,000 crore, with higher spend in Q3 and Q4 as expansion progresses.
Management reiterated a 2x growth ambition and expects the 250 KTPA integrated zinc expansion and the 10 MTPA tailings reprocessing plant to stay on track.
capex_capacity: Q2 capex of about INR1,200 crore sustaining and about INR700 crore growth.
250 KTPA integrated zinc expansion: engineering and procurement almost complete; mine development underway.
10 MTPA tailings reprocessing plant progressing as per plan.
Four critical mineral blocks are mainly exploration; exploration to finish in Q3 FY29. Gundlupet REE and Yttrium block is under a executed mining lease, with resource indications in 2-3 years.
Q2 ore grade 7.6%. Domestic coal share of usage 32% in Q2.
demand_pricing: Management sees a 2026 refined zinc deficit of about 180 KT (demand 13.87 Mt vs supply 13.69 Mt), with the market tight over the next decade.
Silver expected to be in deficit for a sixth consecutive year in 2026, with a shortfall of about 1.44 thousand tonnes.
Zinc hedges: 40 KT for Q3 at INR3,476 and 36 KT for Q4 at INR3,698; silver hedge of 8 t for Q3 at $68/oz.
Sulfuric acid by-product prices were strong; FY26 sulfuric acid revenue was about INR1,000-1,200 crore per management, with no FY27 guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the hedge quantities and rates by quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: 40 KT zinc hedged for Q3 at INR3,476 and 36 KT for Q4 at INR3,698; 8 t silver hedged for Q3 at $68/oz.

qa_highlights.question: Can COP go below the revised $825-850/t guidance given sulfuric acid strength?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulfuric acid gave a positive surprise, but geopolitical cost escalation added about $50/t; Q3 is expected broadly in the same range and FY guidance is kept at $825-850/t.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic coal share and Q2 capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic coal was 32% of usage. Q2 capex was about INR1,200 crore sustaining and about INR700 crore growth; FY capex about INR5,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Update on new critical mineral blocks?
qa_highlights.answer: Three of four are exploration blocks, with exploration finishing in Q3 FY29. The Gundlupet REE and Yttrium block has an executed mining lease, with resource and business plan indications in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Lead concentrate revenue, margin and plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 sale of 10 KT gave about INR300 crore revenue and INR155 crore profit. No specific concentrate sales plan; sales depend on concentrate availability relative to smelter capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Silver guidance and FY28 outlook; sulfuric acid contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 silver guidance of 680 t is maintained (H1 about 340 t including concentrate). FY28 730-750 t is a hope pending debottlenecking. Management declined to guide on sulfuric acid, saying it is auctioned at market prices; FY26 contribution was about INR1,000-1,200 crore.

risks_watch: Zinc and silver prices and hedge roll-off: Q3-Q4 zinc hedges are at INR3,476-3,698, versus spot levels not disclosed.
Sulfuric acid by-product pricing, which lowers COP and is not guided.
Geopolitical energy and input cost escalation (about $50/t impact on COP).
Execution of the 250 KTPA expansion and tailings plant, with capex stepping up in H2.
FY28 silver target of 730-750 t depends on debottlenecking projects still in pipeline.

Our EBITDA stands at INR9,285 crores, and the net profit is at a record level of INR6,412 crores.

500201|2026-03.headline: India Glycols FY26 net revenue rose 11.8% to INR4,211 crores, with EBITDA up 24.5% to INR654 crores and margin at 15.5%.
500201|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed strong operating performance: gross revenue INR9,827 crores (+8.7%), net revenue INR4,211 crores (+11.8%), EBITDA INR654 crores (+24.5%) and PAT INR293 crores (+26.8%). Q4 net revenue rose 13.1% to INR976 crores with EBITDA of INR167 crores (+13.3%). Bio-Fuels and Chemicals drove margin gains, while Chemicals sales fell and Ennature Biopharma margins stayed under pressure. Management said the Middle East war had a mixed but slightly positive effect via ethanol competitiveness, though export business to the Middle East was on hold. Debt was reduced by prepaying about INR804 crores in the quarter, including INR467 crores from a November 2025 equity issue.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 net revenue INR1,203 crores (-10.4%), EBIT INR141 crores (+12.5%), EBIT margin 11.7%. Q4 net revenue INR301 crores (+18.8%), EBIT INR37 crores (+37.4%), margin 12.2%.

segments.name: Potable Spirits (IMFL + IMIL)
segments.commentary: FY26 top-line INR1,331 crores (+14.4%), EBIT INR285 crores (+11.1%). Q4 top-line INR306 crores (+7.9%), EBIT INR68 crores, margin 22.1%. IMFL is about 31% of segment revenue per management, with Amrut about 5-6%.

segments.name: Bio-Fuels
segments.commentary: FY26 top-line INR1,470 crores (+40.9%), EBIT INR115 crores (+103.3%), margin 7.8%. Q4 top-line INR305 crores (+11.6%), EBIT INR30 crores (+90.0%), margin 9.9%.

segments.name: Ennature Biopharma
segments.commentary: FY26 top-line broadly flat with a nominal decline, margins under pressure. Q4 top-line grew 23.2%, but EBIT was only INR3 crores.

guidance_outlook: Management expects improved profitability and top-line growth in Chemicals for FY27, and expects performance chemicals to more than double in FY27 (hoped, not projected).

Interest cost expected to stay around INR25 crores per quarter; FY27 scheduled term-loan repayment about INR268 crores (liquor INR168 crores, chemicals INR100 crores), plus further prepayments of high-cost debt.
Management expects the JV share of profit to improve drastically from FY26 INR46.42 crores as 49% JV is consolidated into the Chemicals business.
Plan to sell a further 24% JV equity in FY28-29 per agreement, proceeds to repay term loans and make the Chemical business debt-free by FY28-29 (hoped).

Management aims for high double-digit IMFL growth via geographic expansion (Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan) and new brands; no formal margin guidance for Potable Spirits beyond Q4's 22% EBIT margin.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR830 crores in FY26, with about INR600 crores spent in the last six months; about INR400 crores capitalised from grain distilleries at Gorakhpur and Kashipur.
Plant shutdown from 17 March to 2 April 2026 for catalyst change, reducing production and some sales; EO supply to the Clariant JV stopped for 15-20 days.
Ethanol capacity now slightly exceeds in-house Bio-Fuels consumption; grain-based (dual feedstock) ethanol flexibility retained.
Ennature Biopharma investing in manufacturing capability and branded nutraceutical clinical studies, with some studies to complete in FY27.
demand_pricing: Potable Spirits: IMIL is about 75% of segment volume but about 52% of UP value; IMFL is about 16% of UP volume and 34% of value. IMFL volumes grew 30% in the year, with UP IMFL top-line growth of 25% last year.
IMIL growth was 21% in Uttarakhand and 11% in UP; Amazing Vodka reached a 21% market share in Uttarakhand vs 18% last year.
Bacardi bottling revenue sits in miscellaneous income, with filling charges estimated at 2-3% of Potable revenue.
Grain prices fell from about INR24/kg mid-2025 to about INR21-22/kg in Q4 FY26; DDGS prices improved.

Imported ethanol prices rose sharply on freight and other factors, while domestic prices were stable or slightly lower; the Middle East war raised crude and constrained MEG and ethanol availability, which improved ethanol-based product competitiveness.
Oilfield chemical exports to the Middle East, largely for New Park, are on hold due to the war; propylene oxide prices and availability were also affected.
Chemicals sales declined due to Chinese low-cost glycol ethers, weaker gases sales after argon price spikes, and lower EO sales to the JV when EO was uncompetitive versus Reliance.

qa_highlights.question: How was business disturbed by the plant shutdown, and what is the Potable Spirits split and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Shutdown for catalyst change (about every 1.5 years) affected EO supply to the Clariant JV and some specialty products, not MEG. IMFL is about 25% and IMIL about 75% of Potable Spirits (Raju Vaziraney, although later data cite IMFL at 31% of revenue). Management did not guide to a margin number, saying Q4's 22% EBIT margin is not assured to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BSPC/Chemicals top-line decline, and are plants at optimal level?
qa_highlights.answer: Glycol ethers lost share to cheaper Chinese and propylene/butylene-based material, gases declined on high argon prices in the prior year, and EO sales to the JV fell. Management expects improved profitability and top-line growth in FY27 and said the large EO price delta with Reliance has narrowed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was JV profit INR13 crores in Q4 and what is the JV monetisation plan?
qa_highlights.answer: JV profit improved on mix and imported traded materials from Clariant; FY26 share of profit was INR46.42 crores vs INR46.40 crores. The company plans to sell a further 24% equity in FY28-29 per the agreement to repay term loans and make Chemicals debt-free.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost run-rate and FY27 debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR804 crores prepaid in Q4 (INR467 crores from promoter equity, rest internal cash). Interest cost to stay around INR25 crores per quarter. FY27 scheduled repayment is INR268 crores (liquor INR168 crores, chemicals INR100 crores), plus prepayments.

qa_highlights.question: Silver sale during shutdown and grain availability?
qa_highlights.answer: Silver sold for INR98 crores against purchase cost of INR51 crores; no profit was booked because catalyst consumption was not yet provided. Grain stocks are adequate and prices are stable; grain was about 73% of ethanol feedstock in FY26 with maize about 46%.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the Ennature Biopharma outlook and nicotine pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is shifting nicotine to value-added long-term customers and diversifying into branded nutraceuticals with clinical studies. EBITDA improvement may not show in FY27 despite customer acquisition.

risks_watch: Middle East war: export business for oilfield chemicals on hold; propylene oxide availability and prices affected; demand softening in some areas.
Ennature Biopharma margins under pressure from nicotine price competition and the Thiocolchicoside price cycle; EBIT was only INR3 crores in Q4.
Bio-Fuels profitability depends on government blending policy (20% achieved; talk of higher blending and flex-fuel) and feedstock prices.
Pending NCLT-approved demerger of a division; order expected around 21 May 2026 with a possible June 2026 order.
Chemicals volume recovery depends on JV EO offtake, which was affected by the shutdown and the Reliance price gap.

Cautious on Chemicals and Ennature, where management said results will improve but gave few numbers.

rows.why: Management hopes performance chemicals more than double in FY27 (hoped, not projected) and expects Chemicals profitability to improve, but gave no numbers.

rows.why: Middle East war has put oilfield chemical exports (largely New Park) on hold, Chinese glycol ethers have taken share, and Ennature EBIT was only INR3 crores in Q4, so Chemicals and Ennature could miss.

rows.why: Management is diversifying Ennature into branded nutraceuticals with clinical studies finishing in FY27 and is adding new IMFL brands, but no specific launch dates were named.

rows.why: Management plans to sell a further 24% JV equity in FY28-29 per agreement and hopes Chemicals is debt-free then, with FY27 scheduled term-loan repayment of INR268 crores and interest steady at about INR25 crores per quarter after INR804 crores of Q4 prepayments.

rows.why: Order expected around 21 May 2026 with a possible June 2026 order, a near-term event in the window.

500201|2026-06.headline: India Glycols Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 9% to INR1,130 crore and record EBITDA of INR170 crore (+13%), with PAT up 32%.
500201|2026-06.overview: Consolidated net revenue reached INR1,130 crore (+9% YoY) and EBITDA INR170 crore (+13%), with EBITDA margin at 15.0% versus 14.3%. Management said PAT rose 32% and finance costs fell to INR25 crore from INR45 crore on debt reduction. The NCLT sanctioned the demerger scheme on 17 July 2026 and the company is now reporting under three entities. Management attributed part of the quarter's gains to the war-driven crude spike, which made bio-based EO competitive with Reliance's product again. Sequential EBITDA comparison is distorted by Q4 FY26 including about INR39 crore of Clariant dividend income.

segments.name: IGL Spirits (potable spirits)
segments.commentary: Spirits net revenue INR371 crore with EBITDA margin 22.9% (+207 bps). IMFL revenue grew 26% to 1.4 million cases (+55% volume); non-IMFL revenue was flat at INR279 crore with volume of 7.5 million cases (+6%).

segments.name: Bio-Fuel (ethanol)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR323 crore (+7%), EBIT INR27 crore (+19%), EBIT margin 8.4%; management also cited EBITDA margin of 10.8% (+250 bps).

segments.name: Chemicals (India Glycols)
segments.commentary: Chemicals revenue INR332 crore (+25%) at 11.4% EBITDA margin; small gases INR13 crore at 23.1% margin. Glycols value up 83%; green solvents and glycol ethers volume +6%, value +13%, gross margin close to 50%. Performance chemicals grew 40%, below target.

segments.name: Ennature Bio Pharma
segments.commentary: Best-ever quarter at INR83 crore revenue (per call) / INR90 crore net revenue under new structure, up 53-65%; EBITDA up ~188% per the prepared remarks. Nicotine sales doubled QoQ on European customer conversions; thiocolchicoside up 26% QoQ.

segments.name: Clariant JV (Kashipur)
segments.commentary: JV net revenue up 21% QoQ with EBITDA up in high double digits QoQ; JV profit cited at about INR21 crore versus about INR19 crore a year earlier.

guidance_outlook: IGL Spirits: EBITDA above INR500 crore for FY27 (INR120 crore already delivered in Q1); IMFL volume to roughly double versus FY26 (FY26 IMFL volume 3.4 million cases).
Spirits: management expects healthy double-digit growth in FY28 and aims to be debt-free from FY28; target EBITDA above INR1,000 crore in four to five years.

Chemicals aspiration (explicitly not a projection): EBITDA about INR400 crore and revenue about INR2,500 crore in four to five years; FY27 revenue aspiration INR150 crore-plus for the new performance chemicals business; margin targeted to rise toward 30% gross margin.
Ennature aspiration: EBITDA INR130-150 crore over the next four to five years.
Capex in chemicals expected to be small: INR5-20 crore incremental in the current year; no INR400-500 crore plant expected for at least two years.
capex_capacity: Chemicals capex plans: incremental INR5-10 crore, possibly up to INR15-20 crore this year, via modular expansion; new plant additions to date about INR50-60 crore.
Ennature started nicotine crude processing at its Kashipur plant, adding capacity.
Spirits: captive ENA capacity described as sufficient, supporting cost advantage in UP, Uttarakhand and Delhi.

Demerger: after effectiveness, Spirits, Bio-Fuel and Bio Pharma undertakings transfer to dedicated resulting companies; IGL Spirits will hold potable spirits, Bio-Fuel and biopolymers; Ennature retains nutraceuticals and APIs. Effective date not yet communicated.
demand_pricing: Spirits: management says the industry grew at a 4-5% CAGR over the last one to two years; IMFL growth attributed to launches in deluxe whisky, semi-premium vodka and white spirits. Prestige & Above volume ~0.5 million cases, roughly double last year.
Mix: revenue lagged volume in Spirits because of state mix (Delhi growth lower margin) and brand mix (mass premium grew faster).

Chemicals: ethylene oxide became similar to or slightly cheaper than Reliance's EO for a few months, increasing specialty chemicals off-take. Oil and gas and Middle East exports were hit by propylene oxide shortages and freight volatility (westbound freight up 5-20x).
Ennature: raw material availability and pricing volatile and a challenge in Q2 as well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the guidance for potable spirits for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 EBITDA above INR500 crore, with INR120 crore delivered in Q1; volume to double versus last year, with healthy double-digit growth expected next year.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for the NSU (chemicals) business and how will it scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex limited to about INR5-20 crore this year; cumulative new plant investment about INR50-60 crore. Aspiration of INR150 crore-plus revenue this year and INR600-700 crore in 4-5 years, with margins improving over time.

qa_highlights.question: Are JV profits sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a fair assumption; JV PAT about INR19 crore a year ago versus INR21 crore now, with the improvement linked to narrower EO cost disadvantage.

qa_highlights.question: Prestige & Above volumes and IMFL revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: P&A about 0.5 million cases, roughly double last year. FY26 IMFL volume was 3.4 million cases; FY26 IMFL revenue was not disclosed and will be sent later.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volumes grow faster than revenue in Spirits?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to state mix (Delhi growth lower margin) and brand mix (mass premium growing faster); revenue growth expected to exceed volume growth as premium mix rises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IMFL margin versus country liquor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margins in deluxe and semi-premium whisky are almost the same as in P&A and did not give separate EBITDA margins.

Ennature raw material availability and pricing volatile; described as a challenge in Q2 as well.

500207|2026-09.headline: Indo Rama Synthetics Q2 FY27 PAT rose 201.8% YoY to INR74.1 crore on EBITDA margin of 8.8%, with a fresh INR200 crore specialty expansion approved.
500207|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 total income rose 10% YoY to INR1,344 crore and EBITDA rose 46.4% to INR117.7 crore, with margin up 220 bps to 8.8%. H1 total income fell 9.7% to INR2,284 crore on supply chain issues, yet H1 EBITDA rose 24.9% to INR225.7 crore at a 9.9% margin. Net debt fell to about INR852 crore from INR1,113 crore at FY26-end, and H1 operating cash flow was INR328.5 crore. The board approved about INR200 crore of specialty filament and fibre capacity at Butibori, with commercial operations expected in calendar 2027.

financial_highlights.change: +46.4% YoY vs INR80.4 crore; margin +220 bps from 6.6%
+201.8% YoY vs INR24.6 crore; margin from 2%
+24.9% YoY vs INR180.7 crore; margin +280 bps from 7.1%

segments.name: Polyester staple fibre (PSF) and filament yarn (POY/FDY)
segments.commentary: Management said these lines are running at about 100% utilisation. Yarn realisations were cited at roughly INR125-160 per kg across grades.

segments.name: PET chips / bottle-grade PET resin
segments.commentary: Chip plant is running at about 60% of capacity, which management cited as the main reason volumes are lower. Bottle-grade PET resin capacity is 2.28 lakh tonnes per annum.

segments.name: Draw textured yarn (DTY), via subsidiary
segments.commentary: Installed DTY capacity is 1.75 lakh tonnes per annum after 39 machines were added in 2023. Management said DTY's share of the mix stays at 30-35% and textured yarn margins are not currently above average.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 margins to hold near the 9.9% H1 level and sees a path to double-digit EBITDA margins in FY28-29.

FY27 volume expected at about 4 lakh tonnes versus about 4.75 lakh tonnes in FY26, with a return to 4.75 lakh tonnes-plus in FY28; management said FY27 turnover should still exceed FY26's roughly INR5,000 crore.

Specialty expansion (INR200 crore) expected to add about 15% to top line and 20% to EBITDA, with payback under 2 years, subject to execution. Management said about INR100 crore of incremental EBITDA would come in FY28-29.
FY27 EBITDA expected to exceed INR400 crore, implying a strong H2 versus H1's INR225.7 crore.
capex_capacity: Current capacity is 6.72 lakh tonnes per annum: 2.31 lakh tonnes PSF, 1.7 lakh tonnes DTY and 2.28 lakh tonnes bottle-grade PET resin. Polyester chip capacity was debottlenecked to 1,920 tonnes per day in February 2023.
Capacity utilisation was 58% in FY23 and 55% in FY24, then 58% in FY25 and 68% in FY26.

INR200 crore fresh investment at Butibori, across the company and wholly owned subsidiary Indorama Ventures Yarns Private Limited. It adds extruders to existing lines for specialty filament at about 115-120 tonnes per day (converting semi-dull to specialty) and another filament line of about 70 tonnes per day. A closed fibre line is being restarted for specialty and hollow fibre.
Commercial operations expected in calendar 2027, funded by term loans and internal accruals.
Growth capex was about INR20 crore in FY25 and about INR5 crore in FY26, after INR628 crore invested across FY23-FY24.
demand_pricing: Pricing is variable, linked to market prices; management said raw material costs rose 40-50% and that increases were passed through with a lag of about a week to 10 days. Raw material inventory is held for roughly 15 days to 1.5 months.
Management said spreads were about 9.9% EBITDA in H1 and expects this to be maintained for the next two quarters.

Export share fell to about 6% in the last six months from 20-25% earlier, as domestic demand was more lucrative. Management said exports could return to 20-25% after the India-UK and India-EU trade agreements.
Management said Chinese competition has eased because of yuan depreciation (INR12 to INR14.5 per yuan since early 2025) and China exiting commodity business.
Recycled bottle-to-bottle chip was INR8-10 per kg above virgin chip at the start of the year. Virgin chip prices have since risen INR30-40 per kg, so recycled chip is now cheaper, per management.

Management said India imports about 2.5 million tonnes of PTA. New domestic PTA capacity from IOCL at Paradip (1.2 million tonnes), GAIL at Mangalore (1.25 million tonnes), and Reliance is expected in 2027-28. Management expects a 2-3% sourcing gain from this.

qa_highlights.question: What are current spreads and will they hold for the next quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 EBITDA margin was 9.9% and it expects this to be maintained for the next two quarters, with no big change seen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and revenue outlook, and what limits utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 volume is about 4 lakh tonnes versus 4.75 lakh tonnes in FY26, recovering to 4.75 lakh tonnes-plus in FY28. The PET chip plant is at about 60% while PSF and POY run at 100%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR200 crore project add about INR100 crore of EBITDA per year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 EBITDA will be above INR400 crore and the INR100 crore uplift from the project will come in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand polyester capacity given PTA availability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will decide next year once PTA capacity is up and Middle East and oil prices settle, and that a clearer picture will follow then.

qa_highlights.question: Will DTY's share of the mix change, and is the new output for captive use or the market?
qa_highlights.answer: DTY stays at the same share. The new specialty yarn and fibre output is for the market, not captive use.

qa_highlights.question: What is the specialty project's technology and capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Extruders are being added to existing lines to make cationic, dope-dyed and coloured filament, at about 115-120 tonnes per day plus about 70 tonnes per day on separate machines. A closed fibre line will restart for specialty and hollow fibre.

qa_highlights.question: How do proposed duty changes on POY, FDY and textured yarn affect pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see a change. Its PTA and fibre inputs carry 5% duty, so duty cuts would be neutral to positive, and it has asked for an increase from 5% to 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Will new PTA plants change sourcing and freight costs for the Nagpur plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Central India location disadvantage versus Gujarat should narrow as Odisha and Mangalore plants come on stream, though the size of the freight saving is not yet known.

qa_highlights.question: Can double-digit EBITDA margins be sustained in FY28-29, and how soon can new polyester capacity arrive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will target double digits from 9.9%. It said new greenfield polyester capacity would take 3-4 years, not before 2030, because no capacity is currently in the pipeline.

risks_watch: West Asia geopolitical disruption: Strait of Hormuz shipping routes are affecting raw material availability, freight and insurance costs. Crude is at about USD115 per barrel per management.
Margin durability: management expects raw material prices to fall later, which could reduce pass-through pricing; it has not quantified the effect.
Execution on the INR200 crore specialty project (commissioning in calendar 2027) and on the ramp-up of the PET chip plant from 60% utilisation.
Timing of new domestic PTA capacity (IOCL Paradip, GAIL Mangalore, Reliance) in 2027-28, and whether freight and sourcing savings materialise.
Management said Q1 FY27 was weak, and H1 total income fell 9.7%, so H2 needs a sharp step-up to deliver the stated FY27 EBITDA above INR400 crore.

Not less than 3 years to 4 years, because environment nowadays is very important.

500209|2026-03.headline: Infosys guides FY27 revenue growth to 1.5%-3.5% cc and margin 20%-22%, with FY26 growth at 3.1% and margin steady at 21%.
500209|2026-03.overview: Infosys closed FY26 with 3.1% constant-currency revenue growth and Q4 growth of 4.1% year-on-year, with adjusted operating margin stable at 21% (Q4 at 20.9%). Large deal TCV was $14.9-15bn for FY26 (up 28%, 55% net new) but Q4 TCV of $3.2bn was sequentially lower after a mega deal in Q3. FY27 guidance of 1.5%-3.5% cc growth is below FY26 on a midpoint basis, with about 0.75%-1% drag from a European manufacturing client and a further 0.75%-1% from onsite mix reduction. Management cited AI-driven compression offset by AI services growth, and acquisitions (Stratus closed and included, Optimum and Versent JV excluded) are a further swing factor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of FY27 guidance and what do the acquisitions contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Stratus (insurance) is closed and contributes about 25 bps; Optimum (healthcare) and the Versent JV are pending regulatory approvals and are excluded. Management said acquisitions are not baked into the guidance and will be added upon closing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did headcount decline 8,000 QoQ and what is the hiring and wage plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower volumes and utilisation drove the quarterly decline; headcount grew 5,000 YoY. At least 20,000 freshers planned for FY27. No decision yet on wage hike quantum or timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the lower Q4 TCV a sign of AI deflation or client spend cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 included a UK mega deal; excluding it, numbers are comparable. Management noted slower decision making in March in some pockets but did not see a significant impact on large deal sign-ups.

qa_highlights.question: How much does AI-driven productivity compress the existing base, and is it accelerating?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competitive intensity is high and productivity discussions are built into multi-year deals; it did not quantify gross growth vs compression and said there has been no step change in the last two months.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin walk in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Headwinds: 50 bps acquisition amortisation, 30 bps normalisation of Q3 one-off gain, 20 bps compensation costs. Offsets: 40 bps currency and 30 bps Project Maximus.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the FY27 guidance band 200 bps and what is the organic midpoint?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said visibility is better than last year when a wider 3-point band was used; the midpoint of about 2.25% organic reflects a balance of AI services growth and net new deals against compression and the Europe manufacturing ramp-down.

Ramp-down at one large European manufacturing client and the onsite mix reduction both weigh on FY27 revenue.
Wage hike timing and quantum not yet decided; margin guidance assumes its impact is absorbed.
Q4 large deal TCV fell sequentially; watch whether Q1 FY27 large deal wins and net new share recover.
Management declined to disclose AI revenue share; watch for any future disclosure.

500209|2026-06.headline: Infosys cut FY27 cc revenue growth guidance to 1.5%–3% from 1.5%–3.5% after Q1 cc growth of 2.4% YoY; margin guidance held at 20%–22%.
