500214|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA fell to INR 199 million (2.31% margin) on a 3% revenue rise, with Roha plant start-up costs and West Asia disruption driving the squeeze.
500214|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 operating income was INR 8,633 million (up about 3% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 199 million at a 2.31% margin and net profit of INR 243 million. For FY26, operating income rose about 7% to INR 29,148 million while EBITDA fell 29% to INR 2,102 million (7.21% margin) and PAT was INR 1,432 million (4.91%). Management attributed the weakness to West Asia crisis disruptions (about Rs 60 crore of deferred GCC engineering exports), input cost inflation (styrene, oleum), Roha plant depreciation and interest, and slow government fund flow on the UP Jal Jeevan project. Management declined to give FY27 sales, margin, or gross debt guidance until the second half of the year.

500214|2026-06.headline: Ion Exchange Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 49% YoY to INR 32 crore (4.54% margin) on 20% revenue growth to INR 701 crore, with treatment solutions still loss-making.
500214|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating income rose 20% YoY to INR 701 crore, but EBITDA fell 49% to INR 32 crore and PAT was INR 3 crore (0.44% margin). Management split the former engineering segment into Treatment Solutions, Industrial Products and Lifecycle Services, and reported Specialty Chemicals and Consumer Products separately. Treatment Solutions posted a EBIT loss of INR 17 crore on legacy projects, while Industrial Products margin rose to 11.89%. Management said Roha resin capacity is ramping slower than expected and guidance will be reviewed by end of Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Portugal/Iberian acquisition: progress and margin profile versus India?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition was about three years ago and integration is complete; management declined to give geography-specific margins but said margins would be similar to or better than India, with four of five segments present there (not Consumer).

qa_highlights.question: Why reclassify segments and is a corporate action or separate listing planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Engineering was not showing the full picture of products, services and solutions; no separate listing or corporate action is planned, and about 60% of the company is now products, chemicals and services versus about 40% treatment solutions.

qa_highlights.question: Roha 5x capacity claim and link to resin revenue of about INR 500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: 5x is a group-level resin capacity figure across Roha and Ankleshwar after debottlenecking; Phase I doubles capacity, and Phase II plus debottlenecking takes output to about 5x the original Ankleshwar capacity. Management aspires to about 10% of global resin volume and gave no segment split.

qa_highlights.question: Pharma resin 6x expansion: timeline, capex and revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is in process and targeted within 12 months; management said capex is manageable and the constraint is technical know-how, with asset turn well above Roha's 2-2.5x. FY26 pharma revenue was not disclosed and the segment stays within Specialty Chemicals.

qa_highlights.question: Treatment Solutions profitability: why has EBIT fallen over five years and what is the path back?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to large legacy projects, now in final stages but with a sizable portion remaining, plus a move to selective bidding, advanced and emerging solutions, and walking away from difficult projects. Cost overruns on the large project were acknowledged as a meaningful impact.

qa_highlights.question: Did the WQA certification contribute to Q1 revenue, and what is the North America outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: No quantification was given for Q1 contribution; management said a significant, though not majority, part of Roha volume is expected to go to overseas markets, notably North America, after WQA certification.

qa_highlights.question: Roha 25% first-year utilisation guidance and Consumer breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Roha guidance of 25% is still held but has been softer than expected; management will update by end of Q2 FY27. Consumer Products breakeven is the first FY27 target, with single-digit margins to be discussed later.

qa_highlights.question: Specialty Chemicals margin compression: Roha drag and other factors?
qa_highlights.answer: Roha impact on segment margin was about 6%; the prior-year FX gain reversal was about 3-4 points; and pass-through of input cost increases lagged, with some moderation expected if crude stays near USD 80.

qa_highlights.question: UP legacy project: unexecuted portion, receivables and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Unexecuted UP portion is about 11% of the June order backlog of INR 2,473 crore; receivable exposure is materially unchanged over recent quarters. Closure is not expected in FY27 and will depend on government fund flows, which have started to come in.

500215|2026-03.headline: Sundrop Brands Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 11% with EBITDA margin near 7.2% ex one-offs and ESOPs; FY26 margin up 270 bps.
500215|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 consolidated (Sundrop plus Del Monte, shown on a like-for-like basis) revenue growth of 11%, with B2B up 12% and e-commerce up 26%. Gross margin expanded close to 4% year on year, and EBITDA margin reached about 7.2% excluding ESOP and one-off costs (Wage Code related), or roughly INR28 crore. For FY26, consolidated growth was 10%, EBITDA grew about 96%, and margin reached about 5.7% with a 270 bps expansion. Management guided to a 150-225 bps annual margin expansion path, targeting double-digit EBITDA margin by FY29, while Italian olive oil value declines and peanut butter share losses remained the main drags.

segments.commentary: Del Monte is about 33% of revenue and grew about 9% in FY26 against 13% earlier. Culinary grew about 11% for the year; Italian olive oil value fell about 5% for the year while volume grew about 16-17%.

capex_capacity: Sales force automation completed: about 475,000 outlets covered (about 375,000 dedicated field force and about 100,000 via distributors), all on the Bizom mobile platform.
Direct reach of about 4.5-5 lakh outlets for ready-to-eat popcorn; total addressable outlets estimated near 1 million.
Common ERP integration under way across the two organisations, expected in about 12-14 months.

Around 70+ launches in the last year, contributing about 4% of overall sales.

Bigger packs grew about 10 percentage points faster than small packs in RTE; bigger RTC packs are about 6-7% of RTC; INR20/INR30 price points are about 6% of the business.
Olive oil deflation was passed on to consumers; Italian value fell 5% for FY26 while volume rose 16-17%, with Del Monte at about third place in Italy behind Figaro and Borges.
Price cuts in peanut butter were achieved through competitive sourcing rather than margin sacrifice; small consumer packs grew double digits in volume.
Core categories (about 62% of portfolio) are expected to grow about 12-13% this year; gross margin for the food business is about 28-30%, with edible oil about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: How far has integration of Sundrop and Del Monte progressed and what benefits have been captured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two businesses still operate largely independently. Integration so far covers back-end CFA network alignment and early use of Sundrop's distribution to push Del Monte ketchup and mayo in general trade; margin gains came mostly from standalone manufacturing and logistics work, about 4%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the merger synergy plan, timelines and quantum, and can margins expand 200-250 bps a year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 150-225 bps of annual margin expansion, around 200 bps as a midpoint, and about 100 bps in the next year plus 150-200 bps in FY28. ERP integration is due in about 12-14 months, and the coverage strategy in 6-9 months with harmonisation from FY28. Management confirmed the intent to reach double-digit EBITDA margin by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Italian olive oil business declining and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Kapoor, CEO of Del Monte Foods, said the value decline reflects olive oil commodity deflation passed through to consumers, with volume up about 17%; no significant margin deterioration. Price corrections are behind the company, and like-for-like value growth is expected from Q2, with an Italian-origin brand campaign starting in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the peanut butter decline and how will it be fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Asheesh Kumar Sharma said the issue was low-priced entrants in commoditised big packs; the company has re-sourced competitively to match prices and expects volume growth from Q2. Small packs grew double digits in volume, and seven new chocolate and high-protein variants were launched in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How are high-protein peanut butter launches priced against peers, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitish Bajaj said introductory discounts are used to drive trial; the product is said to be slightly better on protein. The approach is described as transient, with media and performance marketing supporting new users.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core versus non-core growth and gross margin split?
qa_highlights.answer: Core categories are expected to grow about 12-13% this year. Food gross margin is about 4-5 points above the company average (about 25%), so about 30%, and edible oil is about 7-8 points lower, around 20%. Gross margin excludes material, manufacturing, freight and logistics costs.

Marketing spend is set to rise toward 8% of revenue, which could compress near-term margin gains.
Reclassification of about INR6 crore of visibility spend affected reported Q4 advertising figures, so underlying comparisons need care.

qa_highlights.question: Pritesh Chheda (Lucky Investments): What are the blended volume and value growth rates for core and non-core?
qa_highlights.answer: Core (about 60% of sales) grows about 14-15% in value and 9-10% in volume. Edible oil (about 20% of business) grew about 16% in value and 7% in volume. The remaining ~20% grows about 15% in value and 8% in volume, helped by CP manufacturing such as energy drinks. Overall, about 80% of the business grows 15-16% in value and 8-9% in volume.

qa_highlights.question: Pritesh Chheda: What are the key growth pillars and the expected value and volume mix?
qa_highlights.answer: For Popcorn, Ketchup and Mayo the pillars are distribution, media investment ahead of curve, and innovation; Italian is driven more by innovation and investment, and peanut butter by innovation. Management sees about 4-5% volume growth in most categories and aims for about 10% volume, plus 4-5% price and 4-5% innovation, targeting mid-teens to high-teens growth.

qa_highlights.question: Balaji Vaidyanath (Nafa Asset Management): Is the 6-10% Italian realisation decline due to quick-commerce discounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Kapoor said no. Q1 is running on higher-cost inventory bought before last year's commodity deflation, with price pass-through having started only in Q2 last year. Prices are now stabilising and the effect should end from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Balaji Vaidyanath: Is GT/MT growth likely low single digit given B2B at 18% and e-commerce at 32%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Popcorn, Italian and oil are primarily retail. Culinary is the only mixed retail and B2B business. B2B grows faster than retail, and retail is roughly 10-12% if B2B is at 18%. The company did not give a specific GT/MT number.

qa_highlights.question: Balaji Vaidyanath: How much of the 15% edible oil growth is price pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Asheesh Sharma said about 9 points is price pass-through (per-kg increase passed on almost fully) with 7% volume, giving roughly 16% value growth.

qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki (IIFL Capital): What is the status of the Del Monte and Sundrop integration, and what savings are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is under a single operations team. Del Monte had 10 unique CFAs, with 2 already consolidated and a third underway; about 8 consolidations are targeted by year-end, leaving 2. ERP migration to a single system is expected within about 12 months, before sales-force integration. East distribution of Del Monte already runs through the Sundrop team. Synergies are about 200 bps over 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki: EBITDA goes from about 7% to about 12% in three years. What is the breakup beyond the 200 bps synergies?
qa_highlights.answer: ESOP cost (about 5.66% after ESOP) is front-loaded for 18-21 months, adding roughly 100 bps after that. Scale is worth about 100 bps a year, premiumisation 80-100 bps a year, and synergies about 100 bps a year for two years. Management aims for about 300 bps of margin expansion a year, split half to growth and half to shareholders. FY30 12% is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Shirish Pardeshi (Motilal Oswal): What is the economics and sustainability of the Rs. 10 popcorn RTC/RTE packs and their supply chain?
qa_highlights.answer: Assorted manufacturing and direct factory-to-distributor shipping cut freight and packaging cost, with a 4.5-5 month shelf life. RTE Rs. 10 has moved from margin-dilutive to margin-accretive over 18 months. Bigger packs are about one-third of the RTE mix (from one-fifth/one-third earlier), growing 42% against 33% for the rest, and e-commerce is growing about 55%.

qa_highlights.question: Shirish Pardeshi: Will premium staples volume (7%) hold if sunflower inflation drives price up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to lower-priced variants as a safety net: Sundrop Lite and Sundrop Heart Plus, with a new Sundrop Heart blend using less-inflated commodities. It targets 4-5% volume growth in the category, which is growing about 3-4%. The Sundrop Heart Jodi pack will continue through the festive season.

qa_highlights.question: Nachiket Kale (Emkay): What is the strategy for peanut butter given competition from new digital-first and PE-backed brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it lost the protein, natural and chocolate variant race because it lacked those products. The market is about 85% value-added and 15% standard. The company holds about 33% of standard and 3% of value-added peanut butter. It is launching new variants, investing in digital consumer acquisition, and aims for double-digit growth in the near term.

risks_watch: A&P optics: reported A&P is down about 12% YoY, but like-for-like is about 5% lower after the contra-revenue reclassification. Watch whether reclassification distorts sales and margin comparisons.
Input cost inflation in edible oil (sunflower), packaging and commodities. Management says price pass-through has so far protected margins, but B2B and some contracts have lagged price increases.
Peanut butter: still in decline at about 3% in value and volume, with only 3% share of value-added formats against 85% of the market. Competition from digital-first and PE-backed brands.
Italian business: realisation down 6-10% in Q1 from old inventory. Management expects stabilisation from Q2 and value growth of about 15% if volume growth holds at 15%.
Integration execution: CFA consolidation (about 8 targeted by year-end), ERP migration within about 12 months, and sales-force integration. Synergies of about 200 bps over 18 months.

Margin path to about 12% EBITDA by FY30 depends on ESOP cost rolling off after 18-21 months and on premiumisation and scale. Juices has been dropped as non-core, and any further portfolio exits or inorganic moves are open questions.
key_quotes: So, we are a tad higher, I would say sharply higher also than 4%, which we used to be about a year and a half back.
We have lost out that race because we did not have any of that product in the portfolio.
Our overall endeavor is to improve our margins by 300 basis points every year, of which we would want to deploy half back to the business and half back to the shareholders.
Our stated position on this category will be to protect volumes.
So, we will have to play the game as it is being played, that we are cognizant of.

500219|2026-03.headline: Jain Irrigation Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 4% to INR1,800 crore and EBITDA about 7%, but a March raw-material shock cost an estimated INR200-250 crore of quarterly sales.
500219|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was about INR1,800 crore versus about INR1,750 crore a year earlier, with Hi-Tech up about 8%, Plastics down slightly and Agro Processing up about 6%. Consolidated EBITDA grew about 7% and margin rose to 13.2% from 12.8%, with Hi-Tech margin at 19.8% versus 17.5%. Management attributed the shortfall versus its earlier expectation to a polymer price spike in late February to March that made farmers postpone purchases. Reported PAT was negative at about INR40 crore, driven by one-time tax and non-cash items; management cited an adjusted PAT of about INR133 crore. Management said the debt repayment due in September and March FY27 will be met from internal accruals, with refinancing and equity as backups.

segments.name: Hi-Tech (drip irrigation, tissue culture, solar agri pumps)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up about 8% and EBITDA up about 22%, margin 19.8%; FY26 revenue up over 20%. Domestic business grew about 12% and retail about 13% (target above 15%).

segments.name: Plastics (pipes and plastic sheets)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue slightly down and EBITDA up 3.3%, margin 10.2%; FY26 revenue up only 2.4% and EBITDA declined. Pipes did not grow in FY26 and are expected to grow in FY27; overseas sheet business doing well.

segments.name: Agro Processing / Food
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up about 6% but EBITDA declined; FY26 revenue above INR2,000 crore (up 9%) and EBITDA up about 9%. UK food revenue rose to GBP68 million from GBP60 million, with cost headwinds; beverage lines started in Q4.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 exports about INR455 crore versus INR500 crore, down about 10%.

guidance_outlook: Management plans to be PAT positive (after adjustments) in FY27, and says it expects FY27 to be better than FY26 on revenue, margins, cash flow and balance sheet.

Standalone operating cash flow expected to rise from about INR350 crore to INR750-800 crore in FY27, helped by about INR450 crore of government receivables and about INR150 crore of government benefits.
Management expects the second half of Q4 to be better than the first and July onwards to be better, unless another price shock occurs.
Beverage: three more lines under discussion for FY27 investment. Tomato processing plant with a Japanese partner expected to start around January.
Management declined to give numeric FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance, citing uncertainty.
Management said a food IPO is not expected in the first half of FY27; it will reassess in the second half.
capex_capacity: Beverage bottling: about INR140 crore invested over December and March quarters; two lines started in February and March, with about INR27-28 crore revenue before end-March. Three more lines are under discussion, with investment possibly in December-January.
Tamil Nadu land asset sale: MoU signed; management expects closure within weeks to a month or two. Amount not disclosed.
Alwar plant in Rajasthan is being expanded to grow pipe sales in North India.
Management says the first big government projects are complete, but final milestones remain pending.
demand_pricing: PVC and polyethylene prices rose by more than 50% within about 20 days (polyethylene about 60%) between 20 February and 25 March. Late April and early May, PVC fell to about 10% above February levels, while polyethylene remained about 40% higher.
Farmers postponed purchases in March and April; management says PVC pipe demand has since returned. Monsoon is expected to be below normal, which management sees as supportive of irrigation demand.

Management says about INR200-250 crore of Q4 revenue was lost to the March shock; standalone Q4 revenue would otherwise have been about INR1,250 crore versus about INR1,000 crore, with EBITDA about INR25 crore higher.
Export prices for farmers' produce (banana, onion, grapes) fell during the conflict-related shock; management says prices have since stabilised.

FY26 drip sales by region: Maharashtra about INR700 crore, South four states about INR400 crore, West about INR250 crore, North about INR88 crore (up from INR75 crore), East about INR107 crore (up from INR60 crore), North East about INR100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will debt repayment be serviced given limited standalone cash flow, and what restructuring or fundraising backups exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects standalone operating cash flow to rise from about INR350 crore to INR750-800 crore, plus about INR150 crore of government benefits, and expects to repay most of the debt from internal accruals. Backups include refinancing and equity. A smaller amount is due in September and the majority in March. Management says the Tamil Nadu land sale is near closure and that it will provide more clarity in July.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Tamil Nadu asset sale near closure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an MoU is signed and closure is expected within a couple of weeks to a month, though it did not give a value or a firm date.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company turn PAT positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan is to be PAT positive for FY27 on a reported basis. FY26 reported PAT was about minus INR40 crore; adjusted PAT was about INR133 crore after one-time and non-cash items.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress in beverages and bottling, and what revenue is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Two lines started in February and March with about INR27-28 crore revenue before end-March. Three more lines are under discussion. UK food EBITDA is expected to recover in FY27 as one-off cost headwinds fade.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 revenue short of expectations by about INR200-250 crore, and where was it lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the shortfall to the March raw-material price shock, which led farmers to delay purchases, and to weaker farm-gate prices from reduced exports. It said margins were held, and the lost revenue would otherwise have added about INR25 crore of EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why is drip irrigation adoption weaker in North India and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said farmers in North have lower groundwater costs and free power, so water conservation matters less. North drip sales rose about 20% to INR88 crore in FY26. Management expects adoption to grow over the next 5-7 years as dealers expand and farmers shift to value-added crops.

risks_watch: Debt servicing: additional obligations fall due in September and March FY27, and the company depends on government receivable collections, the Tamil Nadu asset sale and possible refinancing or equity.
Polymer price volatility: PVC and polyethylene remain elevated and could spike again, and management says the outlook is contingent on no new price shock.
Food business: UK and US overseas operations had challenges, with management expecting these to ease in FY27; beverage ramp-up and the tomato plant timeline are unproven.
Exports fell about 10% in FY26 to INR455 crore, with trade and tariff uncertainty flagged.
Reported PAT remains negative, and FY27 PAT positivity is only a plan.
Management did not provide quantitative FY27 guidance; watch the July update on refinancing and asset sale closure.

500219|2026-06.headline: Jain Irrigation Q1 FY27 revenue fell about 2.5% to Rs 1,500 crore; adjusted PAT dropped to Rs 3 crore from Rs 30 crore, with Rs 680 crore NCDs due this fiscal.
500219|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was about Rs 1,500 crore, down roughly 2.5% YoY, with Hi-Tech degrowing, Plastics flat and Agro-Processing growing on beverages and overseas sales. EBITDA fell because standalone India volumes were lower and fixed costs went unabsorbed; Hi-Tech margin fell to 14.4% from 16.6%. Management said April was weak, May-June improved, and July was positive, and it expects a stronger second half. Working capital days improved (consolidated net working capital 183 days vs 210 a year ago) and about 78% of EBITDA converted to cash.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (after non-cash NCD interest unwinding)

financial_highlights.change: from 210 days in June 2025 and 186 days in March 2026

segments.commentary: Revenue fell about 22% YoY; retail (MIS drip, tissue culture, solar) fell about 17% and projects fell about 63%. Drip (MIS) fell 16% from Rs 438 crore to Rs 368 crore; tissue culture fell 10%.

segments.name: Plastics
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly flat YoY; overseas plastics revenue grew about 40%, and segment EBITDA margin rose to about 11% from 10%.

segments.name: Agro-Processing (food)
segments.commentary: Grew significantly on new beverage business (about Rs 60 crore in April-June) and overseas sales, but EBITDA fell about 3 points on seasonality.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA lost in Q1 to be recovered in H2 FY27 and full-year PAT to beat FY26.
Hi-Tech: double-digit revenue growth targeted for FY27; solar pump sales expected to pick up from September.
FY27 margin guidance: about 14% standalone and about 12-13% consolidated.

Debt: about Rs 680 crore of NCDs due in FY27, about Rs 230 crore in September 2026 and the rest in March 2027; management says internal cash flows will cover them, with refinancing term sheets in hand.
Legacy government receivables target for FY27 is Rs 422 crore (minimum Rs 380 crore for the remaining nine months); Rs 60 crore collected in Q1 and Rs 25-30 crore in July.
Food business IPO deferred; management says it will look at it from September if markets improve.
capex_capacity: Biochar plant recently started (mango stones, corn cob, cotton stalk feedstock); management expects financial impact from next fiscal, with carbon credits taking 6-9 months.
Tamil Nadu land monetisation delayed by elections; management hopes it will be delivered in the current quarter.
Remaining project billing outside Pune is about Rs 40-50 crore; the large Pune water-supply project still has triple-digit crore billing left; Q2 project billing could be below Rs 24 crore.
demand_pricing: Polymer prices rose about 50%; most increases were passed to customers, and some customers postponed purchases until prices fall.
Delayed monsoon onset in June pushed drip sales into the current quarter; July was positive and August-September are expected to be good.
Government-linked and subsidy-driven micro-irrigation sales were deliberately not pursued because of cash flow and long receivables; management estimated Rs 50-60 crore of sales were forgone.
Dam storage was about 67% of capacity; management expects about 85% by monsoon-end, supportive of the rabi season and next summer.

qa_highlights.question: How much legacy government receivables were recovered and how much project work is left?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 60 crore received in Q1 and Rs 25-30 crore in July. Remaining project billing outside Pune is about Rs 40-50 crore, with no working capital needed; about 10-12 of 72 projects carry O&M over two to three years, which management called light.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 674-680 crore of debt due this fiscal be repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited internal accruals first, then legacy receivable collections, asset monetisation (surplus land) and refinancing; it said Rs 1,300 crore of bank debt was repaid over three and a half years and that the company has never missed a payment in four years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Hi-Tech down about 22% and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail fell about 17% and projects about 63%; management called the drip decline a one-off from the delayed monsoon and polymer-driven postponements. Hi-Tech margin was 14.4% vs 16.6%, and management expects margins to recover to typical levels through the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of write-offs on project receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said provisions were made in FY21-22 after a project review and it does not expect material write-offs; net receivables of Rs 1,975 crore in June are largely good, with about 55% linked to government-related items.

qa_highlights.question: Why are working capital requirements higher than listed peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to legacy long-term project receivables and state-government orders paid after 6-12 months, and said the cycle should improve substantially in FY28 once project receivables are cleared.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of refinancing and the food-business IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no pushback from lenders, a couple of term sheets are in hand, and talks are ongoing. The food-business IPO (about Rs 1,000 crore including PE exit) has been deferred due to weak valuations; the company will revisit it from September.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT negative when revenue is flat, and what are the coffee and biochar updates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the loss to higher raw-material costs and lower standalone India volumes, and expects a full-year PAT improvement. First coffee orders have come from the Coffee Board; the biochar business has started, with impact on numbers from next fiscal.

risks_watch: Refinancing of about Rs 230 crore NCD due in September 2026 and about Rs 450 crore due in March 2027 has not yet been completed; management relies on term sheets and internal cash flows.
Legacy government receivables of about Rs 800-900 crore and about Rs 500 crore of agency receivables above 180 days; collection pace against the Rs 380 crore minimum target is key.
Polymer price volatility and geopolitical oil-price movements may keep customers postponing purchases.

Food-business IPO and Tamil Nadu land monetisation timelines have slipped repeatedly.

500233|2026-03.headline: Kajaria Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% to INR 1,373 crore with volume up 11% and EBITDA margin at 19.19% versus 10.01% a year ago.
500233|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 12% YoY to INR 1,373 crore, with tiles volume up 11%, helped by sales-channel unification and a Morbi shutdown that cut industry supply. EBITDA margin expanded to 19.19% from 10.01%, and PAT rose to INR 136 crore from INR 43 crore. Management says all plants, including Morbi, have run at full capacity since 16 April, but outsourcing from Morbi remains uncertain. Management declined to give volume guidance and said it expects margins of 18% to 19%.

500233|2026-06.headline: Kajaria Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20% to INR1,328 crore and EBITDA margin hit 19.6%, driven mainly by fuel-cost-led price hikes.

500238|2026-03.headline: Whirlpool of India Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 7% to INR 2,181 crore, but PBT margin fell to 5% on e-waste and energy-change costs.
500238|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew high single digits to INR 2,181 crore, helped by washers, air conditioners (up about 50%) and Elica (up 30%), with March 2026 the highest shipment month in company history. Profit fell sharply: EBITDA was INR 121 crore (5.6%, down 33.7%) and profit before exceptional items INR 110 crore (5%, down 29%), mainly from incremental e-waste provisions and unrecovered BEE energy-upgrade costs. Refrigerator market share fell triple digits in direct cool and frost free due to the January 2026 energy-regulation phase-in/phase-out and deliberate non-matching of competitor pricing. For FY26, revenue rose 1.4% to INR 8,034 crore, EBITDA was INR 481 crore (6%), and reported PBT fell 19% including a INR 38.8 crore one-time wage code charge. Management gave no margin guidance and flagged FY27 as a difficult year.

qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify the split. E-waste is provided at the highest rate under discussion with the ministry and recyclers; any rationalisation would be a benefit. The energy upcharge is a permanent BOM cost increase, and the next energy change is about three years away.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said anything could happen and called it a roll of the dice. It is focused on component supply through the Strait of Hormuz, forex (imported content 20-35%) and pricing, and it will protect volume if it is materially outpriced.

qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said cash will go to innovation, automation, cost capex, backward integration and possible inorganic deals; there is no dividend or buyback plan at present. Management said buyback has not been looked at yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the three-to-five-year strategy, and why not a buyback despite the stock price?
qa_highlights.answer: The vision is to become the number one in refrigerators and washing machines in under 10 years, probably more than five. Management said it is focused on the next 12 to 24 months of investment and said executives bought shares personally.

qa_highlights.answer: Management described a K-curve with the entry segment (direct cool and semi-automatic) lagging. Replacement demand is being postponed. It said higher star ratings raise cost and price, so the effect on demand is complex.

500241|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 14.151 bn, but FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 13.7% amid SPP UK service-mix shift and Rs 389 mn labour-code charge.
500241|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 10% YoY to Rs 14.151 bn with EBITDA of Rs 2.093 bn (14.8% margin) and PAT of Rs 1.121 bn. Full-year revenue was flat-to-marginally up at Rs 45.380 bn (+1%), with EBITDA of Rs 6.213 bn (13.7%) and PAT of Rs 3.772 bn. Domestic revenue fell 3% for FY26 while Q4 grew 3%; international grew 7% for the year and 25% in Q4. Management attributed the year's shortfall to JJM funding delays, a foundry ERP transition, and a Rs 389 mn labour-code charge classified as exceptional. Order books grew strongly: domestic Rs 24.680 bn (+30%) and international Rs 14.808 bn (+21%).

500241|2026-06.headline: Kirloskar Brothers Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% YoY to Rs.11,049 million, but EBITDA grew only 2% at an 11.8% margin.
500241|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to Rs.11,049 million and consolidated EBITDA rose 2% to Rs.1,306 million, a margin of 11.8%. Standalone domestic revenue grew 9% to Rs.6,738 million, EBITDA 16% to Rs.920 million, and PAT 15% to Rs.540 million. International revenue grew 19%, but international EBITDA margin fell to 5.1% on lower high-margin services revenue at SPP UK and weak Rodelta execution. Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for FY27 on both standalone and consolidated bases, while acknowledging that a large order slipped and foundry modernisation delayed some dispatches.

moderated due to lower services contribution

qa_highlights.question: When will the services expansion lift SPP UK margins, and what is the outlook for Rodelta?
qa_highlights.answer: SPP UK services expected to restart in Q2 FY27 (Q3 for KBL) as power plant and water utility contracts ramp. Rodelta delays are due to consolidating Dutch entities; improvement expected in the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why was consolidated margin down from 13% in Q4 to 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said standalone EBITDA margin was 13.7% vs 12.8% last year; the drop was mainly SPP UK. Management agreed margins should recover as services revive from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the domestic order book executes in FY27, and what drove the power order book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds of the ~Rs.2,500 crore domestic order book expected in FY27. Power growth is largely nuclear, with primary and secondary circuit orders received in Q1 and new thermal plants.

500245|2026-03.headline: Kirloskar Ferrous Q4 FY26 PBT rose to INR514 crore from INR432 crore, with FY27 casting volume target of about 1.85 lakh tonnes.
500245|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 pig iron production fell 3% YoY to 1,58,152 tonnes after a roughly 3.5-month Hiriyur blast furnace stoppage cut FY26 output by about 68,000 tonnes. Casting volumes grew 13% in Q4 and 7% for the year, helped by Oliver Engineering in Rajpura, while tube production rose 6% in Q4. Management said pig iron prices recovered in Q4 and into April, with reported PBT of INR514 crore versus INR432 crore a year earlier. Management guided to 15% volume growth in FY27 and an EBITDA margin of about 12.5%, below its 15% comfort level.

financial_highlights.change: approx. INR 100 crore improvement on PBT per management

segments.commentary: Q4 production 36,596 t (up 13%) and sales 34,980 t (up 9%). FY26 production 1,48,564 t (up about 7%); including Oliver, about 1.62 lakh t, with Oliver contributing about 23,000 t (16% of sales).

segments.commentary: Q4 production 56,119 t (up 6%) and sales 51,106 t (flat vs 51,500 t). FY26 production 2,16,914 t vs 1,99,443 t; FY26 sales 1,88,700 t vs 1,68,800 t.

segments.commentary: Q4 production 58,119 t (down about 10%) and sales 24,812 t (up 20% from 20,700 t). FY26 production about 2.40 lakh t vs 2.42 lakh t, hit by two fume-extraction shutdowns.

qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 1,80,000-1,90,000 t as target, with about 1.05 lakh t from Koppal, 60,000 t from Solapur and 25,000 t from Oliver; the 45,000 t/quarter run rate expected within a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trajectory and backward integration plan?

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 pig iron price hikes lag and how will Q1 FY27 spreads move?
qa_highlights.answer: Lag came from 15-day order books and monthly commitments to regular customers; price increase effect partly in April. Management said pig iron price increase is inevitable but coal and coke costs are rising, and it is still assessing spreads.

qa_highlights.question: How much power cost saving from solar, wind and captive power?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar delivered about INR 70 crore benefit in FY26; wind and solar commissioning June-September should add about INR 45 crore in FY27, with INR 90 crore possible at full run-rate after new Maharashtra regulations.

qa_highlights.question: Tube business order book and ONGC orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the pending order figure; expects new tenders this year and better domestic and export oil and gas demand. Targets 10-11% volume growth in tubes.

qa_highlights.answer: Bigger tube mill at Baramati about INR 500 crore, within a 1.5-year completion; total capex about INR 600-700 crore per year, with borrowings reduced.

500245|2026-06.headline: Kirloskar Ferrous Q1 FY27: castings sales up 18% to 41,345 t, tube sales down 14% to 41,512 t, and power and fuel costs rose about INR58 crore YoY.
500245|2026-06.overview: Pig iron and castings output rose in Q1 FY27, while tube output and sales fell on weaker high-value oil and gas and export orders. Power and fuel costs rose sharply, with about INR58 crore of the INR100 crore YoY jump in other expenses coming from power and fuel, half of it from rate increases. A change in green-power rules (8 hours instead of 17) and the end of power trading (about INR10 crore a year) cut the expected solar and wind savings to about INR80 crore a year from about INR100 crore. Management guided to recovery in pricing and volumes from Q2, and said Q1 EBITDA margin was 12-13%.

financial_highlights.change: -3% YoY vs 132,392 t; management attributed to higher internal consumption
Company level; steel and tube margins cited at 14-17%

financial_highlights.metric: Power and fuel cost increase in other expenses
financial_highlights.value: INR58 crore of ~INR100 crore YoY jump
financial_highlights.change: About INR50 crore sequential jump in other expenses; about INR30 crore from rate increases

segments.name: Castings
segments.commentary: Sales of 41,345 t, up 18% YoY; pricing passed through to customers, with further price increases still being concluded. Rajpura foundry is fully sold out at about 2,200 t per month.

segments.name: Tubes
segments.commentary: Sales of 41,512 t, down 14% YoY, with a weaker product mix as more line pipe was sold in place of high-realising export and oil and gas tubes. Management is in a wait-and-watch stance due to Chinese dumping and subdued demand.

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: Realisation improved YoY and QoQ (about INR42,400/t vs INR39,000/t base, as cited on the call); about 30,000 t exported at slightly better than domestic prices. Pig iron EBITDA is expected to support the company margin.

segments.name: Steel (alloy)
segments.commentary: Management expects external sales of 100,000-110,000 t this year vs about 84,000 t, but cost pass-through is still under discussion.

guidance_outlook: Castings volumes expected to rise to about 162,000 t gross sales and then about 188,000 t, implying roughly 17-20% growth.
Overall volume growth of at least 15% across products in the remaining three quarters, with tube volumes up at least 10% YoY and steel external sales up more than 20%.
Pig iron output close to 700,000 t this year, possibly slightly less.
Price-increase and cost pass-through benefits expected from Q2 and Q3 onward.

Medium term: about INR14,000 crore revenue aspiration with 300,000 t castings, 300,000 t casting sales and 400,000 t tube sales. Management said castings reach 270,000 t realisable capacity in this year plus two more years, with tubes at 350,000 t in 3-4 years.
Capex of INR600-700 crore this year, rising in the following years; about INR3,000-3,500 crore over the next four years.
capex_capacity: 35 MW solar plant in commissioning stage; 12 windmills of 2.1 MW each; both expected to be commissioned between June and September 2026.
Solapur two-part (no-bake) foundry, 15,000 t per annum, with commissioning expected by October 2026. Management said it has capacity of about 1,250 t per month.
Rajpura expansion: first phase to 40,000-50,000 t per annum within about 8 months; second phase to 70,000 t per annum. Total realisable castings capacity across six foundries is 270,000 t per annum.
Koppal oxygen plant and enhanced pulverised coal injection in blast furnaces 1 and 2, expected to complete by February-March 2027. Hiriyur pig iron upgrade to 360,000 t, taking about nine months.
Jejuri rolling capacity to rise from 15,000 t to 25,000 t per month (about 3 lakh t per annum), with about 240,000 t saleable; about 18-month timeline.

Premium couplings plant in Baramati, order expected within weeks. Koppal steel plant (about 2 years) and Baramati expander mill (2 years to build) are at early stages. Iron ore mines and pelletisation at Koppal are in progress.
One blast furnace to move to steelmaking, with government clearances in place; decision expected within 2-3 months, commissioning in about 2 years.
demand_pricing: Castings demand described as strong across tractors, automobiles, earthmoving equipment and stationary engines; management expects realisation improvement.
Tube demand subdued by oil and gas slowdown and export disruption; Chinese dumping is pressuring pricing. Management expects the tube market to recover.
Coke dumping into India has reportedly eased, which supports domestic pig iron prices. Pig iron exports are running at about 30,000 t.
Fuel costs rose sharply: LPG cost in Solapur roughly doubled versus pre-war levels. Coking coal cost is expected to peak in June-August because of a three-month coal inventory.
Monthly pig iron sales plan of about 58,000 t including internal sales (about 48,000 t external); foundry grade about 20,000-25,000 t of that.

qa_highlights.question: Nirmal (Unique PMS): what drove the ~INR100 crore YoY and ~INR50 crore QoQ jump in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR58 crore of the increase is power and fuel, split roughly INR28-29 crore rate-driven and INR28 crore volume-driven, with Rajpura castings volumes and a full-month Jejuri run versus last year's shutdown. Power trading (about INR10 crore a year) has stopped and green power use is now limited to 8 hours instead of 17.

qa_highlights.question: Nirmal: does the regulation change hit the solar and wind savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, savings fall to about INR80 crore a year from about INR100 crore, and payback stretches from 3 years to 3.6-3.7 years. Battery storage at MW scale is being examined, with some power expected through batteries shortly.

qa_highlights.question: Nirmal: what is the INR350 crore contingent liability for forest development fee?
qa_highlights.answer: Karnataka levied forest development fees in 2016; the company won in the High Court, the state appealed to the Supreme Court, and the matter is sub judice after hearings with orders reserved. The company provides at 8% and discloses it as a contingent liability.

qa_highlights.question: Vipul Mody (individual investor): will the company move into subassemblies, machined components and high-end castings, and what is the status of 3D printing?
qa_highlights.answer: Machine shops at Koppal, Solapur and Rajpura already supply fully machined components, including a 6-cylinder head to an OEM. Maximum casting size after expansion is about 3 tons, the 2-part foundry is about 1,250 t per month, and the company is not yet in mining or wear-resistant parts. Prototyping is near serial production, with 50 cylinder blocks bought via the proto route.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor (Kapoor & Co): what is Q1 EBITDA margin and how will it trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put Q1 company EBITDA at 12-13%, with steel and tube margins at 14-17% and pig iron weighing on the blend. Castings target about 15% plus or minus 1%, with pricing upside, and tubes are in a wait-and-watch phase due to Chinese dumping. Management expects company margin to improve on pig iron support and pass-through from Q2-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: what are current pig iron realisations and how much did raw-material costs absorb?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation moved from a base of about INR39,000/t to about INR42,400/t QoQ. Management said dollar rates and coal costs are pressuring costs, but realisation still improved slightly net of cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Dhruvesh Kanakia (Antique): what volumes are expected for the remaining nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: Pig iron close to 700,000 t this year, possibly slightly less. Castings gross sales to rise from about 162,000 t to about 188,000 t (17-20% growth). Steel external sales of 100,000-110,000 t vs about 84,000 t, and tube volumes up at least 10%, with overall volume growth of at least 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Manish Goyal (Thinkwise): timeline for INR14,000 crore revenue aspiration, seventh foundry, and ONGC/OIL tube order execution?
qa_highlights.answer: Castings realisable capacity of 270,000 t is targeted in this year plus two years, with 300,000 t in 3-4 years; tubes to 350,000 t in 3-4 years after the expander mill (2 years to build); steel external sales of 240,000 t in about 2 years. Blast furnace 1 conversion to steelmaking is expected to be decided within 2-3 months, with commissioning in about 2 years. The 23,000 t tube order should complete in the next two quarters.

Seasonal wind benefit is about 70% in June-September. Koppal is self-sufficient on waste-heat power, but Maharashtra fuel costs need a strategy and power trading is not likely to return without battery storage.

risks_watch: Power and fuel cost inflation: about INR58 crore of YoY increase, LPG in Solapur roughly doubled, and coking coal peaking June-August; watch whether castings and alloy steel price pass-through actually lands in Q2-Q3.

Green power economics: regulatory limit cut from 17 to 8 hours, power trading (about INR10 crore a year) stopped, and solar and wind savings cut to about INR80 crore from about INR100 crore; payback moved to 3.6-3.7 years.

Execution of capex: INR600-700 crore this year against INR3,000-3,500 crore over four years; Solapur 2-part foundry by October 2026, solar and wind commissioning June-September 2026, Koppal oxygen and PCI by February-March 2027.
Pig iron pricing and exports: realisation up to about INR42,400/t from INR39,000/t; about 30,000 t exported; a dollar and coal cost squeeze could offset gains.

500257|2026-03.headline: Lupin Q4 FY26 revenue rose 32% YoY to Rs 7,475 crore and EBITDA 68% to Rs 2,171 crore; FY27 guided to high-single-digit growth and ~25% margin.
500257|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the 15th consecutive quarter of YoY growth, with record sales and profitability; EBITDA margin was 29.4% (ex forex and other income), up 620 bps YoY. Q4 EBITDA moved down QoQ, which management attributed to the Mirabegron settlement payment to Astellas, forex and higher manpower cost booked in other expenses. Management guided FY27 to high-single-digit revenue growth (in rupee terms) and around 25% EBITDA margin, citing Tolvaptan and Mirabegron competition, higher R&D (~8% of sales) and a 25-26% ETR.

500257|2026-06.headline: Lupin Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR 8,277 crore and EBITDA hit INR 2,464 crore (30% margin), but management guided to a sharper US slowdown ahead.
500257|2026-06.overview: Lupin reported a record quarter with revenue from operations of INR 8,277 crore (up 32% YoY) and EBITDA excluding forex and other income of INR 2,464 crore (up 50% YoY, 30% margin, up 340 bps). Growth was broad-based across the US, India, Other Developed Markets, Emerging Markets and GIB, with ex-US organic growth above 20%. Management said Q2 onwards the US will moderate on Tolvaptan and Mirabegron competition, with quarterly US sales of USD 250-280 million, and it trimmed full-year EBITDA margin guidance to 24-25% from around 25%. Net cash fell to INR 2,831 crore from INR 4,636 crore after the VISUfarma acquisition closed.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Sales of USD 366 million, up 30% YoY in constant currency, driven by base volumes and partly offset by Mirabegron competition. FY27 US guidance is USD 1.1-1.2 billion, with management expecting USD 250-280 million per quarter over the next couple of quarters.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Sales of INR 2,380 crore, up 13.9% YoY; diabetes grew 31.8% (1.8x category) and cardiac 1.2x category, while respiratory grew 6.9% vs category 11.3%. Chronic share rose to about 67% from about 65% in FY26; volume growth was 6.1%.

segments.name: Other Developed Markets (Europe, Canada, Australia)
segments.commentary: Sales of INR 1,149 crore, up 48% YoY, with Europe up 83% YoY. VISUfarma consolidation began this quarter. Management guides 10-20% growth over the next couple of years.

segments.name: Emerging Markets
segments.commentary: Sales of INR 990 crore, up 52% YoY. Brazil grew 117% YoY in local currency on Dapagliflozin and Empagliflozin launches.

segments.name: GIB
segments.commentary: Grew 40% YoY in the quarter, per management; no further detail given on the segment's drivers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 US revenue guided at USD 1.1-1.2 billion; US growth expected to resume from FY28.
Full-year high single-digit revenue growth reiterated.
Full-year EBITDA margin now guided at 24-25% (earlier around 25%), with management citing a gross margin reduction from geopolitically driven cost increases and Tolvaptan pricing.
Full-year R&D guided at about 8% of sales; full-year ETR guided at 27-28%.

Biosimilar and launch plan: Pegfilgrastim H2 FY27, Ranibizumab and Aflibercept in Europe and later US; Etanercept in calendar 2029. Management sees biosimilars ramping to a couple of hundred million dollars across US and Europe within three years.

Albuterol US share stabilised at about 16% (down from 19-20%); Tiotropium share about 38%, which management expects to hold.

Europe: Germany's higher rebate affects part of the portfolio, but Ranibizumab and Aflibercept biosimilars are no longer in AOK tenders, creating a branded opportunity; France is pushing biosimilar substitution.
Adjacencies (Diagnostics, Digital, OTC, CDMO) reduce EBITDA margin by about 1-1.5%; management expects them to break even over time, with Diagnostics breaking even next year.
Apixaban 505(b)(2) could reach a scale similar to Mirabegron or Tolvaptan, per management, with targeted channel entry before generics arrive in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Does the USD 1.1-1.2 billion US guidance form the base for the return to growth in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that FY28 growth is expected over the FY27 base of USD 1.1-1.2 billion.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the US guidance imply a step-down from Q1's USD 366 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Tolvaptan faces new entrants from Q2 (Apotex, Teva, possibly a fourth in September), and Mirabegron has a full-quarter impact from Q2, so management expects USD 250-280 million per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is a normalised gross margin given the 74.6% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh Swaminathan said it depends on Tolvaptan volumes and realisations, competition, and price increases after geopolitical cost rises; Q1 benefited from carried-forward inventory, so margins are guided lower at 24-25% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How large can the Apixaban 505(b)(2) opportunity be?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it could reach Mirabegron or Tolvaptan scale, targeting a few large channels ahead of FY29 generic entry, with approval goal date September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How big can biosimilars be across the US and Europe over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees a couple of hundred million dollars in revenue from Pegfilgrastim, Ranibizumab, Aflibercept and Etanercept, though it did not size each product.

qa_highlights.question: Could EBITDA margin fall below 20% in some quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh Swaminathan said quarterly volatility is certain but declined to quantify it; R&D is at least a notch above peers and adjacency losses are a 1-1.5% drag.

500271|2026-06.headline: Axis Max Life VNB rose 33% in Q1 FY27 with VNB margin up to 23.2% from 20.3%, while APE grew 15%.
500271|2026-06.overview: Axis Max Life posted 15% APE growth and 19% GWP growth to INR10,610 crore in Q1 FY27, with individual adjusted first-year premium up 17%. VNB margin expanded about 3 points year on year to 23.2%, driving 33% VNB growth despite the residual GST impact, which management says is now behind them. Solvency was 198% after Axis Bank's INR381 crore equity infusion, which took Axis to 19.99%. Management reiterated plans for structure simplification (merger of MFSL into AMLI, subject to NCLT timelines of 6–12 months) and kept the INR1,600 crore QIP enabling approval open, with a sub-debt raise planned to replace the redeemed sub-debt.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin increase, residual GST effect, and why did solvency stay flat despite protection growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management split the ~3-point margin gain as ~30% protection mix and operating leverage, ~70% yield curve. About 80% of the GST effect was taken in Q4 and no further GST impact is expected. Solvency rose to 198% on the Axis infusion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the structure simplification timeline intact, and how does Axis's potential stake increase affect plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Scheme filing followed by NCLT approval takes 6–12 months and those timelines hold. Management is still doing internal and shareholder consultation; Axis is evaluating going to 30% and both sides will disclose in due course.

qa_highlights.question: Opex-to-GWP improvement despite GST input tax credit loss, and the offline proprietary slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth was held down by productivity gains and cost cuts (travel, advertising, negotiations). Management said some of this will normalise. Offline prop growth was affected by deliberate cancellation of certain sourced policies that did not meet quality standards.

qa_highlights.question: How long can solvency be run before a capital raise is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can stay above its internal threshold for at least two to three quarters comfortably, helped by debt capacity from the Axis equity infusion; RBC and Ind AS 117 clarity expected in the next few months.

qa_highlights.question: Does the annuity push raise any product margin concerns; what is the variable annuity risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Annuity and non-par margins are broadly similar in aggregate. The variable annuity has a fixed return component hedged in line with other products; the equity-linked component is borne by the annuitant, so no additional company risk is claimed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the protection-led margin expansion sustainable given the June yield curve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged that the June curve moved lower and may unwind some Q1 yield benefit, but said repricing is normal and maintained the aspiration of VNB growth outpacing APE growth; it did not accept the 70% yield benefit would fully reverse.

500279|2026-06.headline: Onida Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29.5% YoY to Rs 182.4 crore, but net loss widened to Rs 14.2 crore from Rs 12.5 crore.

Gross margin improved 100 bps to 17.3%, helped by mix and AC/LED realisations, partly offset by washing machine margin pressure from input costs and competitor pricing. Management declined to give revenue or EBITDA guidance or timelines, repeatedly pointing to revenue momentum as the first step and profitability only after scale is reached.

500280|2026-03.headline: Century Enka Q4 FY26 operating revenue Rs 484 crore (+9% YoY) with EBITDA margin up 948 bps YoY to 11.46%, aided by price pass-through and some low-cost inventory.
500280|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sharp YoY profit recovery: volume grew 14% YoY to 20,711 MT and EBITDA rose to Rs 55 crore, with price increases passed through after the Iran-related raw material spike from March. For FY26, revenue fell 15% to Rs 1,705 crore on 6% lower volume, but EBITDA (+29%) and PAT (+52%) improved. Management said the company has raised its indicative operating margin band to 7-10% from 6-8%, though it declined to guide quarterly numbers. Management indicated part of the gain came from consumption of lower-priced raw material, which will fade, and said the Rs 100 crore FY27 capex and renewable power additions will help margins only from H2.

500280|2026-06.headline: Century Enka Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 38% YoY to Rs 554 crore, with EBITDA margin at 15.46%, helped by a Rs 46.24 crore one-time inventory gain.
500280|2026-06.overview: Revenue of Rs 554 crore grew 38% YoY and 15% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs 86 crore (up 331% YoY) and PAT of about Rs 62 crore (up 301% YoY). Management attributed the margin jump partly to a one-time inventory gain from low-cost opening stock (Rs 46.24 crore as reported) and partly to GST-cut-driven auto and tyre demand, pass-through pricing and a higher renewable power share above 40%. Management said margins are expected to normalise, and it kept its normalised operating margin range at 7-10%.

Management flagged geopolitical events, volatile crude, inflation and cheap imports as risks to domestic demand. Exports are very small.

500280|2026-09.headline: Century Enka Q2 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to Rs 558 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 5.88% and PAT dropped 17% YoY to Rs 19 crore.
500280|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations grew 37% YoY to Rs 558 crore in Q2 FY27, with volume up 13% YoY to 20,162 MT, largely on higher raw material-led realisations. EBITDA rose 4% YoY to Rs 33 crore but margin compressed to 5.88% (down 186 bps YoY and 958 bps QoQ) as raw material volatility, a normalising low-cost opening inventory benefit and higher grid power and LNG costs weighed. H1 FY27 revenue rose 37% to Rs 1,113 crore, EBITDA rose 130% to Rs 119 crore and PAT rose 113% to Rs 80 crore. Imports hit tyre cord fabric (NTCF) sales volume in Q2, while PTCF commercial sales are slated to start in Q4 FY27.

500284|2026-03.headline: FY26 PAT rose 360.9% to INR28.49 crore on caustic soda volume up 29.7% to 84,690 MT; Q4 EBITDA margin 14.03% hit by grid power tariff revision.
500284|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 as a step-up year: total income INR393.1 crore (+44.62% YoY), EBITDA INR66.38 crore (+159%) at a 16.89% margin (+747 bps). Q4 FY26 total income was INR97.75 crore (+22.3% YoY), EBITDA INR13.72 crore at 14.03% margin (up 247 bps QoQ), and PAT INR4.39 crore (+68.64% YoY). Q4 margins were below Q3's stated level of above 20% because the grid power rate revision effective 1 October 2025 persisted and one electrolyser was shut for renovation, raising power consumption. Management said a 21 MW solar plant in Rajasthan is due around mid-June 2026, with renewables expected to rise to 40-45% of power needs.

from INR181.67 crore a year ago

segments.name: Caustic soda lye

segments.name: Chlorinated paraffin wax (CPW)
segments.commentary: Contributed meaningfully to Q4 revenue. Capacity is being expanded from 50 to 100 TPD, and management cited it as converting chlorine into a value-added product that stabilises the mix.

guidance_outlook: 21 MW solar plant in Rajasthan expected to be commissioned around mid-June 2026; renewable share expected to rise from about 15-20% to 40-45% of power needs.

10 MW hybrid wind-solar group captive project: management said full 100 MW wind component to be completed next month and full contracted units expected from June 2026 onward, after the shortfall (about 97 lakh units) that was credited to power expenses under the agreement.
Expects caustic capacity utilisation of 80-85% over the next year.
Total installed capacity to reach 360 TPD after the 100 TPD caustic expansion, with an old 40 TPD plant decommissioned (gross would have been 400 TPD).
Management expects the energy-cost benefit to ease margin pressure once renewables are running; expects Q4's power-cost headwind to recede.
Plans to raise about INR90 crore of additional long-term debt; cost of debt around 8% (total about 7.9%).
capex_capacity: Total capex outlay INR315 crore over FY24 to FY27-28; first phase of INR150 crore (90 TPD caustic expansion, 16 MW Bikaner solar, equity in 10 MW hybrid project) completed.
Second phase under execution: 21 MW captive solar, CPW expansion from 50 to 100 TPD, and a further 100 TPD caustic soda expansion. Capital WIP INR43.85 crore at year-end.
Caustic soda capacity to reach 360 TPD post-expansion; new caustic capacity comes online around end-FY27, per analyst's reading of management's timeline.
Sulfuric acid project deferred due to volatile global sulfur prices; management cited heat-recovery use for a planned flaking unit as the rationale.
demand_pricing: Management cited India caustic demand growth of about 5-6% nationally and 4-5% in North India; no new North India capacity is announced in the next 15-18 months, and management sees none for 2-2.5 years. Company has 300 TPD of a roughly 1,600 TPD North India capacity (about 20%), rising to 26-27% after expansion.
Management said salt is contracted yearly at about 11-12% of production cost, with consumption of 1.61-1.62 t salt per t caustic; purification chemicals rose 20-30% but are only 1-2% of cost.
Caustic soda prices spiked 30-35% in March 2026 and have since eased to about 12-15% above pre-war levels, per management.

Management said Indian capacity additions of 2-2.5 million tonnes over three years are largely captive for PVC on the West Coast and expected to export; chlorine prices are currently negative in India.

qa_highlights.question: Shortfall of about 97 lakh units from the consortium: how is it accounted and will it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shortfall reflected committed units not supplied under the power purchase agreement, that the credit taken in power expenses is not reversible, and that full units are expected from June 2026 as the wind project completes.

qa_highlights.question: With utilisation near 80% and new capacity only at end-FY27, how will quarterly growth come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation should reach 80-85% over the next year, with demand exceeding North India supply given no new regional capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the sulfuric acid plant deferred?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulfur supply has been volatile for six to nine months and the war began about three months ago, so the project is on the back burner pending stability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margin fall versus Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Grid tariff revision applied in both quarters; caustic prices eased QoQ, and an electrolyser shutdown for membrane and electrode renovation raised power consumption in the last months of the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net renewable savings and power cost without solar?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a figure. It said the grid landed cost rose from about INR7 to INR8.2-8.3 per unit (a 15-18% rise) and that renewables are about 15-20% of power today.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of debt and FY27 interest outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Average cost of debt is a little under 8% (about 7.9%) and INR90 crore of additional long-term debt is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Is further renewable capex planned beyond current projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is evaluating more opportunities, pausing until the 21 MW project is done and domestic cell mandates settle, with a stated aim of maximising renewable share within regulations.

qa_highlights.question: Will new South and West Coast capacity cause oversupply in the domestic market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued that new capacity is PVC-linked and export-oriented, that chlorine-caustic (ECU) pricing offsets, and that the North India market is small and fragmented.

risks_watch: Q4 margin of 14.03% versus Q3's above 20%: whether electrolyser renovation and the grid tariff of about INR8.2-8.3/unit are reversed in Q1 FY27.

Capacity timing: 21 MW solar and 100 TPD caustic/CPW expansions are due around mid-June 2026 and end-FY27; delays would hit volume and margin guidance.
Sulfur and sulfuric acid supply volatility, plus deferral of the acid project.
Debt rising by about INR90 crore at around 8% cost, with capex of INR315 crore funded by accruals and debt.
Future new capacity from West Coast PVC-linked players could affect pricing, though management argues it is export-oriented.

500292|2026-03.headline: HeidelbergCement India FY26 EBITDA rose 19.8% to a per-ton figure of INR584 (up 10%) as volumes grew 8.8%; company now debt-free.
500292|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed higher EBITDA (up 19.8% YoY), PAT up 25.5%, and sales volume up 8.8%, with EBITDA per ton rising from INR530 to INR584. Q4 was weaker on price: gross realisation fell about INR105/ton QoQ, with INR53 raw material and INR25 other cost headwinds, only partly offset by power, fuel and freight. Management expects H1 FY27 cost pressure of INR100-160/ton (fuel and packaging), which it says it can pass on, though it expects prices to stay under pressure through the monsoon. The company repaid INR687 million of interest-free loans, is fully debt-free, and proposed a INR7 dividend per share.

segments.name: Cement (Central India)
segments.commentary: Clinker production about 3.05 million tons in FY26, running at roughly 90-95% utilisation of about 6 million tons grinding capacity. Clinker-to-cement ratio about 60-61%, targeted to fall 50-100 bps. Blended cement is about 97% of output.

segments.name: Premium and trade mix
segments.commentary: Premium products are 52% of trade volumes, up 9% YoY. Trade sales are 81% of total, with B2B at 19%.

segments.name: Logistics and fuel
segments.commentary: Road dispatches are about 45% of volume (up 1% YoY). AFR is about 11% (up 3% YoY). Lead distance is about 372 km. Petcoke share of fuel fell about 10 points to roughly 50-55%, with coal rising from 30% to 40%.

guidance_outlook: Industry demand in Central India expected to grow at least 7-7.5% in FY27; company volumes to track industry growth, constrained by near-full utilisation.
Q1 FY27 cost increase expected at INR100-150/ton (fuel mix, diesel, packaging); total H1 pressure INR100-160/ton, which management says can be passed on.
Prices expected under pressure through the monsoon (next quarter); firmer demand expected post-monsoon ahead of UP elections.
Capex about INR100 crore in FY27 and about INR120 crore in FY28, including sustaining capex of INR45-50 crore per year and the Khandwa blending unit (about INR130 crore over two years, backloaded).
Green power share targeted to rise above 40% in FY27-FY28, though management said a significant increase is unlikely.
Company has sufficient capacity headroom for the next 1-2 years.
capex_capacity: Khandwa (MP) blending unit: about 0.35 million tons (about 35,000 tons) of extra cement capacity; investment about INR130 crore over two years; CT received; completion expected within about 2 years.

Cement grinding capacity about 5.75 million tons (Central India) plus about 0.5 million tons at Karnataka, for total about 6.26 million tons as confirmed on the call. Clinker capacity about 3.1 million tons, with debottlenecking completed to about 3.23 million tons but awaiting government capacity approval.

Preferred bidder for two limestone mining leases in Madhya Pradesh: Kuria/Shivpur block (about 350 hectares, 62 million tons cement-grade limestone) and a second Shivpur block (about 105 million tons).
Gujarat plant: still awaiting government clearance; capacity figure of 2.5-4 million tons mentioned earlier, not finalised.
Karnataka: 3 million ton integrated plant under construction (not part of the listed entity).
demand_pricing: Central India pricing has been under pressure for several quarters due to new capacity (JK Cement, UltraTech ramp-up, other new cement operations).
Management expects Central India prices to follow Northern markets over the next year. It expects prices to stay soft until the monsoon ends.
Dalmia's integration of the JP assets, expected to add about 5 million tons from Q2, was raised by an analyst; management did not address it directly.
Clinker sales were said to be small and clinker was not purchased; sales volume figures were not split out.

qa_highlights.question: What was FY26 clinker production and what is the utilisation headroom and cement-to-clinker ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Clinker production was about 3.05 million tons in FY26, with cement capacity about 6 million tons and utilisation about 90-95%. Clinker ratio is about 60-61%, targeted to fall 50-100 bps; a new composite cement uses about 17% less clinker.

qa_highlights.question: What cost increase is expected next quarter and what levers exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a cost increase of INR100-150/ton next quarter. It sees INR100-160/ton as passable to customers. Fuel mix optimisation (petcoke to coal) could limit the impact to about INR150/ton versus the industry's about INR300.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Central India pricing weak, and can cost push be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited new capacity (JK, a cement plant that came online, UltraTech ramp-up). It is confident of passing on cost increases with a lag but declined to forecast structural pricing beyond one year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the blending and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Khandwa blending unit adds about 0.35 million tons, costs about INR130 crore over two years, and is back-loaded. Total capex is about INR100 crore in FY27 and about INR120 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Clinker debottlenecking and capacity approval status?
qa_highlights.answer: Kiln debottlenecking is complete, raising clinker capacity to about 3.23 million tons, but the government capacity approval is still pending. Grinding capacity is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for merger with Zuari and clinker sales volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a merger of group entities is planned eventually, but it would not set a timeline. Management declined to disclose clinker sales volume separately.

risks_watch: Central India price pressure from new capacity (JK, UltraTech, Dalmia/JP assets) may persist beyond the monsoon.
Fuel cost inflation from petcoke and diesel tied to the West Asia conflict; the company says it expects to pass on increases with a lag.
Macro risks: elevated headline inflation, currency depreciation (import-dependent), El Nino heat impact on rural demand.
Pending government approvals for clinker capacity (3.23 million tons) and the Gujarat plant.
Clinker ratio reduction and new composite cement ramp-up.

500294|2026-03.headline: NCC Q4 FY26 standalone turnover fell 1% to INR5,382 crores; consolidated order book hit a record INR83,004 crores, but no FY27 guidance was given.
500294|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 turnover rose 1% YoY to INR6,251 crores, while full-year consolidated turnover fell 6% to INR20,944 crores and standalone fell 9% to INR17,669 crores. Consolidated order book reached INR83,004 crores (about 16% up YoY), with Q4 inflows of INR9,573 crores. Margins compressed YoY: consolidated EBITDA 8.83% vs 9.07%, and PAT 3.3% vs 4.1%. Management declined to give FY27 guidance on revenue, margin, order inflow, capex or working capital, citing an uncertain environment, and said it would revisit after Q1. Debt-to-equity improved to 0.30x from 0.40x in Q3, and JJM (UP) receivables fell sharply after roughly INR1,000 crores of collections.

500294|2026-06.headline: NCC Q1 FY27 consolidated turnover rose 12% to INR 5,842 crore with EBITDA margin of 9.38%; FY27 guidance issued (8-10% revenue growth, 8.5-9% margin).
500294|2026-06.overview: Consolidated turnover grew 12% YoY to INR 5,842 crore, the highest Q1 and overall consolidated turnover in company history, while standalone turnover rose 12% to INR 4,952 crore. Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 9.38% from 8.81%, but PAT margin was 3.7% and consolidated PAT fell to INR 216.4 crore from INR 192.1 crore only on a reported basis (standalone PAT fell 1.4% YoY). Order book closed at INR 81,214 crore after INR 3,889 crore of inflows in the quarter, and management issued its first FY27 guidance. Debt rose sharply, with consolidated net debt at INR 3,513 crore, driven by smart-meter project loans.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was encouraging but the environment is uncertain, and guidance was shared after a detailed exercise. Execution capability is unchanged; the performance depends on client funding, approvals and right-of-way, so no upside figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Unbilled revenue ballooning faster than revenue; will conversion be lumpy?

qa_highlights.question: Ken-Betwa status and effect of local protests?

500300|2026-03.headline: Grasim Q4 FY26: Birla Opus revenue up 52% YoY like-to-like, Pivot revenue more than doubled; paint price hikes staggered into Q1 FY27 on crude-linked input cost spike.
500300|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as a record year, with consolidated revenue of INR1,75,431 crores and standalone revenue of INR41,039 crores. Birla Opus grew 52% YoY like-to-like in Q4 and crossed 10% revenue market share in March 2026 on its own, while Birla Pivot's Q4 revenue more than doubled YoY and is close to its INR8,500 crore annual guidance. Raw material costs linked to crude derivatives rose sharply, with management citing up to 20-25% of COGS, prompting two further paint price hikes staggered into Q1 FY27. Cellulosic fibre and cement (UltraTech) contributed strong profit growth, and Grasim announced a INR10 final dividend.

Installed capacity 1,332 MLPA (24% of industry); Kharagpur plant commercialised in Q3 FY26. Network at 11,500 towns, 50,000+ dealers, 1,200+ franchise stores; 218 products.

segments.name: Birla Pivot (B2B e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue more than doubled YoY; close to INR8,500 crore annual revenue guidance. Delivers to 5,000+ pin codes across 400+ cities. Management targets EBITDA break-even exit in FY27, possibly sooner.

segments.commentary: Crossed 200 MTPA grey capacity in April 2026, targeting 240+ MTPA by March 2028. UltraTech declared INR240 per share dividend, implying about INR4,000 crore cash inflow to Grasim before tax.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR4,614 crores (+14% YoY), EBITDA INR588 crores. Harihar Lyocell Phase 1 of 55,000 tpa under way within a total 110,000 tpa expansion. China operating rates at 92% in Q4 versus 87% a year ago.

segments.commentary: Chlor-alkali capacity 1,505 KTPA moving to 1,530 KTPA. Specialty chemicals revenue +5% YoY, but higher ECH input prices hit profitability. Specialty chemicals 27% and chlorine derivatives 22% of revenue mix.

segments.commentary: Board approved a INR4,000 crore preferential equity raise; Grasim to invest INR2,880 crores to keep its 52.3% fully diluted stake.

segments.commentary: Porcelain capacity held flat with productivity focus only; polymer long rods sold out after recent expansion; hollow composite expansion being evaluated. Sales and EBITDA no longer disclosed.

Birla Opus priorities in order: become No.2 decorative paints player, reach INR10,000 crore revenue in the third year of full-scale operations (FY26 treated as year one), then profitability. Paint EBITDA losses to narrow quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year.
