qa_highlights.question: How much growth in paints will come from distribution expansion and tinting machines versus throughput?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth from both numerical dealer expansion (11,500 towns to 15,000+) and throughput gains by adding product ranges to existing dealers. Older dealers over 18 months show 25-50% higher counter share and throughput comparable to legacy players.

qa_highlights.question: Is paint profitability improving from scale, and is FY26 the first full year for the INR10,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed FY26 as the first full operating year internally. Fixed costs (sales and service force, brand spend) were front-loaded and should be covered by growth; variable-cost levers include better procurement, plant and logistics optimisation, and adding second and third raw material suppliers. Paint contribution improved significantly in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How close is Birla Opus to the No.2 position in decorative paints?
qa_highlights.answer: Birla Opus plus Birla White putty is roughly at the level of the current No.2 on a decorative-only basis for Q4 FY26. The ambition is for Birla Opus alone to become No.2 in decorative paints, excluding industrial.

qa_highlights.question: Dealer throughput versus industry benchmarks?
qa_highlights.answer: Throughput is in line with market presence across A/B/C/D dealer classes. Top dealers stock 2-2.5x the bottom dealer and generate 4-5x its throughput. The market leader is estimated to have 20-25% more dealers and a richer A-class mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan after the UltraTech dividend, given about INR2,900 crores for ABC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the INR2,900 crore use (ABC stake maintenance) as a one-off for FY26. Cash is being used for Grasim's dividend, maintaining the ABC stake, and supporting the two new businesses. Capex guidance for FY27 will come next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Pivot profitability path and when will segment disclosure start?
qa_highlights.answer: Pivot aims to exit FY27 at EBITDA break-even and may get there sooner. Paints EBITDA losses are on a glide path to narrow each quarter. Management said segment reporting for paints and Pivot would start shortly.

qa_highlights.question: Will paint EBITDA losses (about INR300 crores per quarter) come down materially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management answered 'Yes, it will come down' without quantifying the timing.

qa_highlights.question: Insulator capacity, sales and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Porcelain capacity is flat, with productivity focus; polymer long rods are sold out after expansion; hollow composite expansion is being evaluated. Insulator sales and EBITDA are no longer disclosed.

This VUCA situation makes demand forecasting difficult and we need to closely monitor the situation as impact of price rise will slowly be felt by consumers and contractors in second half of quarter one and entire quarter two FY '27.

500300|2026-06.headline: Grasim Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR48,716 crore, up 21% YoY, with standalone EBITDA more than doubling to INR1,094 crore.
500300|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached a record INR48,716 crore (up 21% YoY), the 24th consecutive quarter of YoY growth. Standalone revenue rose 28% to INR11,795 crore and standalone EBITDA rose 107% to INR1,094 crore. Birla Opus revenue grew 64% YoY to INR1,661 crore after an 8.8% cumulative price increase to offset a raw material cost shock, and Birla Pivot grew 75% to INR2,548 crore. Management also disclosed a new 0.25% of standalone revenue brand royalty payable to Birla Holdings from June 2026, and a planned Renewables equity infusion below INR1,000 crore in FY27.

segments.name: Birla Pivot (B2B e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,548 crore (+75% YoY), annualised run rate above INR10,000 crore. Management reiterated EBITDA break-even by exit of FY27; private labels more than doubled YoY off a low base.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR4,530 crore (+12% YoY) on volumes down 4% YoY; specialty fibre rose to 27% of sales mix from 21%. EBITDA roughly doubled, helped by a low base and specialty mix.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,640 crore (+10% YoY); ECU realisation INR37,955/t (+6% YoY); caustic share of revenue fell to 49% and specialty chemicals rose to 30%. EBITDA INR491 crore (+16%). Volumes softer on plant maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Is Birla Opus's sequential growth of 17% in line with listed peers, and how should profitability and revenue be prioritised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 industry revenue was inflated by channel stocking ahead of double-digit price hikes; as a new entrant, Birla Opus lacks that stocking power. It will keep the INR10,000 crore revenue target and judge revenue over the longer term.

qa_highlights.question: Will Birla Opus turn profitable on a full-year FY28 basis?

qa_highlights.question: Does the 64% YoY growth give confidence on FY27 growth above 50%?

qa_highlights.question: What is the 0.25% royalty to Birla Holdings and its impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Applicable from 1 June 2026 on standalone revenue, capped at INR225 crore. Management estimated about INR100 crore impact for standalone; on INR50,000 crore revenue it would be about INR125 crore. Subsidiaries pay on their own revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How will Grasim fund the Renewables equity contribution and what is the net debt outlook?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for chemicals margins and caustic pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 margins will face pressure from higher-cost inventory bought in Q1, and it is pricing near daily against commodity prices. It sees domestic caustic trading at import parity and new PVC-linked capacity as small.

qa_highlights.question: Are VSF margins sustainable, and what is the impact of Lenzing exits?
qa_highlights.answer: VSF operating rates in India are close to 100% excluding maintenance. Management said competitor exits are small, high-cost capacity and that Indonesian capacity cuts help global supply-demand balance.

qa_highlights.question: When will Birla Pivot break even, and what share of sales comes from UBS stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Pivot is set to exit FY27 at EBITDA break-even, slightly later than earlier guidance. Retail is 15-20% of mix, and UBS is 70-75% of retail revenue.

500304|2026-03.headline: NIIT Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR997 mn, but EBITDA was near breakeven at negative INR0.2 mn as investment continued.

Order intake rose 17% to INR4,209 mn for the year and 18% YoY in Q4 to INR869 mn, giving a positive book-to-bill entering FY27. Ex-iamneo, Q4 revenue was INR875 mn, only a marginal YoY increase, so growth was largely acquisition-driven. Management guided Q1 FY27 to double-digit revenue growth and breakeven to low-single-digit negative EBITDA, but said full-year visibility depends on quarterly macro conditions.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR367 mn, +21% YoY; consumer tech INR210 mn, +28% YoY. Mix shifted to 63:37 enterprise:consumer from 65:35.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR699 mn, +22% YoY; 70% of revenue versus 67% last year. Management cited AI adoption and higher-level skills as drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Does 'stronger revenue' for FY27 mean growth above FY26's 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Only if the environment stays stable; management said it cannot commit to beating FY26 and expects to revisit guidance every quarter. Q1 FY27 is expected to show double-digit growth.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company shift investment from consumer to enterprise given the job market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed with the direction and said the focus is shifting to working professionals, undergraduates and early-career learners, not only enterprise. Consumer working-professional programs launched in Q3 are showing traction.

qa_highlights.question: Why no acquisitions in the last year, and is the inorganic strategy changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still looking and has an active pipeline, reviewed two or three targets closely, but found none that met its criteria. iamneo was described as a well-timed addition.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins improve in Q2 and Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said platform investment is behind it but content and AI curriculum spend continues; some improvement is expected toward the tail end of the year, not necessarily in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI reskilling market getting crowded, and can NIIT stand out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said many players offer AI skills, but NIIT differentiates on AI fluency and outcome-based, personalised training, which is reflected in contracts won where it must demonstrate value.

qa_highlights.question: What is the addressable market and where can NIIT be in a few years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to size the TAM, pointing to third-party reports, and said AI adoption has moved from pilot to production with more appetite expected in FY27.

500304|2026-06.headline: NIIT Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14% YoY to INR957 million and EBITDA loss narrowed to INR14 million from INR63 million.
500304|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR957 million, up 14% YoY, with enterprise up 8% to INR618 million and consumer up 27% to INR339 million. Operating expenses grew 7%, narrowing EBITDA loss to INR14 million from INR63 million a year earlier. PAT rose 85% YoY to INR81 million, helped by INR180 million net other income, mostly treasury income. Management guided to double-digit YoY revenue growth and near-breakeven EBITDA in Q2 FY27, with positive margins in H2.

500307|2026-03.headline: Nirlon Q4 FY26 PAT rose 32% YoY to Rs 71 crore; FY26 PAT Rs 346 crore includes Rs 69.5 crore one-time deferred tax gain; final dividend Rs 15/share.
500307|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was about Rs 174 crore (+9% YoY), EBITDA about Rs 136 crore (+8%) at a stated 77.85% margin, and PAT about Rs 71 crore (+32%). For FY26, total income was about Rs 683 crore (+6%), EBITDA Rs 535 crore (+5%), and PAT Rs 346 crore (+59%), with PAT growth of about 27% excluding a one-time Rs 69.5 crore deferred tax re-measurement gain after the move to Section 115BAA. Average occupancy across NKP and Nirlon House was 99.7% in Q4, with about 8,000 sq ft vacant at 31 March 2026. The Board proposed a final dividend of Rs 15/share (total FY26 dividend Rs 30 versus Rs 26 previously), and management stressed consistency over a large payout. Much of the Q&A was evasive on cash deployment, Nirlon House, REIT or structure plans, buybacks and valuation.

qa_highlights.question: Why adopt the new tax regime now, and does this shelve a REIT restructuring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it moved to the new regime to optimise existing efficiencies and did not rule out future structures or transactions, without confirming any plan.

qa_highlights.question: Is buyback an option to return cash, and why was the FD placed at 5.5% while the HSBC loan costs about 7.75%?
qa_highlights.answer: Buyback is not under consideration at this point, for various reasons. On the FD versus loan spread, management said nothing concrete on the deployment of cash had been decided.

risks_watch: Idle cash of about Rs 165-300 crore (post-dividend) and negative carry versus the HSBC loan at about 7.75%; capital allocation remains undecided.
Lease renewal pricing and tenant retention: the next major renewal cohort (about Rs 3.26 lakh/sq ft per an analyst's reading of the presentation) is due in 2027 and terms were not discussed.
Margin pressure: an analyst noted total expenses up about 11% against income up about 5.9%, with EBITDA margin down from 79.33% to 78.36%; management promised an explanation later.
Tax efficiency for minority shareholders: dividends are taxed at shareholder level, and management did not address buyback or REIT alternatives.
Reconciliation of the lease expiry schedule (about 3,000 sq ft expiring in 12 months) versus 40% of other financial liabilities classified as current; management will respond offline.
Shareholding and promoter classification questions (Brookfield above 10%) were not answered.
500307|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident on operations and the tax-driven PAT growth but evasive on capital allocation, Nirlon House, valuation assumptions, promoter reclassification, buybacks and structure plans, repeatedly deferring to written follow-up through Valorem Advisors.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell from 79.33% to 78.36% in FY26 as total expenses rose about 11% against income up about 5.9%, and management promised an explanation later without guiding to recovery.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capex limited to maintaining NKP as an A-grade asset; management said nothing significant is planned outside the park and no FSI or data centre expansion is being discussed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Average occupancy is 99.7% with only about 8,000 sq ft vacant at 31 March 2026, so volume upside is capped and growth depends on new licences and renewals (about Rs 3.26 lakh/sq ft cohort due 2027) rather than occupancy gains.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 99.7% but the park is fully leased and management said nothing significant is planned outside the park, so a new capex plan is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric revenue, margin or PAT guidance was given, so there is no base to upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cost growth (about 11%) is running ahead of income (about 5.9%), and renewal pricing for the 2027 cohort was not discussed, leaving rental uplift uncertain.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches were discussed; the business is a single leasing park.

rows.label: HSBC loan amortisation from May 2027
rows.why: Outstanding loan about Rs 1,150 crore with 5% per year amortisation from May 2027 for five years then bullet (about 75%), while FD cash of about Rs 278-287 crore earns about 5.5% against a loan at about 7.75%.

rows.label: Capital allocation and REIT or structure options
rows.why: Idle cash of about Rs 165-300 crore after the Rs 15 final dividend is undeployed; management declined a special dividend and buyback, but did not rule out future structures or transactions.

rows.label: Licence fee escalation and renewal pricing
rows.why: Management said growth comes from escalating contracted licence fees, new licences and some higher-priced transactions, though no renewal pricing was disclosed and NKP leasing was cited at north of Rs 185/sq ft/month.
